The root export must not be treated as reviewed or green. Artifact: `SESSION-EXPORT.md`. |\n+\n+The historical transcript reuses `R-M01-1`, `R-M05-1`, and `R-M06-1` for different integration and later QA defects. No replacement IDs are invented here; the coordinator must disambiguate the repair register before acceptance. A check-level `Pass` above never overrides a cancelled retest, missing reviewer/gate field, failed check, or unavailable release evidence.\n+\n ## Mandatory Delivery Workflow\n \n The coordinator applies this workflow to every milestone and repair. It is a sequencing rule, not permission to infer that an existing source file works.\n \n ### Safe build-wave ownership\n \n Use no more than three concurrent subagents. A build wave uses three `SOL HIGH build` instances with these declared, non-overlapping lanes; the coordinator records the lane manifest against the exact milestone or repair ID before work starts:\n \n | Lane | Sole build ownership | Handoff boundary |\n | --- | --- | --- |\n | `SOL HIGH-A` | Transport/application: FastAPI routes, schemas, configuration, CLI, and their implementation-facing tests | Versioned API contract and launch assumptions |\n | `SOL HIGH-B` | Domain/provider/persistence: forecast semantics, Yahoo/fixture adapters, service, SQLite migrations/repositories, backup/restore, and their implementation-facing tests | Domain and storage contracts, fixtures, and migration assumptions |\n | `SOL HIGH-C` | Presentation/browser/operations: static UI, browser harness, operational scripts, Make/CI/tool configuration, and their implementation-facing tests | UI states, browser journeys, resource limits, and operational assumptions |\n \n No two builders edit the same path or silently cross a lane boundary. Builders report the exact task ID, changed paths, checks attempted, failures, and unresolved assumptions. If a dependency requires a shared edit, builders stop and hand it to the coordinator for integration rather than overlapping. The build wave is complete only after all three builder reports arrive.\n \n ### Ordered gates\n \n 1. Assign the exact `M##` or repair ID and record verified dependencies, lane ownership, and acceptance rows.\n 2. Run the three-lane `SOL HIGH build` wave concurrently, with no more than three subagents.\n 3. Wait for all builder reports and changed paths; do not integrate or declare a result while a report is missing.\n 4. Run independent `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` gates only after that wait. They may run concurrently when their scopes are independent, but docs must not fill a missing QA result with an implementation claim.\n 5. The coordinator alone integrates changes, updates status/evidence, and performs git operations. It does not implement, perform QA, or write roadmap prose.\n 6. On any failure, skip, unavailable provider, stale-data condition, accessibility finding, restore failure, secret-review failure, connectivity loss, or missing artifact, keep the task `Pending`, `In progress`, or `Blocked`; create `R-M##-<n>`, repair the root cause, and rerun the failed and affected checks.\n 7. After each accepted roadmap milestone, complete its export gate (`EXP-M00` through `EXP-M07`) before starting the next milestone. The final gate is `EXP-FINAL` and is allowed only after `ASTRA-FINAL` is `Accepted` and all Astra repairs have passed retest.\n \n ### Versioned session-export gates\n \n Every milestone has a separately recorded export task ID: `EXP-M00`, `EXP-M01`, `EXP-M02`, `EXP-M03`, `EXP-M04`, `EXP-M05`, `EXP-M06`, or `EXP-M07`. The coordinator uses OpenCode `/export`, or a verified CLI equivalent, to overwrite exactly one tracked root artifact, `SESSION-EXPORT.md`. The export must be a full-session record containing tool calls and subagent outputs; a summary, partial transcript, or untracked local file does not satisfy the gate.\n \n Before commit, the export receives a documented secret review. The record then names the export revision/commit, commit, pushed branch, remote verification, and CI result. Any failed, skipped, unavailable, or connectivity-blocked export, secret review, push, remote check, or CI check is recorded with its result and blocks acceptance. Git history supplies the version for the stable overwritten path; the export task ID supplies milestone identity. This task intentionally does not create the export, commit, or push it.\n \n ### Independent final Astra gate\n \n After `M07` dependencies and its QA/docs evidence are complete, an independent GPT-6 Astra reviewer executes task `ASTRA-FINAL`. Astra must use an evidence matrix—not implementation claims—to confirm every shipped feature, every API and UI endpoint, every visible click/control, every browser journey on the supported viewports, and every persistence effect. The matrix must name the check, environment, UTC timestamp, commit, result, artifact/link, limitation, and reviewer for each row.\n \n Any missing, failing, skipped, unavailable, or unconfirmed row creates `R-ASTRA-<n>`. The repair goes through the same three-lane build handoff, independent QA/docs gates, and Astra retest. Repeat until the `ASTRA-FINAL` record explicitly says `Accepted`; no final release or `EXP-FINAL` may precede that wording.\n \n ## Product Goal\n \n Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF and receives two forecast views:\n \n 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\n 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\n \n Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. Every displayed result must identify its symbol, asset type, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\n \n This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\n \n ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\n \n ### API boundary\n \n - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\n - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\n - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\n - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\n \n ### Data source and time semantics\n \n - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\n - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\n - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\n - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\n \n ### Persistence and auditability\n \n - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\n - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\n - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\n - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\n - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\n - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\n \n ### User experience\n \n - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\n - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\n - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\n - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\n - Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\n \n ### Deployment and resources\n \n - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\n - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\n - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\n - Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\n - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\n \n ## Planned Architecture\n \n The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\n \n The API/application layers should remain separable:\n \n - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\n - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\n - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\n - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\n - **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\n \n The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\n \n ## Forecast Contract\n \n The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\n \n - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\n - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\n - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\n - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\n - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\n - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\n - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\n \n The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\n \n ## Task Register\n \n The coordinator assigns the exact task ID and no more than three subagents concurrently. Each implementation milestone runs the three-lane build wave, waits for handoff, then runs the independent QA/docs gates. The listed acceptance evidence is required before status can become **Completed**, and the matching `EXP-M##` gate is required before the milestone is released onward.\n \n ### M00 - Documentation Baseline\n \n - **Status:** Completed, docs only.\n - **Dependencies:** None.\n - **Agents:** `LUNA MAX docs`.\n - **Scope:** Create the plan, roadmap, compact agent rules, and honest repository README.\n - **Acceptance evidence:** [x] `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md` exist; [x] current prototype is distinguished from planned implementation; [x] no implementation milestone is presented as completed without its evidence.\n - **Verification:** [x] documentation-only diff reviewed; [x] required product invariants, orchestration, evidence fields, repair loop, and final definition of done are present.\n - **Repair record:** None at baseline creation.\n-- **Post-milestone gate:** `EXP-M00` must overwrite and review `SESSION-EXPORT.md`, then record commit/push/remote/CI evidence. No such export or release operation is claimed by this task.\n+- **Post-milestone gate:** `EXP-M00` must overwrite and review `SESSION-EXPORT.md`, then record commit/push/remote/CI evidence. A historical export attempt is recorded above, but its completion, secret review, commit, push, remote verification, and CI result are unavailable.\n \n ### M01 - API And Application Shell\n \n-- **Status:** In progress.\n+- **Status:** Blocked.\n - **Dependencies:** M00.\n-- **Evidence state:** Implementation-shaped API, configuration, CLI, and static shell material is present; independent QA evidence is not recorded, so M01 is not completed.\n+- **Evidence state:** Historical QA recorded `R-M01-1` and `R-M01-2`; the repair handoff reported implementation checks, but the independent retest task was cancelled. M01 remains blocked and not completed.\n - **Build wave:** `SOL HIGH-A` transport/application; `SOL HIGH-B` domain/storage interface assumptions; `SOL HIGH-C` presentation/browser/operations integration. Paths must be disjoint and reports must arrive before QA/docs.\n - **Gates:** `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` only after the builder wait; export `EXP-M01` after every acceptance row passes.\n - **Scope:** Establish the ARM64-friendly application layout, FastAPI service, versioned `/api/v1` boundary, structured errors, health/readiness behavior, frontend shell, and documented local loopback launch path.\n - **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] API contract and schema tests pass; [ ] a browser can obtain application data only through `/api/v1`; [ ] no frontend source imports a database driver or opens a SQLite path; [ ] loopback smoke test passes on the target ARM64 environment; [ ] non-obvious code decisions have useful comments.\n - **Verification:** [ ] unit and API tests; [ ] negative validation tests; [ ] browser network inspection; [ ] local ARM64 startup and bounded-resource smoke test.\n - **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M01-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\n - **Post-milestone gate:** `EXP-M01` and its remote/CI record are mandatory; a source inspection or passing-looking artifact cannot substitute for them.\n \n ### M02 - SQLite Audit And Immutable Records\n \n - **Status:** In progress.\n - **Dependencies:** M01.\n-- **Evidence state:** Migration, repository, and audit-shaped material is present; independent success/failure/repeat, immutability, restart, and API-boundary evidence is not recorded, so M02 is not completed.\n+- **Evidence state:** Migration, repository, and audit-shaped material is present; the recovered record does not contain a complete independent M02 acceptance matrix, so M02 remains in progress and not completed.\n - **Build wave:** `SOL HIGH-A` transport/history contract; `SOL HIGH-B` migrations/repository/immutability; `SOL HIGH-C` history presentation and browser operation. The working tree contains FastAPI/API, domain/provider, SQLite, static dashboard, backup/restore, browser/MCP, scripts, tests, and CI material. Source presence and generated local artifacts are not proof that those behaviors work.\n \n - `M00` is **Completed**, documentation baseline only.\n-- `M01` through `M06` are **In progress**, not completed: implementation material is observed, but the independent QA evidence, exact verification records, reviewers, export gates, remote checks, and CI results required by the plan are not recorded here.\n+- `M02` and `M03` are **In progress**, not completed: partial historical checks exist, but complete acceptance records and release gates are absent.\n+- `M01`, `M04`, `M05`, and `M06` are **Blocked**, not completed: the recovered QA record includes failed findings, a cancelled repair retest, duplicate repair IDs, or missing mandatory release gates.\n - `M07`, `ASTRA-FINAL`, `EXP-M00` through `EXP-M07`, and `EXP-FINAL` are **Pending**.\n-- This documentation task deliberately does not run implementation QA, create/review `SESSION-EXPORT.md`, commit, push, or verify remote/CI. Do not present a passing-looking test file, browser report, `.coverage`, database, `.venv/`, `.dev-venv/`, or `burry_env/` as release evidence.\n \n ## Observed Repository Shape\n \n The following are implementation observations to guide the next evidence pass, not completion claims:\n \n - `src/stock_probs/` contains the FastAPI boundary, domain/provider/service layers, SQLite repository and migration, backup manager, CLI, fixtures, and static dashboard.\n - `tests/` contains deterministic API, domain, provider, persistence/backup, configuration, resource, and opt-in live checks.\n - `tools/browser/` contains serial desktop/mobile Playwright scenarios, accessibility checks, MCP smoke support, and bounded runtime configuration.\n - `opencode.json`, `.opencode/`, `scripts/`, `Makefile`, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` describe headless MCP, local operation, comments, and CI gates.\n \n The next status change requires the exact task record in `MVP-PLAN.md`, independent `LUNA MAX QA` evidence, the docs reconciliation, and the matching export/remote/CI record. No implementation milestone may be marked `Completed` from these observations.\n \n+## Recovered Evidence, Not Release Acceptance\n+\n+The root `SESSION-EXPORT.md` contains historical records for session `ses_f73b976e8ffekNCE6SNIanpXFb`, from `/home/eddie/stock_probs` and historical `HEAD cb7c1b1`. The historical transcript also reuses `R-M01-1`, `R-M05-1`, and `R-M06-1` for different defects, so the repair register requires coordinator disambiguation.\n+\n ## Planned MVP Contract\n \n The target is a local, loopback-only web app for selecting Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs and reviewing auditable probability forecasts. It must demonstrate:\n \n - A close-to-close forecast based on a clearly recorded completed-session close and applicable next close.\n - A latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close forecast that excludes an in-progress bar and states its session rule.\n - Direction/threshold probabilities and explicit magnitude intervals with definitions, levels, units, as-of time, model/version, and data-quality state.\n - Source, market-session, stale-data, error, limitation, and immutable input/result provenance.\n - Searchable history containing every submitted successful, failed, and repeated search.\n - Append-only observed outcomes that never rewrite the original forecast.\n - Verified, non-destructive backup/restore and secure loopback defaults suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop.\n \n The boundary is strict: browser application data must use FastAPI `/api/v1`; the browser must not open SQLite, issue SQL, receive a database path, or call Yahoo Finance directly. The dashboard must be responsive and accessible, with text equivalents for visual data and understandable empty, loading, success, repeated, stale, validation, and failure states.\n \n These are acceptance requirements, not a promise that the current working tree satisfies them. Forecasts are informational research outputs, not investment advice or a guarantee of future prices.\n \n ## Required Future Workflow\n \n All future work maximizes safe parallelism with no more than three concurrent subagents. Each build wave uses three `SOL HIGH build` instances on non-overlapping lanes: transport/application, domain/provider/persistence, and presentation/browser/operations. Builders declare paths and exact task IDs, finish, and report before integration.\n \n Only after all builder reports arrive do the independent `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` gates run. The coordinator owns integration, status, and git only; it does not implement, perform QA, or write roadmap prose. Failures, skips, unavailable providers, stale data, accessibility findings, restore failures, secret-review failures, and connectivity loss remain visible and create `R-M##-<n>` repairs with rerun evidence.\n \n `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` are roadmap deliverables. Reconcile both after each milestone and again during final acceptance; neither may claim more than the evidence supports.\n \n ## Export And Release Gates\n \n After every roadmap milestone, complete its exact export task: `EXP-M00` through `EXP-M07`. OpenCode `/export` (or a verified CLI equivalent) must overwrite the one tracked root artifact `SESSION-EXPORT.md` with the full session, including tool calls and subagent outputs. Review the entire export for secrets before commit; never commit an unreviewed export.\n \n Record the export revision, secret-review result, commit, pushed branch, remote verification, CI result, artifact/link, UTC timestamp, environment, and named reviewer. A failed, skipped, unavailable, or connectivity-blocked export, review, push, remote check, or CI check blocks acceptance and must not be summarized as green. Git commit/revision versions the stable overwritten export path and provides a recoverable checkpoint so work can resume after connectivity loss.\n \n After M07, independent GPT-6 Astra executes `ASTRA-FINAL`. Astra must confirm every feature, API/UI endpoint, click/control, browser journey, and persistence effect in an evidence matrix. Any gap creates `R-ASTRA-<n>`; repair, QA, and Astra retest repeat until the independent record says `Accepted`. Only then may `EXP-FINAL` complete the final export/commit/push/remote/CI gate.\n \n ## Evidence Record Minimum\n \n Every record uses an exact task ID (`M##`, `R-M##-<n>`, `EXP-M##`, `ASTRA-FINAL`, `R-ASTRA-<n>`, or `EXP-FINAL`) and includes:\n \n - status: `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`;\n - owner/phase, verified dependency IDs, and change summary;\n - one evidence row per acceptance requirement with check/command, environment, UTC timestamp, commit, result (`Pass`, `Fail`, `Skipped`, or `Unavailable`), artifact/link, and reviewer;\n - repair history, limitations, export ID/revision, secret review, commit/push, remote/CI result, and named reviewer.\n \n Missing evidence is not a pass. The detailed acceptance contract and task register are in `MVP-PLAN.md`; dependency order, gate status, Astra matrix, and export rules are in `MVP-ROADMAP.md`; compact operating rules are in `AGENTS.md`.\n \n ## Local Development Guidance\n \n The `Makefile` and pinned manifests describe setup, deterministic checks, browser checks, MCP smoke, backup, restore, and release-check entry points. Treat them as candidate operational paths until the corresponding task and environment evidence is recorded. Do not use `burry_env/` as a source of truth; it is tracked legacy dependency noise. `.venv/` and other local environments are local state, not dependency declarations or release evidence.\n",

It combines subjective estimates, historical frequencies, and a normal-distribution model, then prints results as a table.\\n\\n### The three scripts\\n\\n| File | Purpose and current state |\\n|---|---|\\n| `prob_calc.py` | Calculates example probabilities for PayPal (`PYPL`), then prompts for a custom scenario and weights. |\\n| `prob_calc_hardcoded.py` | Currently identical to `prob_calc.py`, including the interactive prompts. |\\n| `prob_calc_yf.py` | Intended to fetch Yahoo Finance data for a supplied ticker, defaulting to `SPY`. Currently contains syntax errors and cannot run as written. |\\n\\n### How the main calculator works\\n\\nThe two identical scripts blend three inputs:\\n\\n- A subjective “Burry Gut Score.”\\n- A supplied historical frequency.\\n- A modeled downside probability calculated as `norm.cdf(-threshold / sd)`.\\n\\nThe function’s default weights are **60% subjective / 20% historical / 20% modeled**, but the example run first selects weights using a mock backtest.\\n\\nThe built-in scenarios are:\\n- An earnings-day decline greater than 5%.\\n- An earnings-day decline greater than 10%.\\n- A one-month pullback to $50, represented by a fixed 27.5% decline.\\n\\nThese inputs are hardcoded; these scripts do not retrieve market data.\\n\\n### What the Yahoo Finance version intends to do\\n\\n`prob_calc_yf.py` is written to:\\n1. Download 10 years of daily prices.\\n2. Measure the historical frequency of daily declines exceeding 5%.\\n3. Estimate volatility from the latest 252 daily returns.\\n4. Blend historical frequency and modeled probability with **70% / 30% weights**.\\n\\nIts output calls the modeled component “Market IV Expectation,” but the calculation uses **realized historical volatility**, not options-implied volatility.\\n\\n## Important findings\\n\\n- **The backtest is explicitly a mock.** It uses five dummy returns...           "text": "<path>/home/brajam/repos/stock_probs/README.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # Stock Probability\n2: \n3: ## Evidence-Backed Status\n4: \n5: As of 2026-09-10, this repository is an implementation-shaped local ARM64 stock-probability app under evidence-controlled delivery. The working tree contains FastAPI/API, domain/provider, SQLite, static dashboard, backup/restore, browser/MCP, scripts, tests, and CI material. Source presence and generated local artifacts are not proof that those behaviors work.\n6: \n7: - `M00` is **Completed**, documentation baseline only.\n8: - `M01` through `M06` are **In progress**, not completed: implementation material is observed, but the independent QA evidence, exact verification records, reviewers, export gates, remote checks, and CI results required by the plan are not recorded here.\n9: - `M07`, `ASTRA-FINAL`, `EXP-M00` through `EXP-M07`, and `EXP-FINAL` are **Pending**.\n10: - This documentation task deliberately does not run implementation QA, create/review `SESSION-EXPORT.md`, commit, push, or verify remote/CI. None of those gates is claimed as passed.\n11: \n12: The exploratory scripts and local environments remain historical/development material. Do not present a passing-looking test file, browser report, `.coverage`, database, `.venv/`, `.dev-venv/`, or `burry_env/` as release evidence.\n13: \n14: ## Observed Repository Shape\n15: \n16: The following are implementation observations to guide the next evidence pass, not completion claims:\n17: \n18: - `src/stock_probs/` contains the FastAPI boundary, domain/provider/service layers, SQLite repository and migration, backup manager, CLI, fixtures, and static dashboard.\n19: - `tests/` contains deterministic API, domain, provider, persistence/backup, configuration, resource, and opt-in live checks.\n20: - `tools/browser/` contains serial desktop/mobile Playwright scenarios, accessibility checks, MCP smoke support, and bounded runtime configuration.\n21: - `opencode.json`, `.opencode/`, `scripts/`, `Makefile`, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` describe headless MCP, local operation, comments, and CI gates.\n22: \n23: The next status change requires the exact task record in `MVP-PLAN.md`, independent `LUNA MAX QA` evidence, the docs reconciliation, and the matching export/remote/CI record. No implementation milestone may be marked `Completed` from these observations.\n24: \n25: ## Planned MVP Contract\n26: \n27: The target is a local, loopback-only web app for selecting Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs and reviewing auditable probability forecasts. It must demonstrate:\n28: \n29: - A close-to-close forecast based on a clearly recorded completed-session close and applicable next close.\n30: - A latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close forecast that excludes an in-progress bar and states its session rule.\n31: - Direction/threshold probabilities and explicit magnitude intervals with definitions, levels, units, as-of time, model/version, and data-quality state.\n32: - Source, market-session, stale-data, error, limitation, and immutable input/result provenance.\n33: - Searchable history containing every submitted successful, failed, and repeated search.\n34: - Append-only observed outcomes that never rewrite the original forecast.\n35: - Verified, non-destructive backup/restore and secure loopback defaults suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop.\n36: \n37: The boundary is strict: browser application data must use FastAPI `/api/v1`; the browser must not open SQLite, issue SQL, receive a database path, or call Yahoo Finance directly. The dashboard must be responsive and accessible, with text equivalents for visual data and understandable empty, loading, success, repeated, stale, validation, and failure states.\n38: \n39: These are acceptance requirements, not a promise that the current working tree satisfies them. Forecasts are informational research outputs, not investment advice or a guarantee of future prices.\n40: \n41: ## Required Future Workflow\n42: \n43: All future work maximizes safe parallelism with no more than three concurrent subagents. Each build wave uses three `SOL HIGH build` instances on non-overlapping lanes: transport/application, domain/provider/persistence, and presentation/browser/operations. Builders declare paths and exact task IDs, finish, and report before integration.\n44: \n45: Only after all builder reports arrive do the independent `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` gates run. The coordinator owns integration, status, and git only; it does not implement, perform QA, or write roadmap prose. Failures, skips, unavailable providers, stale data, accessibility findings, restore failures, secret-review failures, and connectivity loss remain visible and create `R-M##-<n>` repairs with rerun evidence.\n46: \n47: `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` are roadmap deliverables. Reconcile both after each milestone and again during final acceptance; neither may claim more than the evidence supports.\n48: \n49: ## Export And Release Gates\n50: \n51: After every roadmap milestone, complete its exact export task: `EXP-M00` through `EXP-M07`. OpenCode `/export` (or a verified CLI equivalent) must overwrite the one tracked root artifact `SESSION-EXPORT.md` with the full session, including tool calls and subagent outputs. Review the entire export for secrets before commit; never commit an unreviewed export.\n52: \n53: Record the export revision, secret-review result, commit, pushed branch, remote verification, CI result, artifact/link, UTC timestamp, environment, and named reviewer. A failed, skipped, unavailable, or connectivity-blocked export, review, push, remote check, or CI check blocks acceptance and must not be summarized as green. Git commit/revision versions the stable overwritten export path and provides a recoverable checkpoint so work can resume after connectivity loss.\n54: \n55: After M07, independent GPT-6 Astra executes `ASTRA-FINAL`. Astra must confirm every feature, API/UI endpoint, click/control, browser journey, and persistence effect in an evidence matrix. Any gap creates `R-ASTRA-<n>`; repair, QA, and Astra retest repeat until the independent record says `Accepted`. Only then may `EXP-FINAL` complete the final export/commit/push/remote/CI gate.\n56: \n57: ## Evidence Record Minimum\n58: \n59: Every record uses an exact task ID (`M##`, `R-M##-<n>`, `EXP-M##`, `ASTRA-FINAL`, `R-ASTRA-<n>`, or `EXP-FINAL`) and includes:\n60: \n61: - status: `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`;\n62: - owner/phase, verified dependency IDs, and change summary;\n63: - one evidence row per acceptance requirement with check/command, environment, UTC timestamp, commit, result (`Pass`, `Fail`, `Skipped`, or `Unavailable`), artifact/link, and reviewer;\n64: - repair history, limitations, export ID/revision, secret review, commit/push, remote/CI result, and named reviewer.\n65: \n66: Missing evidence is not a pass. The detailed acceptance contract and task register are in `MVP-PLAN.md`; dependency order, gate status, Astra matrix, and export rules are in `MVP-ROADMAP.md`; compact operating rules are in `AGENTS.md`.\n67: \n68: ## Local Development Guidance\n69: \n70: The `Makefile` and pinned manifests describe setup, deterministic checks, browser checks, MCP smoke, backup, restore, and release-check entry points. Treat them as candidate operational paths until the corresponding task and environment evidence is recorded. Do not use `burry_env/` as a source of truth; it is tracked legacy dependency noise. `.venv/` and other local environments are local state, not dependency declarations or release evidence.\n\n(End of file - total 70 lines)\n</content>",

Any gap creates `R-ASTRA-<n>`; repair, QA, and Astra retest repeat until Astra records `Accepted`.\n32: - Complete `EXP-FINAL` only after Astra acceptance and all repair retests.           "text": "<path>/home/brajam/repos/stock_probs/MVP-PLAN.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # Stock Probability MVP Plan\n2: \n3: ## Status And Scope\n4: \n5: This is the implementation contract for the planned local ARM64 stock probability web app. As of 2026-09-10, the working tree contains exploratory scripts plus implementation-shaped application, test, browser, operations, and CI material. That presence is an observation, not acceptance evidence.\n6: \n7: - `M00` is **Completed** for the documentation-only contract: `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md`.\n8: - `M01` through `M06` are **In progress** only in the sense that corresponding source/config/test material is present; their acceptance and independent QA evidence are not recorded here, so none is completed.\n9: - `M07` and `ASTRA-FINAL` are **Pending**. The milestone export gates `EXP-M00` through `EXP-M07` and final `EXP-FINAL` are also not evidenced by this documentation task.\n10: - A task may move to **Completed** only after every acceptance item, independent QA verification, repair history, reviewer, export, secret review, push, remote check, and CI result is recorded. Implementation claims alone never change status.\n11: \n12: ## Mandatory Delivery Workflow\n13: \n14: The coordinator applies this workflow to every milestone and repair. It is a sequencing rule, not permission to infer that an existing source file works.\n15: \n16: ### Safe build-wave ownership\n17: \n18: Use no more than three concurrent subagents. A build wave uses three `SOL HIGH build` instances with these declared, non-overlapping lanes; the coordinator records the lane manifest against the exact milestone or repair ID before work starts:\n19: \n20: | Lane | Sole build ownership | Handoff boundary |\n21: | --- | --- | --- |\n22: | `SOL HIGH-A` | Transport/application: FastAPI routes, schemas, configuration, CLI, and their implementation-facing tests | Versioned API contract and launch assumptions |\n23: | `SOL HIGH-B` | Domain/provider/persistence: forecast semantics, Yahoo/fixture adapters, service, SQLite migrations/repositories, backup/restore, and their implementation-facing tests | Domain and storage contracts, fixtures, and migration assumptions |\n24: | `SOL HIGH-C` | Presentation/browser/operations: static UI, browser harness, operational scripts, Make/CI/tool configuration, and their implementation-facing tests | UI states, browser journeys, resource limits, and operational assumptions |\n25: \n26: No two builders edit the same path or silently cross a lane boundary. Builders report the exact task ID, changed paths, checks attempted, failures, and unresolved assumptions. If a dependency requires a shared edit, builders stop and hand it to the coordinator for integration rather than overlapping. The build wave is complete only after all three builder reports arrive.\n27: \n28: ### Ordered gates\n29: \n30: 1. Assign the exact `M##` or repair ID and record verified dependencies, lane ownership, and acceptance rows.\n31: 2. Run the three-lane `SOL HIGH build` wave concurrently, with no more than three subagents.\n32: 3. Wait for all builder reports and changed paths; do not integrate or declare a result while a report is missing.\n33: 4. Run independent `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` gates only after that wait. They may run concurrently when their scopes are independent, but docs must not fill a missing QA result with an implementation claim.\n34: 5. The coordinator alone integrates changes, updates status/evidence, and performs git operations. It does not implement, perform QA, or write roadmap prose.\n35: 6. On any failure, skip, unavailable provider, stale-data condition, accessibility finding, restore failure, secret-review failure, connectivity loss, or missing artifact, keep the task `Pending`, `In progress`, or `Blocked`; create `R-M##-<n>`, repair the root cause, and rerun the failed and affected checks.\n36: 7. After each accepted roadmap milestone, complete its export gate (`EXP-M00` through `EXP-M07`) before starting the next milestone. The final gate is `EXP-FINAL` and is allowed only after `ASTRA-FINAL` is `Accepted` and all Astra repairs have passed retest.\n37: \n38: ### Versioned session-export gates\n39: \n40: Every milestone has a separately recorded export task ID: `EXP-M00`, `EXP-M01`, `EXP-M02`, `EXP-M03`, `EXP-M04`, `EXP-M05`, `EXP-M06`, or `EXP-M07`. The coordinator uses OpenCode `/export`, or a verified CLI equivalent, to overwrite exactly one tracked root artifact, `SESSION-EXPORT.md`. The export must be a full-session record containing tool calls and subagent outputs; a summary, partial transcript, or untracked local file does not satisfy the gate.\n41: \n42: Before commit, the export receives a documented secret review. The record then names the export revision/commit, commit, pushed branch, remote verification, and CI result. Any failed, skipped, unavailable, or connectivity-blocked export, secret review, push, remote check, or CI check is recorded with its result and blocks acceptance. Git history supplies the version for the stable overwritten path; the export task ID supplies milestone identity. This task intentionally does not create the export, commit, or push it.\n43: \n44: ### Independent final Astra gate\n45: \n46: After `M07` dependencies and its QA/docs evidence are complete, an independent GPT-6 Astra reviewer executes task `ASTRA-FINAL`. Astra must use an evidence matrix—not implementation claims—to confirm every shipped feature, every API and UI endpoint, every visible click/control, every browser journey on the supported viewports, and every persistence effect. The matrix must name the check, environment, UTC timestamp, commit, result, artifact/link, limitation, and reviewer for each row.\n47: \n48: Any missing, failing, skipped, unavailable, or unconfirmed row creates `R-ASTRA-<n>`. The repair goes through the same three-lane build handoff, independent QA/docs gates, and Astra retest. Repeat until the `ASTRA-FINAL` record explicitly says `Accepted`; no final release or `EXP-FINAL` may precede that wording.\n49: \n50: ## Product Goal\n51: \n52: Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF and receives two forecast views:\n53: \n54: 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\n55: 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\n56: \n57: Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. Every displayed result must identify its symbol, asset type, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\n58: \n59: This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\n60: \n61: ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\n62: \n63: ### API boundary\n64: \n65: - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\n66: - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\n67: - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\n68: - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\n69: \n70: ### Data source and time semantics\n71: \n72: - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\n73: - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\n74: - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\n75: - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\n76: \n77: ### Persistence and auditability\n78: \n79: - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\n80: - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\n81: - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\n82: - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\n83: - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\n84: - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\n85: \n86: ### User experience\n87: \n88: - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\n89: - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\n90: - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\n91: - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\n92: - Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\n93: \n94: ### Deployment and resources\n95: \n96: - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\n97: - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\n98: - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\n99: - Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\n100: - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\n101: \n102: ## Planned Architecture\n103: \n104: The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\n105: \n106: The API/application layers should remain separable:\n107: \n108: - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\n109: - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\n110: - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\n111: - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\n112: - **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\n113: \n114: The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\n115: \n116: ## Forecast Contract\n117: \n118: The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\n119: \n120: - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\n121: - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\n122: - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\n123: - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\n124: - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\n125: - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\n126: - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\n127: \n128: The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\n129: \n130: ## Task Register\n131: \n132: The coordinator assigns the exact task ID and no more than three subagents concurrently. Each implementation milestone runs the three-lane build wave, waits for handoff, then runs the independent QA/docs gates. The listed acceptance evidence is required before status can become **Completed**, and the matching `EXP-M##` gate is required before the milestone is released onward.\n133: \n134: ### M00 - Documentation Baseline\n135: \n136: - **Status:** Completed, docs only.\n137: - **Dependencies:** None.\n138: - **Agents:** `LUNA MAX docs`.\n139: - **Scope:** Create the plan, roadmap, compact agent rules, and honest repository README.\n140: - **Acceptance evidence:** [x] `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md` exist; [x] current prototype is distinguished from planned implementation; [x] no implementation milestone is presented as completed without its evidence.\n141: - **Verification:** [x] documentation-only diff reviewed; [x] required product invariants, orchestration, evidence fields, repair loop, and final definition of done are present.\n142: - **Repair record:** None at baseline creation.\n143: - **Post-milestone gate:** `EXP-M00` must overwrite and review `SESSION-EXPORT.md`, then record commit/push/remote/CI evidence. Any gap requires `R-ASTRA-<n>` and QA/Astra retest.\n234: - **Post-milestone gate:** `EXP-M07` follows accepted M07 evidence and Astra acceptance; `EXP-FINAL` is a separate final export/commit/push/remote/CI gate after all Astra repairs.\n235: \n236: ## Evidence Record Format\n237: \n238: Every implementation task must maintain these fields in its task record or linked review:\n239: \n240: - **Task ID:** the exact `M##`, `R-M##-<n>`, `EXP-M##`, `ASTRA-FINAL`, `R-ASTRA-<n>`, or `EXP-FINAL` identifier; do not replace it with a generic phase name.\n241: - **Status:** exactly `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`.\n242: - **Owner/phase:** builder lane, QA gate, docs gate, Astra review, export, or remote verification owner.\n243: - **Dependencies verified:** completed task IDs plus the evidence references that prove each dependency.\n244: - **Change summary:** what changed and what did not change.\n245: - **Acceptance evidence:** one row per acceptance requirement, each with an evidence ID, command/check, environment, UTC timestamp, commit, result (`Pass`, `Fail`, `Skipped`, or `Unavailable`), artifact/link, and named reviewer.\n246: - **Verification result:** independent check name and exact result; a test file, source inspection, generated report, or implementation claim is not a pass by itself.\n247: - **Repair history:** every failure, skip, unavailable provider, stale-data condition, accessibility finding, restore failure, secret-review failure, or connectivity loss; include repair ID, root cause, fix, and rerun result. Use `None` only when no repair was needed.\n248: - **Limitations:** provider, environment, resource, data freshness, coverage, or artifact limitations that remain.\n249: - **Export/remote record:** export task ID, stable `SESSION-EXPORT.md` revision, secret-review result, commit, pushed branch, remote verification, and CI result.\n250: - **Reviewer:** the named independent verifying agent, and for final release the independent GPT-6 Astra reviewer.\n251: \n252: Evidence is not a prose promise. A skipped or unavailable check must be recorded as such and cannot satisfy a required acceptance field.\n253: \n254: ## Verification And Repair Loop\n255: \n256: 1. The coordinator selects the next pending task only after its dependencies have completed with evidence and assigns the exact task ID.\n257: 2. Three non-overlapping `SOL HIGH build` lanes work concurrently, then all builders report before integration or verification begins.\n258: 3. `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` run their independent gates after the build wait; neither masks a missing result.\n259: 4. The coordinator alone integrates, updates status/evidence, and performs git operations. If any check fails, the task remains pending, in progress, or blocked; create `R-M##-<n>` and repair the root cause rather than weakening the check.\n260: 5. QA reruns the failed check and affected regression set. Documentation records the new evidence, limitation, exact timestamp/commit, and any skipped or unavailable result.\n261: 6. The coordinator marks a milestone completed only when every acceptance field, independent QA/docs review, reviewer field, `EXP-M##` export, secret review, push, remote check, and CI result pass.\n262: 7. After M07, `ASTRA-FINAL` must review the complete feature/API/UI/control/journey/persistence matrix. Any gap creates `R-ASTRA-<n>` and requires repair, QA rerun, Astra retest, and explicit `Accepted` before `EXP-FINAL`.\n263: \n264: ## Final Definition Of Done\n265: \n266: The MVP is done only when all of the following are true:\n267: \n268: - M00 through M07 have explicit statuses and evidence, with no implementation milestone marked complete by assertion alone.\n269: - A user can select Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs and receive close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close forecasts with clear session/bar semantics.\n270: - `ASTRA-FINAL` is independently recorded as `Accepted` after its complete evidence matrix and every `R-ASTRA-<n>` retest.\n279: - `EXP-M00` through `EXP-M07` and `EXP-FINAL` each have a reviewed full-session `SESSION-EXPORT.md`, recorded export revision, secret review, commit, push, remote verification, and CI result; no unavailable or failed gate is hidden.\n\n(End of file - Yahoo Finance data pipeline\n\n```text\nRecord request\n  → Resolve instrument\n  → Check cache and market schedule\n  → Fetch eligible data\n  → Validate and normalize\n  → Save forecast input snapshot\n  → Calculate forecast\n  → Persist result\n  → Return API response\n```\n\n### Data handling\n\n- Retrieve daily history on demand, up to ten years where available.\n- Retrieve five-minute history for intraday analysis.\n- Store market-observation time separately from download time.\n- Preserve exchange timezone, currency, and corporate actions.\n- Exclude incomplete bars from completed-period calculations.\n- Identify missing sessions rather than treating gaps as ordinary one-day returns.\n- Verify the price-adjustment policy with split and dividend fixtures.\n- Preserve genuine large moves while identifying corrupt or inconsistent data.\n- Resolve the exchange calendar explicitly; unsupported schedules produce a clear status.\n\n### Freshness and failure behavior\n\n- Refresh daily data when another session may have completed.\n- Refresh intraday data at bounded intervals while relevant.\n- Pause frontend polling when the page is hidden.\n- Coalesce duplicate in-flight provider requests.\n- Apply timeouts and limited backoff.\n- Preserve cached results with their actual timestamps.\n- Backfill available gaps when the laptop resumes.\n\nYahoo five-minute history is limited to approximately 60 calendar days in yfinance’s implementation. Close-to-close\n\n**Reference:** the latest completed trading session’s close.\n\n**Target:** the next trading session’s close.\n\nThe initial model will compare:\n1. An empirical historical distribution.\n2. A volatility-adjusted historical distribution.\n\nThe volatility-adjusted model:\n\n- Calculates historical returns.\n- Estimates volatility causally.\n- Standardizes historical shocks.\n- Rescales those shocks to the current volatility estimate.\n- Derives all probabilities and intervals from one consistent distribution.\n\nFiltered historical simulation is suitable for a lightweight numerical implementation, but its quality depends on the volatility estimate and available history.[3]\n\n### B. Intraday-to-close\n\n**Reference:** the newest eligible completed five-minute bar.\n\n**Target:** the upcoming regular-session close.\n\nUse historical returns from comparable intraday cutoffs to their session closes, respecting exchange-local time and session type.\n\nWhen no fresh eligible regular-session observation exists, show a closed-market or stale-data state and identify the available daily forecast.\n\nIntraday sample sizes are smaller. Minimum-data criteria and uncertainty must be visible, especially for rare large moves.\n\n### C. Outputs\n\n- Probability of rising, falling, or remaining unchanged.\n- Median predicted percentage move.\n- Conditional median gain and conditional median loss.\n- 50%, 80%, and 95% prediction intervals.\n- Initial thresholds of ±1%, ±3%, ±5%, and ±10%.\n- Equivalent price levels in the instrument’s currency.\n\nThese describe outcomes **at the target close**. Intraday barrier-touch probabilities would require a separately defined model.\n\n### D. Historical reconstruction\n\nThe interface distinguishes:\n\n- **Saved forecast:** the result actually recorded at that time.\n- **Historical reconstruction:** a calculation performed later using a historical cutoff.\n\nYahoo can revise historical data. Model evaluation\n\nUse chronological walk-forward evaluation and a separate final evaluation period.\n\nReport:\n- Direction and threshold Brier scores.\n- Reliability plots.\n- Prediction-interval coverage.\n- Baseline comparisons.\n- Sample counts and evaluation dates.\n\nNo future prices, current retrospective metadata, or future corporate-action information may enter historical features improperly.\n\nVolatility adjustment primarily affects move magnitude and tail risk. Frontend experience\n\n### Dashboard\n\n- Company/ticker search with identity confirmation.\n- Forecast-mode selection.\n- Historical cutoff controls.\n- Reference price, target close, and freshness.\n- Direction-probability cards.\n- Threshold table.\n- Prediction-interval and distribution displays.\n- Historical-price chart.\n- Model and sample-size details.\n\n### History\n\n- Search by original text, company, and symbol.\n- Filter by date, mode, and status.\n- Reopen original results.\n- Compare forecasts with observed outcomes.\n- Start a fresh analysis from a previous query.\n- Export CSV/JSON.\n\n### Design acceptance\n\n- Responsive desktop and narrow-screen layouts.\n- Keyboard-accessible controls.\n- Readable contrast and typography.\n- Optional dark mode.\n- Numerical summaries for charts.\n- Clear loading, error, empty, stale-data, and insufficient-history states.\n\nCharts are downsampled for rendering while calculations retain full eligible data.\n\n---\n\n## 9. SQLite persistence and backups\n\n### Core records\n\n| Record | Contents |\n|---|---|\n| Instruments | Canonical symbol, company, exchange, currency, timezone |\n| Market bars | Daily/intraday OHLCV, actions, timestamps, provenance |\n| Queries | Original input, parameters, timestamps, status, failure information |\n| Input snapshots | Immutable, compressed, deduplicated forecast inputs |\n| Forecasts | Saved results, reference/target times, model version |\n| Outcomes | Observed returns and scoring results |\n\nEvery submitted search, analysis, reconstruction, and refresh is recorded. Deliberately repeated submissions remain distinct. Autocomplete keystrokes are interface activity rather than submitted queries.\n\n### Database behavior\n\n- Explicit transactions and foreign keys.\n- Short writes; provider calls outside transactions.\n- Thread-owned connections.\n- Busy timeout.\n- Versioned SQL migrations.\n- Indexed filters and full-text search.\n- No automatic expiry of query history.\n\nStart with rollback-journal mode. This suits the workload and avoids relying on WAL behavior in the installed SQLite version, which falls within the documented WAL-reset issue’s affected range.[4]\n\n### Backup acceptance\n\n- Automatic backup when due while the app is running.\n- Backup before migrations.\n- Manual backup command.\n- SQLite online backup API.\n- Integrity checks before marking a backup successful.\n- Configurable destination, retention, and disk limits.\n- Restore while the application is stopped.\n- Browser verification of restored history.\n\nGit stores source revisions. SQLite backups preserve application data.\n\n---\n\n## 10. Security and performance\n\n### Security\n\n- Bind to `127.0.0.1`.\n- Validate Host/Origin and protect state-changing requests.\n- Use parameterized SQL and allowlisted sort fields.\n- Validate symbol syntax, input lengths, dates, and thresholds.\n- Escape user/provider text.\n- Serve scripts locally under a restrictive Content Security Policy.\n- Keep databases, backups, logs, secrets, and caches outside static paths.\n- Use restrictive data-file permissions.\n- Sanitize spreadsheet exports.\n- Pin dependencies and run vulnerability checks.\n- Keep restore operations in the local CLI.\n\n### Performance targets\n\nMeasure on this laptop:\n\n| Measurement | Proposed target |\n|---|---|\n| Normal application-server memory | Below 500 MiB |\n| Cached single-symbol forecast | Below one second |\n| Indexed history search on 100,000-query fixture | Below 250 ms |\n| Idle behavior | Negligible background CPU consumption |\n\nNetwork latency and browser-test resource usage are recorded separately.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Playwright MCP acceptance\n\n### Setup\n\nUse the official **`@playwright/mcp`** server through OpenCode’s local MCP integration.\n\n- Install a supported ARM64 Node.js LTS runtime.\n- Pin MCP and browser-test dependencies under `tools/browser/`.\n- Register the server in `opencode.json`.\n- Configure headless Chromium explicitly.\n- Use isolated browser profiles and a dedicated acceptance database.\n- Validate browser/tool compatibility on ARM.\n- Capture session evidence and bounded diagnostic artifacts.\n- Restart OpenCode after configuration changes.\n\nPlaywright MCP is headed by default, making explicit headless configuration important.[5]\n\n### QA ownership\n\n`sol-qa` operates the MCP browser during acceptance. The coordinator verifies that the tools are actually available to that subagent and that the selected model is SOL.\n\nMCP unavailability or browser-launch failure blocks the relevant gate.\n\n### Test path\n\n```text\nSOL QA agent\n  → Playwright MCP\n  → Headless Chromium\n  → Real frontend\n  → Real API\n  → Real application services\n  → Real temporary SQLite database\n```\n\nDeterministic tests substitute data at the Yahoo adapter boundary. Browser/API/database behavior remains real.\n\nFinal live-data checks use the actual Yahoo adapter.\n\n### Browser acceptance matrix\n\n| ID | Required behavior |\n|---|---|\n| B01 | Search by company name and select the correct instrument |\n| B02 | Switch symbols without mixing results or history |\n| B03 | Complete a daily forecast with correct displayed results |\n| B04 | Complete an intraday forecast with correct reference and target times |\n| B05 | Display populated charts, thresholds, and intervals |\n| B06 | Run and correctly label historical reconstruction |\n| B07 | Find successful, failed, and repeated queries |\n| B08 | Restart and reopen an original forecast |\n| B09 | Refresh data without changing an earlier saved result |\n| B10 | Handle invalid symbols, missing data, rate limits, and stale data |\n| B11 | Export and verify CSV/JSON contents |\n| B12 | Restore a backup and retrieve restored history through the browser |\n| B13 | Operate core flows by keyboard and at narrow viewport widths |\n| B14 | Confirm API-mediated data access and inaccessible database files |\n| B15 | Complete real-Yahoo daily and intraday user journeys |\n| B16 | Identify uncaught browser errors and unexpected external dependencies |\n\nSuccessful data-rich scenarios must produce numerical forecasts. Error-state handling alone cannot satisfy forecasting acceptance.\n\n### Automated regression tests\n\nAlongside MCP acceptance:\n- Python pytest covers numerical, API, and database behavior.\n- Checked-in Playwright Test scenarios run in CI.\n- MCP-driven QA covers interactive acceptance and diagnosis.\n\n**Both recorded MCP acceptance and automated regression checks are required.**\n\n---\n\n## 12. Correctness tests\n\nHighest-priority tests include:\n\n1. Appending future prices cannot change an earlier forecast.\n2. Yahoo cache updates cannot alter saved results.\n3. Larger downside thresholds cannot have higher exceedance probabilities.\n4. Up/down/unchanged probabilities sum to one.\n5. Prediction intervals are ordered and use the displayed reference price.\n6. Splits and currency-unit changes do not become artificial crashes.\n7. Incomplete bars are excluded.\n8. Session gaps do not become ordinary daily returns.\n9. Intraday evaluation groups observations by session.\n10. History survives restart and restore.\n11. Interrupted and failed requests remain identifiable.\n12. Orchestrated acceptance loop\n\n### Step 1 — Select and define\n\nThe coordinator:\n- Selects a ready task.\n- Confirms dependencies.\n- Defines observable acceptance criteria.\n- Assigns file ownership.\n- Dispatches up to three SOL roles.\n\n### Step 2 — Build and prepare\n\n- Build implements.\n- QA develops independent verification cases.\n- Documentation prepares relevant updates.\n\n### Step 3 — Stable handoff\n\nBuild reports:\n- Files changed.\n- Implemented behavior.\n- Developer checks performed.\n- Known limitations.\n\nChanges to the verification target pause.\n\n### Step 4 — Independent QA\n\nQA:\n- Reviews the implementation against requirements.\n- Runs focused tests.\n- Exercises applicable flows through Playwright MCP.\n- Inspects API/network behavior, browser errors, and persistence.\n- Returns pass/fail findings with evidence.\n\n### Step 5 — Repair\n\nIf QA fails:\n- Coordinator creates explicit defect tasks.\n- Build repairs the root cause.\n- Documentation adjusts affected descriptions.\n- QA reruns affected checks and the required regression gate.\n\nAn unexplained intermittent pass is not sufficient. Repeated failures without a new diagnosis become a documented blocker rather than an endless blind retry loop.\n\n### Step 6 — Documentation verification\n\nDocumentation confirms:\n- Setup commands execute as documented.\n- API behavior matches actual responses.\n- Model terminology matches implementation.\n- Backup and restore procedures match tested behavior.\n- No unfinished functionality is described as complete.\n\n### Step 7 — Accept and publish\n\nThe coordinator:\n1. Reviews QA and documentation evidence.\n2. Inspects Git status, diff, and recent commits.\n3. Stages intended files.\n4. Commits the checkpoint.\n5. Pushes it.\n6. Verifies the remote revision and CI.\n7. Marks the checkpoint published.\n\n### Step 8 — Continue\n\nAdvance to the next ready task. Regressions reopen affected tasks.\n\n---\n\n## 17.                 "text": "\"\"\"M03/M06 resource smoke tests keep deterministic local work within explicit bounds.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport tracemalloc\nfrom datetime import UTC, datetime\n\nfrom stock_probs.provider import FixtureProvider\nfrom stock_probs.repository import Repository\nfrom stock_probs.service import ForecastService\n\nFIXED_NOW = datetime(2025, 1, 10, 17, 3, tzinfo=UTC)\n\n\ndef test_bounded_fixture_forecast_batch_stays_small(settings):\n    repository = Repository(settings.database_path)\n    repository.migrate()\n    service = ForecastService(repository, FixtureProvider(), lambda: FIXED_NOW)\n\n    tracemalloc.start()\n    for index in range(20):\n        service.search(f\"LOAD{index}\", \"stock\")\n    _, peak = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()\n    tracemalloc.stop()\n\n    # Twenty immutable snapshots cover a useful burst without desktop-scale memory or disk use.\n    assert peak < 64 * 1024 * 1024\n    assert settings.database_path.stat().st_size < 16 * 1024 * 1024\n    assert repository.history(page_size=100)[\"total\"] == 20\n\n\ndef test_dashboard_and_price_slice_stay_lightweight(client):\n    # The shell/docs have no framework bundle, and chart consumers request a tiny captured slice.\n    asset_bytes = sum(\n        len(client.get(path).content)\n        for path in (\n            \"/\",\n            \"/api/v1/docs\",\n            \"/assets/app.css\",\n            \"/assets/app.js\",\n            \"/assets/favicon.svg\",\n        )\n    )\n    created = client.post(\n        \"/api/v1/forecasts\", json={\"symbol\": \"ACDC\", \"asset_type\": \"stock\"}\n    ).json()\n    prices = client.get(\n        f\"/api/v1/history/{created['event']['id']}/prices\",\n        params={\"series\": \"daily\", \"limit\": 10},\n    )\n\n    assert asset_bytes < 96 * 1024\n    assert prices.status_code == 200\n    assert len(prices.content) < 8 * 1024",

If a new shared path is needed, stop the wave, assign one owner, and continue in a later wave.\n\nBuilders may run checks only with isolated:\n\n- loopback ports;\n- SQLite/database files;\n- backup/trust-key directories;\n- browser reports, traces, screenshots, coverage, and logs;\n- task/lane-specific temporary environments.\n\nAfter all three reports arrive, freeze the worktree and candidate revision. Assign exact task ID, dependencies, lane manifest, and acceptance rows.\n2. Run all three builders concurrently.\n3. Wait for every report.\n4. Run independent `LUNA MAX QA`.\n5. After QA has produced its final result, run `LUNA MAX docs`; docs must consume that exact result and cannot fill missing evidence.\n6. Repair every failure, skip, unavailable provider, stale-data issue, accessibility finding, or missing artifact.\n7. Complete the matching export/remote gate before advancing.\n\nThis is stricter than allowing QA and docs to run concurrently and satisfies the requirement that documentation review consume final QA results.\n\n## Export and CI receipt protocol\n\nAvoid a self-referential CI cycle by recording two identities:\n\n- **Tested commit:** the candidate source commit pushed for external CI.\n- **Export commit/revision:** the full-session `SESSION-EXPORT.md` revision containing the precommit session and secret-review result.\n\nProtocol:\n\n1. Freeze candidate.\n2. Generate the complete full-session export before commit.\n3. Review the entire export for secrets before commit.\n4. Commit and push the candidate/export.\n5. Obtain the external post-push CI receipt, including URL, workflow, job conclusions, and exact `head_sha`.\n6. Record that receipt against the tested commit; do not claim that a later receipt-only commit was tested by the CI result it documents.\n7. Preserve the receipt in the next full-session export/checkpoint.\n\nThe current successful run is evidence for its named single-platform jobs only. A future milestone requires a new external receipt for the exact candidate commit. Failed, skipped, unavailable, or connectivity-blocked export, secret review, push, remote verification, or CI remains blocking (`MVP-ROADMAP.md:L66-L76`).\n\n## New architecture and backup gates\n\n### Native toolchain matrix\n\nOn both native `aarch64` and native `x86_64`:\n\n- verify host and interpreter architecture;\n- install the pinned Python environment;\n- run `make check`;\n- portability\n\n`M05` must test:\n\n- backup created on ARM64, restored and promoted on x86-64;\n- backup created on x86-64, restored and promoted on ARM64;\n- schema, SQLite integrity, representative with active data protected.\n\n### Trust-key lifecycle\n\nTest on both architectures:\n\n- initial key creation and permission policy;\n- signing and verification with key IDs;\n- key rotation while retaining verification of permitted historical backups;\n- revoked, missing, unknown, or wrong keys fail closed;\n- keys are not embedded in artifacts, logs, browser responses, or exports;\n- restore
