           }\n-          },\n-          \"id\": \"prt_08c698c2a001YagzeIOLDaGGgW\",\n-          \"sessionID\": \"ses_f73b976e8ffekNCE6SNIanpXFb\",\n-          \"messageID\": \"msg_08c6810cb002cWwlghFkQQMiCJ\"\n-        },\n-        {\n           \"type\": \"text\",\n-          \"text\": \"# Full MVP plan\\n\\n**Build a fully functional local stock-probability application, delivered through a coordinator and up to three SOL subagents per task: Build, QA, and Documentation.**\\n\\nThe application will use Yahoo Finance data, expose all application data through an API, preserve searchable history in SQLite, and require **headless Playwright MCP acceptance testing**.\\n\\nThe sections below form the proposed contents of `MVP-PLAN.md` and `MVP-ROADMAP.md`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n# `MVP-PLAN.md`\\n\\n## 1. Product objective\\n\\nThe application must answer:\\n\\n> “Using the information available at this cutoff, what is the estimated probability this stock rises or falls by the target close, and what sizes of move are plausible?”\\n\\n### Required MVP capabilities\\n\\n| ID | Requirement |\\n|---|---|\\n| R01 | Search by company name or ticker and freely switch between stocks and ETFs |\\n| R02 | Use the most recent eligible Yahoo Finance data, with visible timestamps and freshness |\\n| R03 | Produce close-to-close forecasts |\\n| R04 | Produce intraday-to-close forecasts |\\n| R05 | Display direction probabilities, movement thresholds, conditional gains/losses, and prediction intervals |\\n| R06 | Provide a polished, responsive dashboard with historical charts |\\n| R07 | Route all frontend application-data access through the API |\\n| R08 | Record and search every submitted query, including repeated and failed requests |\\n| R09 | Preserve original forecasts, their inputs, and subsequent outcomes |\\n| R10 | Provide verified SQLite backups and restoration |\\n| R11 | Meet security, correctness, and laptop-performance acceptance criteria |\\n| R12 | Pass Playwright MCP browser acceptance and automated regression tests |\\n| R13 | Provide reproducible setup, documentation, CI, and published Git revisions |\\n\\n**Both forecast modes belong in the completed MVP.** A daily-only dashboard is an intermediate milestone.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 2. Verified environment and constraints\\n\\n| Component | Observed environment |\\n|---|---|\\n| Architecture | ARM64 / `aarch64` |\\n| CPU | 8 cores, Cortex-A55 and Cortex-A76 |\\n| Memory | 6.5 GiB |\\n| Swap | None |\\n| Workspace filesystem | 10 GiB total; approximately 5.9 GiB free during inspection |\\n| OS | Debian 12 |\\n| Python | 3.11.2 |\\n| SQLite | 3.40.1 with full-text search support |\\n| Node.js | Not currently available on `PATH` |\\n| Git remote | `https://github.com/eddiesoz/stock_probs.git` |\\n\\nThe repository currently contains prototype scripts, including a broken Yahoo Finance script, and a committed Python virtual environment.\\n\\n### Design implications\\n\\n- One application service and one SQLite database.\\n- Bounded network concurrency.\\n- Incremental data acquisition and caching.\\n- Serial browser testing on the laptop.\\n- Controlled backup and diagnostic-artifact retention.\\n- Project-local, locked development dependencies.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. SOL subagent orchestration\\n\\n### Coordinator\\n\\nThe primary agent owns:\\n\\n- Task decomposition and dependency order.\\n- Acceptance criteria and file ownership.\\n- Dispatching and resuming subagents.\\n- Resolving disagreements between Build and QA.\\n- Roadmap status and evidence tracking.\\n- Git staging, commits, pushes, and release verification.\\n\\n### Three available SOL roles\\n\\n| Role | Responsibilities | Ownership |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| **`sol-build`** | Implement application behavior, migrations, integrations, and focused developer tests; repair QA findings | Assigned application/configuration files and unit/integration tests |\\n| **`sol-qa`** | Independently verify requirements, review changes, maintain acceptance tests, operate Playwright MCP, and report defects | Acceptance tests and QA evidence; application changes return to Build |\\n| **`sol-docs`** | Document verified setup, API behavior, model behavior, operational procedures, and changes | Assigned documentation files |\\n\\nAll three profiles will explicitly select **GPT-5.6 Sol** using the verified identifier for the authenticated provider.\\n\\nOpenCode documents `opencode/gpt-5.6-sol` for its Zen provider. The current local configuration contains no SOL role profiles, so model availability and actual subagent model selection must be verified during bootstrap.[1]\\n\\n### Orchestration limits\\n\\n- Up to **three subagents per task**, one per role.\\n- At most three active subagents across the project initially.\\n- One implementation workstream at a time on this laptop.\\n- Reuse the same role sessions during repairs.\\n- Subagents do not create additional subagents.\\n- Only the coordinator performs Git publication and changes acceptance status.\\n\\n### Parallel work and handoff\\n\\nAt task start:\\n\\n- Build implements.\\n- QA prepares independent acceptance cases and fixtures.\\n- Documentation prepares the relevant document structure.\\n\\nAfter Build supplies a stable handoff:\\n\\n- Build pauses changes to the files under verification.\\n- QA tests that specific source revision.\\n- Documentation checks the actual implementation and verified commands.\\n- QA findings return to Build.\\n- Any behavior change invalidates the affected acceptance evidence.\\n\\nOnly QA controls the acceptance browser during a verification session. Shared files, such as manifests and the roadmap, have one designated writer.\\n\\n### Task packet\\n\\nEvery delegated task receives:\\n\\n```text\\nTask ID and objective\\nRequirement IDs\\nDependencies and relevant design decisions\\nAssigned files\\nAcceptance criteria\\nRequired verification commands and MCP journeys\\nExpected outputs\\nKnown constraints\\n```\\n\\nEvery role returns a concise report with changed files, evidence, unresolved issues, and handoff instructions.\\n\\n**A Build agent’s completion claim is not sufficient for acceptance.**\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 4. Application architecture\\n\\n```text\\nBrowser\\n  ├── HTML/CSS/JavaScript\\n  └── HTTP requests to /api/v1/*\\n                 │\\n                 ▼\\n              FastAPI\\n                 │\\n                 ▼\\n         Application services\\n          ├── Yahoo adapter\\n          ├── Forecast engine\\n          ├── Outcome evaluation\\n          └── Database repository\\n                       │\\n                       ▼\\n                     SQLite\\n```\\n\\n### Stack\\n\\n| Layer | Technology |\\n|---|---|\\n| Backend | FastAPI, one Uvicorn worker |\\n| Frontend | Jinja2 page shells, CSS, small JavaScript modules |\\n| Charts | Locally served Chart.js |\\n| Market data | yfinance behind an application-owned adapter |\\n| Numerical work | NumPy/pandas, SciPy where useful |\\n| Trading schedules | `exchange_calendars` |\\n| Database | Python `sqlite3` |\\n| Python dependencies | `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` |\\n| Browser tooling | Project-local npm package and lockfile |\\n| Agent browser testing | Official Playwright MCP server |\\n| Regression tests | pytest and Playwright Test |\\n| Code checks | Ruff, mypy, dependency vulnerability checks |\\n\\n### Mandatory API boundary\\n\\nThe frontend obtains forecasts, prices, query history, exports, and backup status through the API.\\n\\nSQL, database connections, provider calls, and database files belong to the backend. Database and backup directories are outside publicly served paths.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 5. API contract\\n\\n| Endpoint | Responsibility |\\n|---|---|\\n| `POST /api/v1/searches` | Record and execute a company/ticker search |\\n| `POST /api/v1/forecasts` | Validate a forecast request, obtain inputs, calculate, and persist |\\n| `GET /api/v1/forecasts/{id}` | Return an original saved forecast |\\n| `GET /api/v1/history` | Search and paginate submitted queries |\\n| `GET /api/v1/instruments/{id}/prices` | Return historical price data |\\n| `GET /api/v1/exports` | Export selected records through validated filters |\\n| `GET /api/v1/backups/status` | Return backup status |\\n| `GET /api/v1/health` | Support readiness checks |\\n\\nForecast responses include:\\n\\n- Instrument identity, exchange, and currency.\\n- Requested mode and effective mode.\\n- Reference price and observation timestamp.\\n- Data-fetch timestamp and freshness.\\n- Target session and close time.\\n- Probabilities, thresholds, and prediction intervals.\\n- Sample size and data-quality status.\\n- Model/configuration version.\\n- Saved forecast identifier.\\n\\nErrors use consistent codes and readable messages. Pagination, query sizes, and sorting are bounded and validated.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 6. Yahoo Finance data pipeline\\n\\n```text\\nRecord request\\n  → Resolve instrument\\n  → Check cache and market schedule\\n  → Fetch eligible data\\n  → Validate and normalize\\n  → Save forecast input snapshot\\n  → Calculate forecast\\n  → Persist result\\n  → Return API response\\n```\\n\\n### Data handling\\n\\n- Retrieve daily history on demand, up to ten years where available.\\n- Retrieve five-minute history for intraday analysis.\\n- Store market-observation time separately from download time.\\n- Preserve exchange timezone, currency, and corporate actions.\\n- Exclude incomplete bars from completed-period calculations.\\n- Identify missing sessions rather than treating gaps as ordinary one-day returns.\\n- Verify the price-adjustment policy with split and dividend fixtures.\\n- Preserve genuine large moves while identifying corrupt or inconsistent data.\\n- Resolve the exchange calendar explicitly; unsupported schedules produce a clear status.\\n\\n### Freshness and failure behavior\\n\\n- Refresh daily data when another session may have completed.\\n- Refresh intraday data at bounded intervals while relevant.\\n- Pause frontend polling when the page is hidden.\\n- Coalesce duplicate in-flight provider requests.\\n- Apply timeouts and limited backoff.\\n- Preserve cached results with their actual timestamps.\\n- Backfill available gaps when the laptop resumes.\\n\\nYahoo five-minute history is limited to approximately 60 calendar days in yfinance’s implementation. The local archive will grow as data is collected; gaps beyond the provider’s retention remain identifiable.[2]\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 7. Forecast definitions and model\\n\\n### A. Close-to-close\\n\\n**Reference:** the latest completed trading session’s close.\\n\\n**Target:** the next trading session’s close.\\n\\nThe initial model will compare:\\n1. An empirical historical distribution.\\n2. A volatility-adjusted historical distribution.\\n\\nThe volatility-adjusted model:\\n\\n- Calculates historical returns.\\n- Estimates volatility causally.\\n- Standardizes historical shocks.\\n- Rescales those shocks to the current volatility estimate.\\n- Derives all probabilities and intervals from one consistent distribution.\\n\\nFiltered historical simulation is suitable for a lightweight numerical implementation, but its quality depends on the volatility estimate and available history.[3]\\n\\n### B. Intraday-to-close\\n\\n**Reference:** the newest eligible completed five-minute bar.\\n\\n**Target:** the upcoming regular-session close.\\n\\nUse historical returns from comparable intraday cutoffs to their session closes, respecting exchange-local time and session type.\\n\\nWhen no fresh eligible regular-session observation exists, show a closed-market or stale-data state and identify the available daily forecast.\\n\\nIntraday sample sizes are smaller. Minimum-data criteria and uncertainty must be visible, especially for rare large moves.\\n\\n### C. Outputs\\n\\n- Probability of rising, falling, or remaining unchanged.\\n- Median predicted percentage move.\\n- Conditional median gain and conditional median loss.\\n- 50%, 80%, and 95% prediction intervals.\\n- Initial thresholds of ±1%, ±3%, ±5%, and ±10%.\\n- Equivalent price levels in the instrument’s currency.\\n\\nThese describe outcomes **at the target close**. Intraday barrier-touch probabilities would require a separately defined model.\\n\\n### D. Historical reconstruction\\n\\nThe interface distinguishes:\\n\\n- **Saved forecast:** the result actually recorded at that time.\\n- **Historical reconstruction:** a calculation performed later using a historical cutoff.\\n\\nYahoo can revise historical data. Saved input snapshots establish what this application used; a later reconstruction cannot establish exactly what Yahoo originally served.\\n\\n### E. Model evaluation\\n\\nUse chronological walk-forward evaluation and a separate final evaluation period.\\n\\nReport:\\n- Direction and threshold Brier scores.\\n- Reliability plots.\\n- Prediction-interval coverage.\\n- Baseline comparisons.\\n- Sample counts and evaluation dates.\\n\\nNo future prices, current retrospective metadata, or future corporate-action information may enter historical features improperly.\\n\\nVolatility adjustment primarily affects move magnitude and tail risk. Additional directional models should be introduced only after demonstrating value in out-of-sample evaluation.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 8. Frontend experience\\n\\n### Dashboard\\n\\n- Company/ticker search with identity confirmation.\\n- Forecast-mode selection.\\n- Historical cutoff controls.\\n- Reference price, target close, and freshness.\\n- Direction-probability cards.\\n- Threshold table.\\n- Prediction-interval and distribution displays.\\n- Historical-price chart.\\n- Model and sample-size details.\\n\\n### History\\n\\n- Search by original text, company, and symbol.\\n- Filter by date, mode, and status.\\n- Reopen original results.\\n- Compare forecasts with observed outcomes.\\n- Start a fresh analysis from a previous query.\\n- Export CSV/JSON.\\n\\n### Design acceptance\\n\\n- Responsive desktop and narrow-screen layouts.\\n- Keyboard-accessible controls.\\n- Readable contrast and typography.\\n- Optional dark mode.\\n- Numerical summaries for charts.\\n- Clear loading, error, empty, stale-data, and insufficient-history states.\\n\\nCharts are downsampled for rendering while calculations retain full eligible data.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 9. SQLite persistence and backups\\n\\n### Core records\\n\\n| Record | Contents |\\n|---|---|\\n| Instruments | Canonical symbol, company, exchange, currency, timezone |\\n| Market bars | Daily/intraday OHLCV, actions, timestamps, provenance |\\n| Queries | Original input, parameters, timestamps, status, failure information |\\n| Input snapshots | Immutable, compressed, deduplicated forecast inputs |\\n| Forecasts | Saved results, reference/target times, model version |\\n| Outcomes | Observed returns and scoring results |\\n\\nEvery submitted search, analysis, reconstruction, and refresh is recorded. Deliberately repeated submissions remain distinct. Autocomplete keystrokes are interface activity rather than submitted queries.\\n\\n### Database behavior\\n\\n- Explicit transactions and foreign keys.\\n- Short writes; provider calls outside transactions.\\n- Thread-owned connections.\\n- Busy timeout.\\n- Versioned SQL migrations.\\n- Indexed filters and full-text search.\\n- No automatic expiry of query history.\\n\\nStart with rollback-journal mode. This suits the workload and avoids relying on WAL behavior in the installed SQLite version, which falls within the documented WAL-reset issue’s affected range.[4]\\n\\n### Backup acceptance\\n\\n- Automatic backup when due while the app is running.\\n- Backup before migrations.\\n- Manual backup command.\\n- SQLite online backup API.\\n- Integrity checks before marking a backup successful.\\n- Configurable destination, retention, and disk limits.\\n- Restore while the application is stopped.\\n- Browser verification of restored history.\\n\\nGit stores source revisions. SQLite backups preserve application data.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 10. Security and performance\\n\\n### Security\\n\\n- Bind to `127.0.0.1`.\\n- Validate Host/Origin and protect state-changing requests.\\n- Use parameterized SQL and allowlisted sort fields.\\n- Validate symbol syntax, input lengths, dates, and thresholds.\\n- Escape user/provider text.\\n- Serve scripts locally under a restrictive Content Security Policy.\\n- Keep databases, backups, logs, secrets, and caches outside static paths.\\n- Use restrictive data-file permissions.\\n- Sanitize spreadsheet exports.\\n- Pin dependencies and run vulnerability checks.\\n- Keep restore operations in the local CLI.\\n\\n### Performance targets\\n\\nMeasure on this laptop:\\n\\n| Measurement | Proposed target |\\n|---|---|\\n| Normal application-server memory | Below 500 MiB |\\n| Cached single-symbol forecast | Below one second |\\n| Indexed history search on 100,000-query fixture | Below 250 ms |\\n| Idle behavior | Negligible background CPU consumption |\\n\\nNetwork latency and browser-test resource usage are recorded separately.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 11. Playwright MCP acceptance\\n\\n### Setup\\n\\nUse the official **`@playwright/mcp`** server through OpenCode’s local MCP integration.\\n\\n- Install a supported ARM64 Node.js LTS runtime.\\n- Pin MCP and browser-test dependencies under `tools/browser/`.\\n- Register the server in `opencode.json`.\\n- Configure headless Chromium explicitly.\\n- Use isolated browser profiles and a dedicated acceptance database.\\n- Validate browser/tool compatibility on ARM.\\n- Capture session evidence and bounded diagnostic artifacts.\\n- Restart OpenCode after configuration changes.\\n\\nPlaywright MCP is headed by default, making explicit headless configuration important.[5]\\n\\n### QA ownership\\n\\n`sol-qa` operates the MCP browser during acceptance. The coordinator verifies that the tools are actually available to that subagent and that the selected model is SOL.\\n\\nMCP unavailability or browser-launch failure blocks the relevant gate.\\n\\n### Test path\\n\\n```text\\nSOL QA agent\\n  → Playwright MCP\\n  → Headless Chromium\\n  → Real frontend\\n  → Real API\\n  → Real application services\\n  → Real temporary SQLite database\\n```\\n\\nDeterministic tests substitute data at the Yahoo adapter boundary. Browser/API/database behavior remains real.\\n\\nFinal live-data checks use the actual Yahoo adapter.\\n\\n### Browser acceptance matrix\\n\\n| ID | Required behavior |\\n|---|---|\\n| B01 | Search by company name and select the correct instrument |\\n| B02 | Switch symbols without mixing results or history |\\n| B03 | Complete a daily forecast with correct displayed results |\\n| B04 | Complete an intraday forecast with correct reference and target times |\\n| B05 | Display populated charts, thresholds, and intervals |\\n| B06 | Run and correctly label historical reconstruction |\\n| B07 | Find successful, failed, and repeated queries |\\n| B08 | Restart and reopen an original forecast |\\n| B09 | Refresh data without changing an earlier saved result |\\n| B10 | Handle invalid symbols, missing data, rate limits, and stale data |\\n| B11 | Export and verify CSV/JSON contents |\\n| B12 | Restore a backup and retrieve restored history through the browser |\\n| B13 | Operate core flows by keyboard and at narrow viewport widths |\\n| B14 | Confirm API-mediated data access and inaccessible database files |\\n| B15 | Complete real-Yahoo daily and intraday user journeys |\\n| B16 | Identify uncaught browser errors and unexpected external dependencies |\\n\\nSuccessful data-rich scenarios must produce numerical forecasts. Error-state handling alone cannot satisfy forecasting acceptance.\\n\\n### Automated regression tests\\n\\nAlongside MCP acceptance:\\n- Python pytest covers numerical, API, and database behavior.\\n- Checked-in Playwright Test scenarios run in CI.\\n- MCP-driven QA covers interactive acceptance and diagnosis.\\n\\n**Both recorded MCP acceptance and automated regression checks are required.**\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 12. Correctness tests\\n\\nHighest-priority tests include:\\n\\n1. Appending future prices cannot change an earlier forecast.\\n2. Yahoo cache updates cannot alter saved results.\\n3. Larger downside thresholds cannot have higher exceedance probabilities.\\n4. Up/down/unchanged probabilities sum to one.\\n5. Prediction intervals are ordered and use the displayed reference price.\\n6. Splits and currency-unit changes do not become artificial crashes.\\n7. Incomplete bars are excluded.\\n8. Session gaps do not become ordinary daily returns.\\n9. Intraday evaluation groups observations by session.\\n10. History survives restart and restore.\\n11. Interrupted and failed requests remain identifiable.\\n12. API validation and frontend/export handling resist injection.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 13. Repository layout and commands\\n\\n### Proposed layout\\n\\n```text\\nMVP-PLAN.md\\nMVP-ROADMAP.md\\nAGENTS.md\\nREADME.md\\nopencode.json\\npyproject.toml\\nuv.lock\\nMakefile\\n\\n.opencode/agents/\\n  sol-build.md\\n  sol-qa.md\\n  sol-docs.md\\n\\nsrc/stock_probs/\\n  app.py\\n  cli.py\\n  services.py\\n  db.py\\n  providers/\\n  forecasting/\\n  templates/\\n  static/\\n\\nmigrations/\\ntests/\\ntools/browser/\\ndocs/\\nlegacy/\\n.github/workflows/\\n```\\n\\n`AGENTS.md` will reference the plan and roadmap and contain only verified commands, boundaries, and repository-specific pitfalls.\\n\\n### Commands to implement\\n\\n| Command | Purpose |\\n|---|---|\\n| `make setup` | Install locked development dependencies |\\n| `make browser-install` | Install compatible Chromium and system prerequisites |\\n| `make dev` | Start the local application |\\n| `make check` | Format check, lint, typecheck, unit/API tests |\\n| `make browser-test` | Run deterministic browser regressions |\\n| `make acceptance` | Run deterministic acceptance, including restore tests |\\n| `make live-smoke` | Run explicit real-Yahoo verification |\\n| `make release-check` | Verify release evidence and required checks |\\n\\nMCP browser journeys are performed by QA through the configured tools. A shell command passing does not imply those journeys have occurred.\\n\\n---\\n\\n# `MVP-ROADMAP.md`\\n\\n## 14. Task states and evidence\\n\\n### States\\n\\n```text\\npending\\n  → in_progress\\n  → verifying\\n  → accepted\\n  → published\\n```\\n\\nFailures return work to implementation. Missing external prerequisites produce `blocked`.\\n\\n### Required task record\\n\\n```text\\nTask ID:\\nRequirement IDs:\\nAcceptance criteria:\\nDependencies:\\nBuild / QA / Documentation assignments:\\nAssigned files:\\nStatus:\\nVerification commands:\\nMCP scenarios:\\nTested source revision or working-tree identifier:\\nObserved results:\\nArtifact/report locations:\\nOutstanding defects:\\nPublished checkpoint and CI URL:\\n```\\n\\nThe coordinator owns status changes. Documentation may prepare evidence summaries, but acceptance requires QA results.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 16. Orchestrated acceptance loop\\n\\n### Step 1 — Select and define\\n\\nThe coordinator:\\n- Selects a ready task.\\n- Confirms dependencies.\\n- Defines observable acceptance criteria.\\n- Assigns file ownership.\\n- Dispatches up to three SOL roles.\\n\\n### Step 2 — Build and prepare\\n\\n- Build implements.\\n- QA develops independent verification cases.\\n- Documentation prepares relevant updates.\\n\\n### Step 3 — Stable handoff\\n\\nBuild reports:\\n- Files changed.\\n- Implemented behavior.\\n- Developer checks performed.\\n- Known limitations.\\n\\nChanges to the verification target pause.\\n\\n### Step 4 — Independent QA\\n\\nQA:\\n- Reviews the implementation against requirements.\\n- Runs focused tests.\\n- Exercises applicable flows through Playwright MCP.\\n- Inspects API/network behavior, browser errors, and persistence.\\n- Returns pass/fail findings with evidence.\\n\\n### Step 5 — Repair\\n\\nIf QA fails:\\n- Coordinator creates explicit defect tasks.\\n- Build repairs the root cause.\\n- Documentation adjusts affected descriptions.\\n- QA reruns affected checks and the required regression gate.\\n\\nAn unexplained intermittent pass is not sufficient. Repeated failures without a new diagnosis become a documented blocker rather than an endless blind retry loop.\\n\\n### Step 6 — Documentation verification\\n\\nDocumentation confirms:\\n- Setup commands execute as documented.\\n- API behavior matches actual responses.\\n- Model terminology matches implementation.\\n- Backup and restore procedures match tested behavior.\\n- No unfinished functionality is described as complete.\\n\\n### Step 7 — Accept and publish\\n\\nThe coordinator:\\n1. Reviews QA and documentation evidence.\\n2. Inspects Git status, diff, and recent commits.\\n3. Stages intended files.\\n4. Commits the checkpoint.\\n5. Pushes it.\\n6. Verifies the remote revision and CI.\\n7. Marks the checkpoint published.\\n\\n### Step 8 — Continue\\n\\nAdvance to the next ready task. Regressions reopen affected tasks.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 17. Git and CI workflow\\n\\nRepository: [`eddiesoz/stock_probs`](https://github.com/eddiesoz/stock_probs).\\n\\n### Foundation work\\n\\n- Verify remote state and write access.\\n- Install/authenticate GitHub CLI as needed.\\n- Untrack virtual environments while preserving local installations.\\n- Exclude databases, backups, caches, browser binaries, dependencies, secrets, and generated artifacts.\\n- Preserve the prototype implementation under `legacy/`.\\n\\n### Checkpoint policy\\n\\n- Coordinator alone stages, commits, and pushes.\\n- Each checkpoint includes implementation, tests, and verified documentation.\\n- Browser-facing checkpoints require MCP evidence and passing browser regressions.\\n- CI failures reopen the relevant milestone.\\n- Release tags identify the accepted source version.\\n\\nSource-control publication and database backups are verified separately.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 18. Final definition of done\\n\\nThe MVP is complete only when:\\n\\n- Every requirement has an accepted task and recorded evidence.\\n- Both forecast modes work with sufficient-data inputs.\\n- User-selected stocks and ETFs work without hardcoded application dependencies.\\n- Frontend data access passes through the API.\\n- Query history is searchable and survives restart.\\n- Saved forecasts and their inputs remain immutable.\\n- Backup restoration is demonstrated through the application.\\n- Playwright MCP acceptance is completed by QA.\\n- Automated checks pass on the laptop and in CI.\\n- Real Yahoo end-to-end verification succeeds.\\n- Security and resource results are documented.\\n- Fresh setup works from the committed instructions.\\n- SOL Build, QA, and Documentation handoffs are complete.\\n- The accepted source revision and release tag are verified on GitHub.\\n\\n## Research references\\n\\n1. [Bank of England: filtered historical simulation](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/working-paper/2015/filtered-historical-simulation-value-at-risk-models-and-their-competitors.pdf)\\n4. GitHub documents native `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners for public repositories; the build phase will use that route and verify actual execution. |\\n\\n**The existing application should be completed and strengthened, with fresh evidence attached to the exact revision being accepted.**\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. Execution and ownership\\n\\nUse three concurrent `SOL HIGH build` agents per build wave. This fits your allowance of up to six while respecting the repository’s current three-agent concurrency contract.\\n\\n| Agent | Sole implementation ownership |\\n|---|---|\\n| **SOL HIGH-A — Application/API** | `api.py`, `schemas.py`, `config.py`, `cli.py`, API and configuration tests |\\n| **SOL HIGH-B — Forecasting/data** | Domain, provider, service, repository, backup, migrations, fixtures, numerical/persistence/restore tests, `tests/conftest.py` |\\n| **SOL HIGH-C — Interface/tooling** | `static/**`, `tools/browser/**`, scripts, Makefile, dependency manifests, CI, OpenCode configuration, resource tests |\\n\\nEvery assignment must name an exact milestone or repair ID, paths, dependencies, acceptance requirements, and expected handoff.\\n\\n**Wave sequence:**\\n\\n1. Declare ownership and interfaces.\\n2. Run the three builders concurrently.\\n3. Wait for all handoffs.\\n4. Freeze the implementation under review.\\n5. Run independent `LUNA MAX QA`; docs may prepare their review concurrently.\\n6. `LUNA MAX docs` finalizes records against the actual QA results.\\n7. Repair failures and rerun affected checks.\\n8. Complete the milestone’s export, commit, push, remote, and CI gate.\\n\\nAgents must use isolated databases, backup directories, ports, and artifacts. Shared-file changes receive one explicit builder owner. The coordinator handles planning, integration, status, and Git.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 2. M00 — Reconcile the contract and recovery record\\n\\n**Owner: LUNA MAX docs, with coordinator evidence and ID assignments.**\\n\\nBefore further implementation:\\n\\n- Preserve and reconcile the existing uncommitted documentation changes.\\n- Update the supported scope to **Linux ARM64/aarch64 and Linux x86-64/amd64**.\\n- Correct historical task references and repair-ID collisions, including the separate issues previously labelled `R-M04-1`.\\n- Record that the late backup retest passed `make check`; preserve the earlier failure as history.\\n- Record the newly verified remote and CI results against their exact commit.\\n- Establish one unambiguous final-review/export order.\\n- Confirm that an independent GPT-6 Astra reviewer can be invoked with the required tools.\\n\\n### Recover requirements missing from the condensed roadmap\\n\\nThe earlier approved plan contains requirements that are no longer explicit acceptance rows:\\n\\n- Company-name lookup and instrument identity.\\n- Historical cutoff reconstruction, distinct from reopening a saved forecast.\\n- Walk-forward model evaluation, baseline comparison, probability scoring, and interval coverage.\\n- Historical-price and distribution charts.\\n- CSV and JSON exports.\\n- Automatic/pre-migration backup behavior and retention limits.\\n- Explicit performance targets.\\n\\nDocs must map these into the existing M01–M07 milestones, distinguishing accepted requirements from optional proposals. **Anything accepted remains an acceptance obligation unless you explicitly change its scope.**\\n\\nThen complete `EXP-M00` before advancing.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. Dependency-ordered build milestones\\n\\n### M01 — Portable application and accurate API contract\\n\\n**Build objectives**\\n\\n- Verify pinned dependencies on both architectures.\\n- Build a distributable package and test a clean, non-editable installation, including static assets, migrations, and fixtures.\\n- Make setup commands architecture-neutral; reconcile the misleading `install-node-arm64.sh` name with its existing x64 support.\\n- Establish the native ARM64/x86-64 CI matrix early enough to verify subsequent milestones.\\n- Independently retest structured 404/405 errors, OpenAPI schemas, CSP-safe API documentation, validation, and startup.\\n- Confirm loopback-only operation and `/api/v1`-only browser data access.\\n\\n**Exit:** native installation/startup and API evidence for both architectures, then `EXP-M01`.\\n\\n### M02 — Complete auditability and durable history\\n\\n**Build objectives**\\n\\n- Verify clean migration and upgrades without rewriting an already-used migration.\\n- Preserve exactly one submission event for every successful, failed, and repeated forecast request.\\n- Verify immutable inputs/results and append-only outcomes/corrections.\\n- Complete bounded history filtering, pagination, exports, restart, and concurrency behavior.\\n- Distinguish saved-result reopening from newly calculated historical reconstruction.\\n- Verify history remains usable at the agreed large-history benchmark.\\n\\n**Exit:** independent persistence/API matrix, then `EXP-M02`.\\n\\n### M03 — Forecast correctness and meaningful model documentation\\n\\n**Build objectives**\\n\\n- Verify both horizons independently, including completed-bar exclusion and origin/target timestamps.\\n- Cover holidays, early closes, special closures, missing bars, stale data, and outside-session requests.\\n- Verify arbitrary supported stock/ETF selections and expose exchange, currency, timezone, and provider limitations.\\n- Confirm probability definitions, threshold ordering, interval levels, units, and reproducibility.\\n- Demonstrate that future or incomplete data cannot alter an earlier forecast.\\n- Implement the recovered evaluation requirements with chronological separation and baseline comparisons.\\n- Exercise live Yahoo through the application/API/persistence path, alongside deterministic fixtures.\\n\\n**Exit:** numerical, temporal, provider, provenance, and evaluation evidence; live availability recorded honestly; then `EXP-M03`.\\n\\n### M04 — Beautiful dashboard and complete user journeys\\n\\n**Build objectives**\\n\\n- Refine the existing **Signal Ledger** design.\\n- Complete forecast comparison, charts, history, reconstruction, exports, and outcome presentation.\\n- Expose important timestamps and repeated-failure status clearly.\\n- Independently retest mobile failure focus/scroll behavior.\\n- Verify every visible control and all loading, empty, success, repeated, stale, validation, and failure states.\\n\\n**Exit:** visual review, browser journeys, accessibility, and API-only network evidence, then `EXP-M04`.\\n\\n### M05 — Reliable backups and cross-architecture recovery\\n\\n**Build objectives**\\n\\n- Verify archive integrity, authenticity, schema compatibility, bounds, staging, promotion, and rollback.\\n- Reject tampered, truncated, forged, incompatible, and unsafe-path artifacts.\\n- Document and test the separate backup trust key’s creation, storage, recovery, and missing/wrong-key behavior.\\n- Test **ARM64-created backups restored on x86-64, and the reverse**.\\n- Demonstrate restored history through the browser.\\n- Implement recovered backup automation/retention requirements with bounded resource use.\\n- Verify permissions, request limits, provider timeouts, and loopback exposure.\\n\\n**Important:** copying the database archive alone is insufficient for the current authenticated-backup design. The recovery procedure must account for its trust key.\\n\\n**Exit:** independent recovery/security evidence, then `EXP-M05`.\\n\\n### M06 — Complete dual-architecture quality gates\\n\\n**Build objectives**\\n\\n- Run the required checks on native `ubuntu-24.04` and `ubuntu-24.04-arm`.\\n- Verify Python dependencies, Node, Chromium, official headless `@playwright/mcp`, and browser regressions on both.\\n- Extend MCP verification beyond initialization to real application interactions.\\n- Verify clean-host installation order, including Chromium prerequisites.\\n- Demonstrate that deliberately failing required checks causes CI failure.\\n- Publish task-, architecture-, and commit-labelled evidence.\\n- Measure process memory, latency, disk use, and idle behavior under documented resource constraints.\\n\\n**Exit:** both native matrices pass; required failures block CI; then `EXP-M06`.\\n\\n### M07 — Integrated acceptance\\n\\nRun the complete journey on both architectures:\\n\\n**Select stock/ETF → obtain both forecasts → inspect probabilities, intervals, and provenance → find successful/failed/repeated history → reopen saved results → append outcomes → export → restart → back up → restore → reopen restored history.**\\n\\nReconcile the final README, agent rules, plan, roadmap, limitations, and evidence records.\\n\\nThen proceed to independent Astra acceptance.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 4. Visual design brief\\n\\nThe presentation builder should evolve Signal Ledger into a polished financial research interface:\\n\\n- Warm paper surfaces, deep ink typography, restrained rust accents, and consistent spacing.\\n- Clear numerical hierarchy and aligned tabular figures.\\n- A compact search area that keeps useful results prominent.\\n- Side-by-side horizon cards on desktop, stacked naturally on mobile.\\n- Readable probability and interval graphics with equivalent tables.\\n- Clearly distinguished current, stale, failed, repeated, and reconstructed states.\\n- Detailed provenance available without overwhelming the primary result.\\n- Locally served assets and a lightweight frontend.\\n\\n### Visual acceptance criteria\\n\\n- Review screenshots at **360, 390, 768, 1280, and 1440 pixels**.\\n- No clipped content, overlapping controls, or unintended page overflow.\\n- Review populated results and every important state—not only the empty screen.\\n- Verify contrast, keyboard focus, touch targets, zoom/reflow, and reduced motion.\\n- Include actual assistive-technology evidence; axe and keyboard tests alone do not establish screen-reader acceptance.\\n- Require a named visual reviewer to record findings and repairs.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 5. Dual-architecture verification contract\\n\\nThe same candidate revision must pass this matrix:\\n\\n| Check | x86-64 | ARM64 |\\n|---|---:|---:|\\n| Native host/runtime identity | Required | Required |\\n| Package build and clean installation | Required | Required |\\n| `make check` | Required | Required |\\n| Loopback startup/API smoke | Required | Required |\\n| Chromium installation | Required | Required |\\n| `make mcp-smoke` and MCP application interaction | Required | Required |\\n| Desktop/mobile browser regressions | Required | Required |\\n| Backup/restore and cross-architecture recovery | Required | Required |\\n| Resource measurements | Required | Required |\\n\\nRecord architecture, OS, tool versions, command, UTC timestamp, exact revision, result, artifact, and reviewer.\\n\\nGitHub’s native ARM64 runner is the planned solution to your unavailable laptop. If it cannot execute the required checks, the affected gate remains blocked. Hosted-runner measurements must also distinguish constrained-resource testing from testing the original physical laptop.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 6. Documentation and code comments\\n\\nKeep the four documentation files purposeful:\\n\\n- **`README.md`:** installation, startup, user guide, model interpretation, platform matrix, troubleshooting, backup/trust-key recovery, and verified limitations.\\n- **`AGENTS.md`:** compact ownership rules, commands, architecture requirements, and repository-specific pitfalls.\\n- **`MVP-PLAN.md`:** complete requirements, API/model/data contracts, acceptance criteria, and repair records.\\n- **`MVP-ROADMAP.md`:** dependencies, current status, next actions, evidence links, and release gates.\\n\\nComments must explain non-obvious intent: time boundaries, leakage prevention, probability assumptions, immutable writes, restore guarantees, security decisions, and resource limits. Comment-presence checks remain useful, but reviewer judgment must establish their quality. Documentation snippets must include useful explanatory comments.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 7. @@\\n+# Agent Rules\\n+\\n+## Repository truth\\n+\\n+- The tracked application material is an exploratory Python probability prototype, not the planned web app.\\n+- `burry_env/` is tracked legacy dependency noise. Do not treat it as source, add to it, repair it, or remove it as part of feature work.\\n+- `.venv/` is a local environment. It is not an application dependency declaration and must not be committed or used as release evidence.\\n+- Do not claim an implementation milestone is complete without the acceptance evidence recorded for its task ID.\\n+\\n+## Product invariants\\n+\\n+- The target is a local ARM64 stock probability web app for user-selected Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs.\\n+- It must provide close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close forecasts, probabilities, and explicit magnitude intervals.\\n+- All frontend application data must go through FastAPI `/api/v1`. The frontend must never access SQLite directly, issue SQL, or receive a database path.\\n+- SQLite must retain every submitted successful, failed, and repeated search, plus immutable forecast inputs, results, and later outcomes.\\n+- Searchable history, verified backup/restore, a responsive accessible dashboard, secure loopback deployment, low-resource operation, and Git/CI gates are release requirements.\\n+- The official `@playwright/mcp` must be configured headless for agent QA, and automated browser regressions must be checked into the repository.\\n+- Every code change must include useful comments where the behavior is not self-evident. It does not yet contain the application described below.\\n+\\n+- `M00` is **Completed** for the four documentation files created in this baseline: `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md`.\\n+- `M01` through `M07` are **Pending**. No implementation milestone is complete.\\n+- A task may move to **Completed** only after its acceptance evidence, verification result, repair history, and reviewer are recorded.\\n+\\n+## Product Goal\\n+\\n+Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF and receives two forecast views:\\n+\\n+1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\\n+2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\\n+\\n+Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. Every displayed result must identify its symbol, asset type, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\n+\\n+This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\\n+\\n+## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\\n+\\n+### API boundary\\n+\\n+- All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\n+- The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\\n+- The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\\n+- API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\\n+\\n+### Data source and time semantics\\n+\\n+- Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\\n+- The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\\n+- The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\n+- Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\n+\\n+### Persistence and auditability\\n+\\n+- Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\n+- A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\n+- The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\n+- An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\n+- Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\n+- History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\n+\\n+### User experience\\n+\\n+- The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\n+- Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\n+- Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\n+- History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\n+- Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\\n+\\n+### Deployment and resources\\n+\\n+- The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\n+- Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\n+- Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\n+- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\\n+- All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\n+\\n+## Planned Architecture\\n+\\n+The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\n+\\n+The API/application layers should remain separable:\\n+\\n+- **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\n+- **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\n+- **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\n+- **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\n+- **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\\n+\\n+The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\n+\\n+## Forecast Contract\\n+\\n+The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\n+\\n+- Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\n+- Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\n+- What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\n+- What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\n+- What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\n+- What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\n+- What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\n+\\n+The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\\n+\\n+## Task Register\\n+\\n+The coordinator assigns no more than three agents to a task in addition to the coordinator. The listed acceptance evidence is required before status can become **Completed**.\\n+\\n+### M00 - Documentation Baseline\\n+\\n+- **Status:** Completed, docs only.\\n+- **Dependencies:** None.\\n+- **Agents:** `LUNA MAX docs`.\\n+- **Scope:** Create the plan, roadmap, compact agent rules, and honest repository README.\\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [x] `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md` exist; [x] current prototype is distinguished from planned implementation; [x] implementation milestones remain pending.\\n+- **Verification:** [x] documentation-only diff reviewed; [x] required product invariants, orchestration, evidence fields, repair loop, and final definition of done are present.\\n+- **Repair record:** None at baseline creation.\\n+\\n+### M01 - API And Application Shell\\n+\\n+- **Status:** Pending.\\n+- **Dependencies:** M00.\\n+- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\n+- **Scope:** Establish the ARM64-friendly application layout, FastAPI service, versioned `/api/v1` boundary, structured errors, health/readiness behavior, frontend shell, and documented local loopback launch path.\\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] API contract and schema tests pass; [ ] a browser can obtain application data only through `/api/v1`; [ ] no frontend source imports a database driver or opens a SQLite path; [ ] loopback smoke test passes on the target ARM64 environment; [ ] non-obvious code decisions have useful comments.\\n+- **Verification:** [ ] unit and API tests; [ ] negative validation tests; [ ] browser network inspection; [ ] local ARM64 startup and bounded-resource smoke test.\\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M01-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\n+\\n+### M02 - SQLite Audit And Immutable Records\\n+\\n+- **Status:** Pending.\\n+- **Dependencies:** M01.\\n+- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\n+- **Scope:** Define migrations and repositories for search events, successful/failed/repeated status, immutable forecast inputs, immutable results, append-only outcomes, provenance, and bounded searchable history.\\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] migration is reproducible on a clean database; [ ] every submission persists exactly one auditable event even on failure or repetition; [ ] input, result, and outcome records cannot be silently overwritten; [ ] history filters and pagination work through `/api/v1`; [ ] restart preserves records.\\n+- **Verification:** [ ] repository and migration tests; [ ] success/failure/repeat matrix; [ ] immutability and concurrent-write tests; [ ] API authorization/boundary test showing no direct browser database access.\\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M02-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\n+\\n+### M03 - Yahoo Finance Data And Forecast Engine\\n+\\n+- **Status:** Pending.\\n+- **Dependencies:** M01 and M02.\\n+- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\n+- **Scope:** Implement the provider adapter, symbol/asset validation, completed-bar selection, close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close horizons, probability calculations, magnitude intervals, provenance, stale/missing-data handling, and immutable forecast writes.\\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] stock and ETF selections follow one tested contract; [ ] an in-progress five-minute bar is excluded; [ ] both horizons identify their origin and target timestamps; [ ] probabilities and magnitude intervals include definitions, levels, units, and model/version; [ ] provider failures and insufficient data create auditable failed searches without fabricated results; [ ] deterministic fixtures reproduce recorded outputs.\\n+- **Verification:** [ ] provider adapter tests with fixtures; [ ] timezone/session and boundary-time tests; [ ] incomplete-bar, missing-bar, stale-data, and out-of-session tests; [ ] numerical invariants and repeatability checks; [ ] ARM64 resource smoke test.\\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M03-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\n+\\n+### M04 - Dashboard And Searchable History\\n+\\n+- **Status:** Pending.\\n+- **Dependencies:** M01, M02, and M03.\\n+- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\n+- **Scope:** Build the responsive accessible dashboard for symbol selection, forecast submission, result comparison, source/as-of/stale/error context, and searchable history.\\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] desktop and mobile layouts retain all essential content; [ ] keyboard and screen-reader flows cover search, results, errors, and history; [ ] loading, empty, failed, repeated, stale, and successful states are understandable without color; [ ] result views show both forecast modes, probabilities, and magnitude intervals; [ ] all data requests use `/api/v1`.\\n+- **Verification:** [ ] component and API integration tests; [ ] accessibility audit and keyboard pass; [ ] checked-in browser regression scenarios; [ ] browser network assertion for the API-only boundary; [ ] low-resource render smoke test.\\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M04-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\n+\\n+### M05 - Backup, Restore, And Secure Loopback Operations\\n+\\n+- **Status:** Pending.\\n+- **Dependencies:** M02 and M04.\\n+- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\n+- **Scope:** Add verified backup and restore workflow, integrity/manifest checks, safe restore staging, loopback deployment defaults, input/path validation, timeout limits, and operational documentation.\\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] a backup includes the required SQLite data and verifiable metadata/checksum; [ ] restore to a clean or staging location validates schema, integrity, and representative counts before promotion; [ ] a tampered, truncated, incompatible, or unsafe-path artifact is rejected; [ ] active data is not silently destroyed; [ ] default bind is loopback and security behavior is documented.\\n+- **Verification:** [ ] backup/restore round trip; [ ] negative artifact and path tests; [ ] restart and recovery test; [ ] loopback exposure check; [ ] resource and timeout checks on ARM64.\\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M05-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\n+\\n+### M06 - QA, Playwright MCP, Browser Regressions, And CI\\n+\\n+- **Status:** Pending.\\n+- **Dependencies:** M01, M02, M03, M04, and M05.\\n+- **Agents:** `LUNA MAX QA`, `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\n+- **Scope:** Configure the official `@playwright/mcp` headless for agent QA, check in automated browser regressions, and establish Git/CI gates for linting, typing or static checks where adopted, unit/API tests, accessibility, security, resource limits, migration, and backup/restore.\\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] the official MCP configuration is discoverable and runs headless; [ ] no test depends on the tracked `burry_env/` or local `.venv/`.\\n+- **Verification:** [ ] clean-environment CI run; [ ] intentional-failure gate test; [ ] headless MCP smoke run; [ ] browser regression run on desktop and mobile viewports; Repeat until the `ASTRA-FINAL` record explicitly says `Accepted`; no final release or `EXP-FINAL` may precede that wording.\\n \\n ## Product Goal\\n \\n-Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF and receives two forecast views:\\n+Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF, confirms its company name and instrument identity, and receives two forecast views:\\n \\n 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\\n 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\\n \\n-Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. Every displayed result must identify its symbol, asset type, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\n+Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. The probability contract includes up/down/unchanged direction, `+/-1%`, `+/-3%`, `+/-5%`, and `+/-10%` return thresholds, conditional gain/loss probabilities, and 50%, 80%, and 95% return and price intervals. Every displayed result must identify its company name, symbol, asset type, instrument identity, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\n \\n-This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\\n+This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy. Optional dark mode and news features are not part of the contract; options trading and public hosting are out of scope.\\n \\n ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\\n \\n ### API boundary\\n \\n - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\n - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\\n - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\\n - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\\n \\n ### Data source and time semantics\\n \\n - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\\n - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\\n - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\n - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\n+- Yahoo Finance five-minute history has an approximate 60-day availability limitation. The provider and UI must state that archive limitation and the applicable archive/session semantics; an unavailable or stale interval is evidence to record, not a reason to fabricate a result.\\n \\n ### Persistence and auditability\\n \\n - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\n - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\n - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\n - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\n - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\n - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\n+- Reopening a saved forecast must display the immutable recorded inputs/results and must not silently recalculate. A historical cutoff reconstruction is a separately labelled fresh analysis using the data available at that cutoff, with its own as-of time, model/version, and provenance.\\n \\n ### User experience\\n \\n - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\n - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\n - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\n+- Historical price and return-distribution charts must have equivalent tables/text and remain understandable in every state. The distinctive Signal Ledger direction is intentional: polished tabular numeric hierarchy, clear status evidence, and restrained visual encoding rather than a generic trading dashboard.\\n - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\n-- Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\\n+- Accessible names, semantic structure, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and actual assistive-technology/screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish. Axe and keyboard checks do not substitute for an actual screen-reader run.\\n \\n ### Deployment and resources\\n \\n - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\n - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\n - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\n-- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\\n+- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for low-resource native x86-64 and ARM64 Linux. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe; the target is below 500 MiB normal server memory, a cached forecast under 1 second, an indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU.\\n - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\n \\n ## Planned Architecture\\n \\n The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\n \\n The API/application layers should remain separable:\\n \\n - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\n - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\n - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\n - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\n-- **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\\n+- **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, dual-architecture, and browser regression checks.\\n \\n The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\n \\n ## Forecast Contract\\n \\n The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\n \\n - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\n - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\n - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\n - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\n - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\n - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\n - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\n \\n+The evaluation record must use chronological walk-forward splits with no future leakage, compare against a documented baseline, and report Brier score, reliability/calibration, and interval coverage. Rare-event estimates must expose sample counts and uncertainty rather than implying precision from sparse observations. Historical price and return-distribution views must use the same recorded provenance and provide text/table equivalents. A saved result remains a recorded result; a historical-cutoff reconstruction is explicitly a fresh analysis.\\n+\\n The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. Start the app locally and open its loopback address. Confirm the displayed source/as-of and data-quality state.\\n+2. Search by symbol or company name. Confirm the returned exchange, asset type, and instrument identity before submitting a forecast.\\n+3. Review both forecast horizons: completed-session close to next close, and latest completed five-minute bar to close. The latter must state why an in-progress bar was excluded.\\n+4. Read the explicit up/down/unchanged and threshold probabilities, conditional gain/loss, 50/80/95 return and price intervals, model/version, units, stale state, provider limitation, and provenance. Do not interpret a probability as a guarantee.\\n+5. Reopen a saved forecast to view the immutable recorded result. Use historical-cutoff reconstruction only when a separately labelled fresh analysis is wanted; it is not a rewrite or reopen of the saved result.\\n+6. Use history filters to find successful, failed, and repeated searches. Review historical price and return-distribution charts alongside their text/table equivalents, then append later outcomes without changing the original forecast.\\n+7. Export the selected records as CSV or JSON when those gates are available. Treat exported data as auditable research data, not investment advice.\\n+\\n+## Eventual Operator Guide\\n+\\n+### Install and run\\n+\\n+Use the pinned dependency manifest and the repository `Makefile`/launch documentation to create an isolated environment and perform a clean install. Do not use `burry_env/`, `.venv/`, or another local environment as a dependency declaration or release artifact. The default service binds to loopback; a broader bind is not part of the supported contract.\\n+\\n+### Data, history, and backups\\n+\\n+The server owns Yahoo Finance access and SQLite. The browser receives application data only through FastAPI `/api/v1` and never receives a database path. Operators should preserve provider/as-of and stale-data messages, keep query history unless an explicit documented policy says otherwise, observe disk/retention limits, and verify automatic due and pre-migration backups. Restore must stage and validate integrity, schema, representative counts, and trust-key state before promotion without destroying active data.\\n+\\n+Trust keys require a documented transfer, rotation, retirement, and backup lifecycle. Missing or incorrect keys must fail closed. A release gate must restore backups in both directions between native x86-64 and native ARM64; a hosted ARM runner does not replace resource measurements on the original physical low-resource laptop.\\n+\\n+### Support and resource gate\\n+\\n+Both native architectures require actual package build/clean install, `make check`, loopback startup, Node/Chromium, official headless `@playwright/mcp` application interaction, desktop/mobile browser checks, and resource evidence. The measured targets are below 500 MiB normal server memory, cached forecast under 1 second, indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU. Current x86_64 host and historical ARM64 results do not yet establish this dual-architecture gate.\\n+\\n+## Visual And Accessibility Direction\\n+\\n+The eventual interface keeps the distinctive **Signal Ledger** direction: calm, high-signal status treatment; polished tabular numeric hierarchy; charts paired with tables/text; and clear provenance instead of decorative trading noise. Every state—empty, loading, validation, success, repeated, stale, and failure—must be legible at 360, 390, 768, 1280, and 1440 CSS-pixel viewports with no overlap or overflow. Reduced motion, WCAG AA contrast/structure, visible keyboard focus, keyboard journeys, and actual assistive-technology/screen-reader runs are release evidence. Axe output and keyboard checks are useful separate checks, but neither substitutes for the actual screen-reader run.\\n+\\n+## Scope Classification\\n+\\n+- **Contract:** local Linux operation on native x86-64/amd64 and ARM64/aarch64; Yahoo stock/ETF lookup and auditable forecasts; `/api/v1` boundary; SQLite audit/history; exports; backup/restore; accessible responsive UI; official MCP/browser/CI and resource gates.\\n+- **Optional, not contract:** dark mode and news.\\n+- **Out of scope:** options trading and public hosting.\\n+\\n ## Required Future Workflow\\n \\n-All future work maximizes safe parallelism with no more than three concurrent subagents. the planned local ARM64 stock probability web app. The repository currently contains only exploratory Python scripts. It does not yet contain the application described below.\\n6: \\n7: - `M00` is **Completed** for the four documentation files created in this baseline: `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md`.\\n8: - `M01` through `M07` are **Pending**. No implementation milestone is complete.\\n9: - A task may move to **Completed** only after its acceptance evidence, verification result, repair history, and reviewer are recorded.\\n10: \\n11: ## Product Goal\\n12: \\n13: Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF and receives two forecast views:\\n14: \\n15: 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\\n16: 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\\n17: \\n18: Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. Every displayed result must identify its symbol, asset type, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\n19: \\n20: This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\\n21: \\n22: ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\\n23: \\n24: ### API boundary\\n25: \\n26: - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\n27: - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\\n28: - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\\n29: - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\\n30: \\n31: ### Data source and time semantics\\n32: \\n33: - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\\n34: - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\\n35: - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\n36: - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\n37: \\n38: ### Persistence and auditability\\n39: \\n40: - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\n41: - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\n42: - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\n43: - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\n44: - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\n45: - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\n46: \\n47: ### User experience\\n48: \\n49: - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\n50: - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\n51: - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\n52: - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\n53: - Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\\n54: \\n55: ### Deployment and resources\\n56: \\n57: - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\n58: - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\n59: - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\n60: - Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\\n61: - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\n62: \\n63: ## Planned Architecture\\n64: \\n65: The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\n66: \\n67: The API/application layers should remain separable:\\n68: \\n69: - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\n70: - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\n71: - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\n72: - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\n73: - **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\\n74: \\n75: The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\n76: \\n77: ## Forecast Contract\\n78: \\n79: The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\n80: \\n81: - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\n82: - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\n83: - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\n84: - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\n85: - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\n86: - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\n87: - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\n88: \\n89: The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\\n90: \\n91: ## Task Register\\n92: \\n93: The coordinator assigns no more than three agents to a task in addition to the coordinator.
