Every displayed result must identify its symbol, asset type, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\n\\nThis is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\\n\\n## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\\n\\n### API boundary\\n\\n- All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\n- The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\\n- The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\\n- API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\\n\\n### Data source and time semantics\\n\\n- Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\\n- The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\\n- The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\n- Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\n\\n### Persistence and auditability\\n\\n- Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\n- A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\n- The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\n- An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\n- Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\n- History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\n\\n### User experience\\n\\n- The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\n- Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\n- Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\n- History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\n- Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\\n\\n### Deployment and resources\\n\\n- The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\n- Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\n- Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\n- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\\n- All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\n\\n## Planned Architecture\\n\\nThe intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\n\\nThe API/application layers should remain separable:\\n\\n- **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\n- **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\n- **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\n- **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\n- **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\\n\\nThe exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\n\\n## Forecast Contract\\n\\nThe forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\n\\n- Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\n- Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\n- What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\n- What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\n- What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\n- What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\n- What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\n\\nThe current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\\n\\n## Task Register\\n\\nThe coordinator assigns no more than three agents to a task in addition to the coordinator. The listed acceptance evidence is required before status can become **Completed**.\\n\\n### M00 - Documentation Baseline\\n\\n- **Status:** Completed, docs only.\\n- **Dependencies:** None.\\n- **Agents:** `LUNA MAX docs`.\\n- **Scope:** Create the plan, roadmap, compact agent rules, and honest repository README.\\n- **Acceptance evidence:** [x] `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md` exist; probabilities; defined magnitude intervals; stale/error handling. |\\n| M04 | Dashboard and searchable history | M01, M02, M03 | Pending | Responsive accessible UI, full state coverage, both forecast views, and API-only application data. |\\n| M05 | Backup, restore, and secure loopback operations | M02, M04 | Pending | Verified integrity/restore round trip, rejected unsafe artifacts, safe promotion, loopback default, and bounded operations. |\\n| M06 | QA, MCP, browser regressions, and CI | M01, M02, M03, M04, M05 | Pending | Official headless `@playwright/mcp`, checked-in browser regressions, Git/CI gates, and ARM64 resource evidence. |\\n| M07 | Integrated MVP acceptance | M06 | Pending | Complete user journey, audit/history/outcome proof, restore proof, accessibility/security/QA sign-off, and honest release docs. |\\n\\n## Delivery Phases\\n\\n### Phase 0: Establish The Contract\\n\\n`M00` is complete for documentation only. The plan defines the API/storage boundary, time semantics, evidence format, verification/repair loop, and final definition of done. It does not mean that any application behavior exists.\\n\\n### Phase 1: Make The Boundary Real\\n\\n`M01` creates the smallest runnable application shape. `M02` makes search activity and forecast records durable. Do not build a UI that bypasses the API, and do not call a database schema complete without failure and repeat cases.\\n\\n### Phase 2: Make Forecasts Traceable\\n\\n`M03` integrates Yahoo Finance through a server-side adapter and separates the two forecast horizons. The key gate is not a plausible number; it is reproducibility from captured completed bars, explicit session rules, model/version, probabilities, intervals, and data-quality state.\\n\\n### Phase 3: Make The Workflow Usable\\n\\n`M04` turns the API into a responsive accessible dashboard and searchable history view. Loading, empty, failure, stale, repeated, and success states are part of the feature. All frontend application data continues to use FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\n\\n### Phase 4: Make Local Operation Durable\\n\\n`M05` adds verified backups/restores and secure loopback defaults. A restore is not accepted because a file exists; it must pass integrity, compatibility, representative-data, and non-destructive promotion checks.\\n\\n### Phase 5: Make Regressions Visible\\n\\n`M06` configures the official `@playwright/mcp` headless for agent QA, checks browser regressions into the repository, and makes Git/CI gates enforce the contract. The test environment must not depend on `burry_env/` or the local `.venv/`.\\n\\n### Phase 6: Release Only With Evidence\\n\\n`M07` exercises the full workflow on a low-resource ARM64 laptop and reconciles every acceptance field. A missing provider result, skipped accessibility check, unverified restore, direct database path, or undocumented limitation keeps the release pending.\\n\\n## Ownership Model\\n\\n- The **coordinator** owns task assignment, dependency checks, integration, status, evidence, and release decisions.\\n- **SOL HIGH build** owns application implementation, API/storage/provider/UI changes, and targeted engineering fixes.\\n- **LUNA MAX QA** owns unit/API/browser/accessibility/security/performance/restore verification and regression evidence.\\n- **LUNA MAX docs** owns this roadmap, the detailed plan, runbooks, evidence records, and honest status wording.\\n- Each task uses the coordinator plus no more than three agents. Agents must work from the explicit task ID and may not silently expand scope.\\n\\n## Gates And Repair Loop\\n\\nThe coordinator uses the following loop for every milestone:\\n\\n1. Confirm all dependency IDs are completed with evidence.\\n2. Assign up to three agents and record the task's change summary and acceptance fields.\\n3. Run targeted checks, then the relevant Git/CI gates.\\n4. On failure, leave the task pending or in progress, record the failed evidence, create a repair ID such as `R-M03-1`, and fix the root cause.\\n5. Rerun the failed check plus the affected regression set. Record the environment, result, and reviewer.\\n6. Mark completed only when all required evidence passes; never replace missing evidence with a narrative status update.\\n\\n## Roadmap Completion Record\\n\\nUse this record when a milestone is reviewed. It is intentionally blank for implementation work until that work occurs.\\n\\n- **Task ID:** `M##`.\\n- **Dependencies verified:** task IDs and evidence references.\\n- **Status:** `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`.\\n- **Acceptance evidence:** test names, logs, screenshots, fixtures, checksums, or measured resource results.\\n- **Verification result:** environment, check, timestamp, and pass/fail.\\n- **Repair history:** repair IDs, root causes, fixes, and reruns.\\n- **Reviewer:** coordinator plus verifying agent.\\n\\n## Release Definition Of Done\\n\\nThe roadmap is complete only when `M00` through `M07` are accounted for and the planned app can demonstrate all of these outcomes:\\n\\n- User-selected Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs support both forecast horizons, with the latest five-minute input always a completed bar.\\n- Probabilities and magnitude intervals have explicit definitions, levels, units, timestamps, source, model/version, and data-quality context.\\n- SQLite retains every successful, failed, and repeated search and immutable forecast inputs/results with append-only outcomes.\\n- Searchable history and verified backup/restore work through the FastAPI boundary; the frontend never accesses SQLite directly.\\n- The dashboard is responsive and accessible, and the default deployment is secure loopback with bounded ARM64 resource use.\\n- The official headless `@playwright/mcp`, checked-in browser regressions, useful code comments, and Git/CI gates are present and passing.\\n- README, plan, and roadmap describe only behavior supported by the final evidence.\",\n-                \"lineStart\": 1,\n-                \"lineEnd\": 95,\n-                \"totalLines\": 95,\n-                \"truncated\": false\n-              }\n-            },\n-            \"title\": \"MVP-ROADMAP.md\",\n-            \"time\": {\n-              \"start\": 1789063154013,\n-              \"end\": 1789063154132\n-            }\n-          },\n-          \"metadata\": {\n-            \"openai\": {\n-              \"itemId\": \"fc_09cb69de2e5decd9016aa2eff1f60887d19c678ed0b06c20af\"\n-            }\n-          },\n-          \"id\": \"prt_08c79493e001jL2Y9Xnc7rFa0g\",\n-          \"sessionID\": \"ses_f73b976e8ffekNCE6SNIanpXFb\",\n-          \"messageID\": \"msg_08c79218c001JVCg3DC6A3z6MZ\"\n-        },\n-        {\n-          \"type\": \"tool\",\n-          \"tool\": \"read\",\n-          \"callID\": \"call_V1HtXOXwvSUcABvt4Yivkzwt\",\n-          \"state\": {\n-            \"status\": \"completed\",\n-            \"input\": {\n-              \"filePath\": \"/home/eddie/stock_probs/AGENTS.md\"\n-            },\n-            \"output\": \"<path>/home/eddie/stock_probs/AGENTS.md</path>\\n<type>file</type>\\n<content>\\n1: # Agent Rules\\n2: \\n3: ## Repository truth\\n4: \\n5: - The tracked application material is an exploratory Python probability prototype, not the planned web app.\\n6: - `burry_env/` is tracked legacy dependency noise. Each remains **Pending** until its exact obligation receives an independent QA rerun and the normal export/remote gates. The old labels remain immutable historical references.\\n44: \\n45: | Historical source-qualified label | Defect obligation carried forward | Fresh repair ID | Status and evidence state |\\n46: | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n47: | `R-M01-1` in QA task `ses_f72f4e2f0ffe6hMpBTmXUnWybW` | Router error envelope/OpenAPI behavior | `R-M01-3` | **Pending**; historical failure, no fresh retest |\\n48: | `R-M01-1` in repair-builder handoff `ses_f72c4f20effeDoLPC0FuHaaGjZ` | Startup harness/launch behavior | `R-M01-4` | **Pending**; builder claim only, cancelled independent retest |\\n49: | `R-M05-1` in QA task `ses_f72f4e163ffehgqJPXwbY7ujrX` | Malicious backup artifact handling | `R-M05-5` | **Pending**; historical finding, no fresh retest |\\n50: | `R-M05-1` in the later backup/operations handoff `ses_f72c4f1baffeECZSQ37ujzSmCJ` | Chunked-request/resource handling | `R-M05-6` | **Pending**; source-qualified obligation, no fresh retest |\\n51: | `R-M06-1` in the historical QA/operations record | Port-collision behavior | `R-M06-2` | **Pending**; no independent retest |\\n52: | `R-M06-1` in the presentation repair handoff | Documentation CSP policy | `R-M06-3` | **Pending**; cancelled independent API/UI retest |\\n53: | `R-M06-1` in the presentation repair handoff | CSV formula-injection/export behavior | `R-M06-4` | **Pending**; cancelled independent API/UI retest |\\n54: | `R-M04-1` in the historical QA record | Actual assistive-technology evidence unavailable | `R-M04-2` | **Pending/Unavailable evidence**; screen-reader/assistive run still required separately |\\n55: | `R-M04-1` in the presentation repair handoff | Mobile error focus behavior | `R-M04-3` | **Pending**; cancelled independent API/UI retest |\\n56: \\n57: The source task IDs above are evidence locators, not acceptance reviewers. No alias is a pass, and no later repair may reuse one of these fresh IDs for a different defect.\\n58: \\n59: ## Mandatory Delivery Workflow\\n60: \\n61: The coordinator applies this workflow to every milestone and repair. It is a sequencing rule, not permission to infer that an existing source file works.\\n62: \\n63: ### Safe build-wave ownership\\n64: \\n65: Use exactly three concurrent `SOL HIGH build` instances in each implementation or repair wave, never more than three. The coordinator records this lane manifest against the exact milestone or repair ID before work starts; the lanes cover every implementation, configuration, and test path:\\n66: \\n67: | Lane | Sole build ownership | Handoff boundary |\\n68: | --- | --- | --- |\\n69: | `SOL HIGH-A` | Transport/application: FastAPI routes, schemas, configuration, CLI, package/launch assumptions, and transport-facing tests | Versioned API contract and launch assumptions |\\n70: | `SOL HIGH-B` | Domain/provider/persistence: forecast semantics, Yahoo/fixture adapters, service, SQLite migrations/repositories, backup/restore, and domain/storage tests | Domain and storage contracts, fixtures, and migration assumptions |\\n71: | `SOL HIGH-C` | Presentation/browser/operations: static UI, browser harness, operational scripts, Make/CI/tool configuration, dependency/runtime tooling, and presentation/operations tests | UI states, browser journeys, resource limits, and operational assumptions |\\n72: \\n73: No two builders edit the same path or silently cross a lane boundary. `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `MVP-PLAN.md`, and `MVP-ROADMAP.md` are documentation-owned; `SESSION-EXPORT.md` is export-owned. Any implementation/config/test path not named in the lane manifest is assigned to A, B, or C before work starts. Builders report the exact task ID, changed paths, checks attempted, failures, and unresolved assumptions. If a dependency requires a shared edit, builders stop and hand it to the coordinator for mechanical integration; the coordinator does not author shared implementation/config/test content. The build wave is complete only after all three builder reports arrive.\\n74: \\n75: ### Ordered gates\\n76: \\n77: 1. Assign the exact `M##` or repair ID and record verified dependencies, lane ownership, and acceptance rows.\\n78: 2. Run the three-lane `SOL HIGH build` wave concurrently, with no more than three subagents.\\n79: 3. Wait for all builder reports and changed paths; do not integrate or declare a result while a report is missing.\\n80: 4. Run independent `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` gates only after that wait. They may run concurrently when their scopes are independent, but docs must not fill a missing QA result with an implementation claim.\\n81: 5. The coordinator alone integrates changes, updates status/evidence, and performs git operations. It does not implement, perform QA, or write roadmap prose.\\n82: 6. On any failure, skip, unavailable provider, stale-data condition, accessibility finding, restore failure, secret-review failure, connectivity loss, or missing artifact, keep the task `Pending`, `In progress`, or `Blocked`; create `R-M##-<n>`, repair the root cause, and rerun the failed and affected checks.\\n83: 7. Follow the canonical sequence exactly: `R-M00-1` -> `EXP-M00` -> `M01`/`EXP-M01` -> ... -> `M06`/`EXP-M06` -> `M07` QA/docs -> `ASTRA-FINAL` -> repairs/retests until `Accepted` -> `EXP-M07` -> `EXP-FINAL`. The final gate is allowed only after Astra acceptance and all repair retests.\\n84: \\n85: ### Versioned session-export gates\\n86: \\n87: Every milestone has a separately recorded export task ID: `EXP-M00`, `EXP-M01`, `EXP-M02`, `EXP-M03`, `EXP-M04`, `EXP-M05`, `EXP-M06`, or `EXP-M07`. The coordinator uses OpenCode `/export`, or a verified CLI equivalent, to overwrite exactly one tracked root artifact, `SESSION-EXPORT.md`. The export must be a full-session record containing tool calls and subagent outputs; a summary, partial transcript, or untracked local file does not satisfy the gate.\\n88: \\n89: Before commit, the export receives a documented full secret review. Commit and push the reviewed export as checkpoint SHA X; only then record external CI that explicitly tests SHA X. Preserve that CI receipt, plus the export and secret-review fields, in the next checkpoint/export; never claim SHA X contains a future CI result. The record names the export revision/commit, pushed branch, remote verification, CI result, artifact/link, UTC time, environment, and reviewer. Any failed, skipped, unavailable, or connectivity-blocked export, secret review, push, remote check, or CI check is recorded with its result and blocks acceptance. Git history supplies the version for the stable overwritten path; the export task ID supplies milestone identity. `R-M00-1` intentionally does not create, review, commit, or push the export.\\n90: \\n91: ### Independent final Astra gate\\n92: \\n93: After `M07` dependencies and its QA/docs evidence are complete, an independent GPT-6 Astra reviewer executes task `ASTRA-FINAL`. Astra must use an evidence matrix—not implementation claims—to confirm every shipped feature, every API and UI endpoint, every visible click/control, every browser journey on the supported viewports, and every persistence effect. The matrix must name the check, environment, UTC timestamp, commit, result, artifact/link, limitation, and reviewer for each row.\\n94: \\n95: Any missing, failing, skipped, unavailable, or unconfirmed row creates `R-ASTRA-<n>`. The repair goes through the same three-lane build handoff, independent QA/docs gates, and Astra retest. Repeat until the `ASTRA-FINAL` record explicitly says `Accepted`; no final release or `EXP-FINAL` may precede that wording.\\n96: \\n97: ## Product Goal\\n98: \\n99: Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF, confirms its company name and instrument identity, and receives two forecast views:\\n100: \\n101: 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\\n102: 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\\n103: \\n104: Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. The probability contract includes up/down/unchanged direction, `+/-1%`, `+/-3%`, `+/-5%`, and `+/-10%` return thresholds, conditional gain/loss probabilities, and 50%, 80%, and 95% return and price intervals. Every displayed result must identify its company name, symbol, asset type, instrument identity, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\n105: \\n106: This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy. Optional dark mode and news features are not part of the contract; options trading and public hosting are out of scope.\\n107: \\n108: ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\\n109: \\n110: ### API boundary\\n111: \\n112: - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\n113: - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\\n114: - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\\n115: - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\\n116: \\n117: ### Data source and time semantics\\n118: \\n119: - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\\n120: - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\\n121: - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\n122: - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\n123: - Yahoo Finance five-minute history has an approximate 60-day availability limitation. The provider and UI must state that archive limitation and the applicable archive/session semantics; an unavailable or stale interval is evidence to record, not a reason to fabricate a result.\\n124: \\n125: ### Persistence and auditability\\n126: \\n127: - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\n128: - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\n129: - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\n130: - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\n131: - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\n132: - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\n133: - Reopening a saved forecast must display the immutable recorded inputs/results and must not silently recalculate. A historical cutoff reconstruction is a separately labelled fresh analysis using the data available at that cutoff, with its own as-of time, model/version, and provenance.\\n134: \\n135: ### User experience\\n136: \\n137: - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\n138: - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\n139: - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\n140: - Historical price and return-distribution charts must have equivalent tables/text and remain understandable in every state. The distinctive Signal Ledger direction is intentional: polished tabular numeric hierarchy, clear status evidence, and restrained visual encoding rather than a generic trading dashboard.\\n141: - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\n142: - Accessible names, semantic structure, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and actual assistive-technology/screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish. Axe and keyboard checks do not substitute for an actual screen-reader run.\\n143: \\n144: ### Deployment and resources\\n145: \\n146: - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\n147: - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\n148: - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\n149: - Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for low-resource native x86-64 and ARM64 Linux. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe; the target is below 500 MiB normal server memory, a cached forecast under 1 second, an indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU.\\n150: - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\n151: \\n152: ## Planned Architecture\\n153: \\n154: The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\n155: \\n156: The API/application layers should remain separable:\\n157: \\n158: - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\n159: - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\n160: - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\n161: - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\n162: - **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, dual-architecture, and browser regression checks.\\n163: \\n164: The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\n165: \\n166: ## Forecast Contract\\n167: \\n168: The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\n169: \\n170: - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\n171: - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\n172: - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\n173: - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\n174: - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\n175: - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\n176: - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\n177: \\n178: The evaluation record must use chronological walk-forward splits with no future leakage, compare against a documented baseline, and report Brier score, reliability/calibration, and interval coverage. Rare-event estimates must expose sample counts and uncertainty rather than implying precision from sparse observations. Historical price and return-distribution views must use the same recorded provenance and provide text/table equivalents. A saved result remains a recorded result; a historical-cutoff reconstruction is explicitly a fresh analysis.\\n179: \\n180: The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\\n181: \\n182: ## Restored Acceptance Contract Map\\n183: \\n184: These requirements were omitted from a condensed milestone plan and are restored here as milestone acceptance rows. They are requirements only; none is currently accepted by this documentation repair.\\n185: \\n186: | Contract requirement | Milestone acceptance row |\\n187: | --- | --- |\\n188: | Company-name lookup preserves symbol, exchange, asset type, and other instrument identity; stocks and ETFs follow one explicit identity contract. | `M01` API/schema row and `M03` provider/selection row; `M04` must display the identity without ambiguity. |\\n189: | Saved forecast reopen is immutable recorded output; historical cutoff reconstruction is labelled fresh analysis with separate provenance. | `M02` immutable-record row, `M03` horizon/provenance row, and `M04` saved/reconstruction journey row. |\\n190: | Chronological walk-forward evaluation, baseline comparison, Brier/reliability, interval coverage, and rare-event uncertainty are recorded without leakage. | `M03` forecast-engine/evaluation row and `M07` end-to-end evidence matrix row. |\\n191: | Historical price and return-distribution charts have text/table equivalents and preserve the Signal Ledger visual direction. | `M04` chart/state/accessibility row and `M07` visual gate row. |\\n192: | Direction is explicit up/down/unchanged; thresholds are `+/-1%`, `+/-3%`, `+/-5%`, `+/-10%`; conditional gain/loss and 50/80/95 return and price intervals are defined. | `M03` numerical contract row and `M04` result presentation row. |\\n193: | Yahoo approximate 60-day five-minute limitation and archive/session semantics are visible and auditable. | `M03` provider limitation row and `M07` limitation/release row. |\\n194: | Automatic due and pre-migration backups, retention/disk limits, and no automatic query-history expiry are verified. | `M05` operations/persistence row and `M07` restore/retention row. |\\n195: | Both CSV and JSON export are available, safe, and traceable to immutable records. | `M04` user export row and `M06` security/regression row. |\\n196: | Measured targets: below 500 MiB normal server memory, cached forecast under 1 s, indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, negligible idle CPU. | `M06` resource-gate row on both architectures and `M07` release-resource row. |\\n197: | Native x86-64/amd64 and native ARM64/aarch64 gates cover clean install/package build, `make check`, loopback, Node/Chromium, official MCP interaction, desktop/mobile tests, and resource evidence. A hosted ARM runner does not replace measurement on the original physical low-resource laptop. |\\n198: | Viewports 360/390/768/1280/1440 have polished no-overlap/no-overflow layouts, tabular numeric hierarchy, all states, charts/tables, reduced motion, WCAG AA, keyboard, and actual assistive-technology evidence. | `M04` visual/accessibility row, `M06` browser gate, and `M07` final visual/AT row; axe/keyboard are not screen-reader substitutes. |\\n199: \\n200: Optional dark mode/news are explicitly non-contract; options and public hosting are out of scope.\\n201: \\n202: ## Task Register\\n203: \\n204: The coordinator assigns the exact task ID and no more than three subagents concurrently. Each implementation milestone runs the three-lane build wave, waits for handoff, then runs the independent QA/docs gates. A skipped or unavailable check must be recorded as such and cannot satisfy a required acceptance field.\\n325: \\n326: ## Verification And Repair Loop\\n327: \\n328: 1. The coordinator selects the next pending task only after its dependencies have completed with evidence and assigns the exact task ID.\\n329: 2. Three non-overlapping `SOL HIGH build` lanes work concurrently, then all builders report before integration or verification begins.\\n330: 3. `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` run their independent gates after the build wait; neither masks a missing result.\\n331: 4. The coordinator alone integrates, updates status/evidence, and performs git operations. If any check fails, the task remains pending, in progress, or blocked; create `R-M##-<n>` and repair the root cause rather than weakening the check.\\n332: 5. QA reruns the failed check and affected regression set. Documentation records the new evidence, limitation, exact timestamp/commit, and any skipped or unavailable result.\\n333: 6. The coordinator marks a milestone completed only when every acceptance field, independent QA/docs review, reviewer field, `EXP-M##` export, secret review, push, remote check, and CI result pass.\\n334: 7. After M07, `ASTRA-FINAL` must review the complete feature/API/UI/control/journey/persistence matrix. Any gap creates `R-ASTRA-<n>` and requires repair, QA rerun, Astra retest, and explicit `Accepted` before `EXP-FINAL`.\\n335: \\n336: ## Final Definition Of Done\\n337: \\n338: The MVP is done only when all of the following are true:\\n339: \\n340: - M00 through M07 have explicit statuses and evidence, with no implementation milestone marked complete by assertion alone.\\n341: - A user can select Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs and receive close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close forecasts with clear session/bar semantics.\\n342: - Results contain probabilities and defined magnitude intervals with source, as-of, stale/error, model/version, input, and output provenance.\\n343: - Every submitted successful, failed, and repeated search is retained, history is searchable through `/api/v1`, and forecast inputs/results/outcomes are immutable or append-only as specified.\\n344: - Backup artifacts and restores are verified through integrity, compatibility, representative-data, and non-destructive promotion checks.\\n345: - The frontend uses FastAPI `/api/v1` for all application data and has no direct SQLite access.\\n346: - The dashboard is responsive and accessible, including keyboard, screen-reader, text-equivalent, loading, empty, stale, repeated, and failure behavior.\\n347: - The default deployment is secure loopback, bounded for a low-resource ARM64 laptop, and documented with its limitations.\\n348: - The official headless `@playwright/mcp` supports agent QA, automated browser regressions are checked in, and Git/CI gates fail closed on required regressions.\\n349: - Code comments explain non-obvious behavior, the supported local workflow is documented, and `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` are reconciled with the evidence actually shipped.\\n350: - `ASTRA-FINAL` is independently recorded as `Accepted` after its complete evidence matrix and every `R-ASTRA-<n>` retest.\\n\\n(Output capped at 50 KB.      },\\n824:         {\\n825:           \\\"type\\\": \\\"text\\\",\\n826:           \\\"text\\\": \\\"## What this application does\\\\n\\\\nThis is a small **Python command-line prototype for estimating the probability of stock-price declines**. It combines subjective estimates, historical frequencies, and a normal-distribution model, then prints results as a table.\\\\n\\\\n### The three scripts\\\\n\\\\n| File | Purpose and current state |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| `prob_calc.py` | Calculates example probabilities for PayPal (`PYPL`), then prompts for a custom scenario and weights. |\\\\n| `prob_calc_hardcoded.py` | Currently identical to `prob_calc.py`, including the interactive prompts. |\\\\n| `prob_calc_yf.py` | Intended to fetch Yahoo Finance data for a supplied ticker, defaulting to `SPY`. Currently contains syntax errors and cannot run as written. |\\\\n\\\\n### How the main calculator works\\\\n\\\\nThe two identical scripts blend three inputs:\\\\n\\\\n- A subjective “Burry Gut Score.”\\\\n- A supplied historical frequency.\\\\n- A modeled downside probability calculated as `norm.cdf(-threshold / sd)`.\\\\n\\\\nThe function’s default weights are **60% subjective / 20% historical / 20% modeled**, but the example run first selects weights using a mock backtest.\\\\n\\\\nThe built-in scenarios are:\\\\n- An earnings-day decline greater than 5%.\\\\n- An earnings-day decline greater than 10%.\\\\n- A one-month pullback to $50, represented by a fixed 27.5% decline.\\\\n\\\\nThese inputs are hardcoded; these scripts do not retrieve market data.\\\\n\\\\n### What the Yahoo Finance version intends to do\\\\n\\\\n`prob_calc_yf.py` is written to:\\\\n1. Download 10 years of daily prices.\\\\n2. Measure the historical frequency of daily declines exceeding 5%.\\\\n3. Estimate volatility from the latest 252 daily returns.\\\\n4. Blend historical frequency and modeled probability with **70% / 30% weights**.\\\\n\\\\nIts output calls the modeled component “Market IV Expectation,” but the calculation uses **realized historical volatility**, not options-implied volatility.\\\\n\\\\n## Important findings\\\\n\\\\n- **The backtest is explicitly a mock.** It uses five dummy returns... It is a sequencing rule, not permission to infer that an existing source file works.\\n \\n ### Safe build-wave ownership\\n \\n Use exactly three concurrent `SOL HIGH build` instances in each implementation or repair wave, never more than three. The coordinator records this lane manifest against the exact milestone or repair ID before work starts; the lanes cover every implementation, configuration, and test path:\\n \\n | Lane | Sole build ownership | Handoff boundary |\\n | --- | --- | --- |\\n | `SOL HIGH-A` | Transport/application: FastAPI routes, schemas, configuration, CLI, package/launch assumptions, and transport-facing tests | Versioned API contract and launch assumptions |\\n | `SOL HIGH-B` | Domain/provider/persistence: forecast semantics, Yahoo/fixture adapters, service, SQLite migrations/repositories, backup/restore, and domain/storage tests | Domain and storage contracts, fixtures, and migration assumptions |\\n-| `SOL HIGH-C` | Presentation/browser/operations: static UI, browser harness, operational scripts, Make/CI/tool configuration, dependency/runtime tooling, and presentation/operations tests | UI states, browser journeys, resource limits, and operational assumptions |\\n+| `SOL HIGH-C` | Presentation/browser/operations: static UI, browser harness, operational scripts, Make/local-gate tooling, dependency/runtime tooling, and presentation/operations tests | UI states, browser journeys, resource limits, and operational assumptions |\\n \\n No two builders edit the same path or silently cross a lane boundary. `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `MVP-PLAN.md`, and `MVP-ROADMAP.md` are documentation-owned; `SESSION-EXPORT.md` is export-owned. Any implementation/config/test path not named in the lane manifest is assigned to A, B, or C before work starts. Builders report the exact task ID, changed paths, checks attempted, failures, and unresolved assumptions. If a dependency requires a shared edit, builders stop and hand it to the coordinator for mechanical integration; the coordinator does not author shared implementation/config/test content. The build wave is complete only after all three builder reports arrive.\\n \\n ### Ordered gates\\n \\n 1. Assign the exact `M##` or repair ID and record verified dependencies, lane ownership, and acceptance rows.\\n 2. Run the three-lane `SOL HIGH build` wave concurrently, with no more than three subagents.\\n 3. They may prepare concurrently when their scopes are independent, but docs finalizes only after consuming the completed QA record and must not fill a missing QA result with an implementation claim.\\n 5. The coordinator alone integrates changes, updates status/evidence, and performs git operations. It does not implement, perform QA, or write roadmap prose.\\n 6. On any failure, skip, unavailable provider, stale-data condition, accessibility finding, restore failure, secret-review failure, connectivity loss, or missing artifact, keep the task `Pending`, `In progress`, or `Blocked`; create `R-M##-<n>`, repair the root cause, and rerun the failed and affected checks.\\n-7. Repeat until the `ASTRA-FINAL` record explicitly says `Accepted`; no final release or `EXP-FINAL` may precede that wording.\\n \\n ## Product Goal\\n \\n Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF, confirms its company name and instrument identity, and receives two forecast views:\\n \\n 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\\n 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\\n \\n Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. The probability contract includes up/down/unchanged direction, `+/-1%`, `+/-3%`, `+/-5%`, and `+/-10%` return thresholds, conditional gain/loss probabilities, and 50%, 80%, and 95% return and price intervals. Every displayed result must identify its company name, symbol, asset type, instrument identity, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\n \\n This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy. Optional dark mode and news features are not part of the contract; options trading and public hosting are out of scope.\\n \\n ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\\n \\n ### API boundary\\n \\n - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\n - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\\n - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\\n - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\\n \\n ### Data source and time semantics\\n \\n - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\\n - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\\n - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\n - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\n - Yahoo Finance five-minute history has an approximate 60-day availability limitation. The provider and UI must state that archive limitation and the applicable archive/session semantics; an unavailable or stale interval is evidence to record, not a reason to fabricate a result.\\n \\n ### Persistence and auditability\\n \\n - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\n - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\n - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\n - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\n - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\n - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\n - Reopening a saved forecast must display the immutable recorded inputs/results and must not silently recalculate. A historical cutoff reconstruction is a separately labelled fresh analysis using the data available at that cutoff, with its own as-of time, model/version, and provenance.\\n \\n ### User experience\\n \\n - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\n - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\n - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\n - Historical price and return-distribution charts must have equivalent tables/text and remain understandable in every state. The distinctive Signal Ledger direction is intentional: polished tabular numeric hierarchy, clear status evidence, and restrained visual encoding rather than a generic trading dashboard.\\n - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\n - Accessible names, semantic structure, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and actual assistive-technology/screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish. Axe and keyboard checks do not substitute for an actual screen-reader run.\\n \\n ### Deployment and resources\\n \\n - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\n - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\n - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\n-- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for low-resource native x86-64 and ARM64 Linux. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe; the target is below 500 MiB normal server memory, a cached forecast under 1 second, an indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU.\\n+- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for low-resource Linux x86-64 and ARM64. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe; the target is below 500 MiB normal server memory, a cached forecast under 1 second, an indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU. Native x86-64 measurements are native evidence; ARM64 performance is measured only on local native ARM64 hardware. Emulation can verify packaging/runtime portability and functional/build/tool behavior, but cannot prove physical ARM64 performance.\\n - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\n \\n ## Planned Architecture\\n \\n The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\n \\n The API/application layers should remain separable:\\n \\n - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\n - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\n - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\n - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\n - **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, dual-architecture, and browser regression checks.\\n \\n The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\n \\n ## Forecast Contract\\n \\n The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\n \\n - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\n - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\n - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\n - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\n - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\n - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\n - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\n \\n The evaluation record must use chronological walk-forward splits with no future leakage, compare against a documented baseline, and report Brier score, reliability/calibration, and interval coverage. Rare-event estimates must expose sample counts and uncertainty rather than implying precision from sparse observations. Historical price and return-distribution views must use the same recorded provenance and provide text/table equivalents. A saved result remains a recorded result; a historical-cutoff reconstruction is explicitly a fresh analysis.\\n \\n The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\\n \\n ## Restored Acceptance Contract Map\\n \\n These requirements were omitted from a condensed milestone plan and are restored here as milestone acceptance rows. After M08 QA/docs and Astra review, repair and retest all gaps until the Astra result is `Accepted`; then `EXP-M08` records the reviewed walkthrough/export revision and local Git checkpoint before `EXP-FINAL`.\\n+\\n ## Evidence Record Format\\n \\n Every implementation task must maintain these fields in its task record or linked review:\\n \\n-- **Task ID:** the exact `M##`, `R-M##-<n>`, `EXP-M##`, `ASTRA-FINAL`, `R-ASTRA-<n>`, or `EXP-FINAL` identifier; do not replace it with a generic phase name.\\n+- **Task ID:** the exact `M00`–`M08`, `R-M##-<n>`, `EXP-M00`–`EXP-M08`, `ASTRA-FINAL`, `R-ASTRA-<n>`, or `EXP-FINAL` identifier; do not replace it with a generic phase name.\\n - **Status:** exactly `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`.\\n-- **Owner/phase:** builder lane, QA gate, docs gate, Astra review, export, or remote verification owner.\\n+- **Owner/phase:** builder lane, QA gate, docs gate, Astra review, export, or Git remote verification owner.\\n - **Dependencies verified:** completed task IDs plus the evidence references that prove each dependency.\\n - **Change summary:** what changed and what did not change.\\n - **Acceptance evidence:** one row per acceptance requirement, each with an evidence ID, command/check, environment, UTC timestamp, commit, result (`Pass`, `Fail`, `Skipped`, or `Unavailable`), artifact/link, and named reviewer.\\n - **Verification result:** independent check name and exact result; a test file, source inspection, generated report, or implementation claim is not a pass by itself.\\n - **Repair history:** every failure, skip, unavailable provider, stale-data condition, accessibility finding, restore failure, secret-review failure, or connectivity loss; include repair ID, root cause, fix, and rerun result. Use `None` only when no repair was needed.\\n - **Limitations:** provider, environment, resource, data freshness, coverage, or artifact limitations that remain.\\n-- **Export/remote record:** export task ID, stable `SESSION-EXPORT.md` revision, full-session artifact, secret-review result, checkpoint commit, pushed branch, remote verification, CI result tied to the tested checkpoint SHA, and the next-checkpoint receipt that preserves that result.\\n+- **Export/Git record:** export task ID, stable `SESSION-EXPORT.md` revision, full-session artifact, secret-review result, checkpoint commit, pushed branch, exact Git remote revision verification, and the next-checkpoint receipt that preserves that result. There is no external-pipeline field.\\n - **Reviewer:** the named independent verifying agent, and for final release the independent GPT-6 Astra reviewer.\\n \\n Evidence is not a prose promise. No replacement IDs are invented here; the coordinator must disambiguate the repair register before acceptance. A check-level `Pass` above never overrides a cancelled retest, missing reviewer/gate field, failed check, or unavailable release evidence.\\\\n+\\\\n ## Mandatory Delivery Workflow\\\\n \\\\n The coordinator applies this workflow to every milestone and repair. It is a sequencing rule, not permission to infer that an existing source file works.\\\\n \\\\n ### Safe build-wave ownership\\\\n \\\\n Use no more than three concurrent subagents. A build wave uses three `SOL HIGH build` instances with these declared, non-overlapping lanes; the coordinator records the lane manifest against the exact milestone or repair ID before work starts:\\\\n \\\\n | Lane | Sole build ownership | Handoff boundary |\\\\n | --- | --- | --- |\\\\n | `SOL HIGH-A` | Transport/application: FastAPI routes, schemas, configuration, CLI, and their implementation-facing tests | Versioned API contract and launch assumptions |\\\\n | `SOL HIGH-B` | Domain/provider/persistence: forecast semantics, Yahoo/fixture adapters, service, SQLite migrations/repositories, backup/restore, and their implementation-facing tests | Domain and storage contracts, fixtures, and migration assumptions |\\\\n | `SOL HIGH-C` | Presentation/browser/operations: static UI, browser harness, operational scripts, Make/CI/tool configuration, and their implementation-facing tests | UI states, browser journeys, resource limits, and operational assumptions |\\\\n \\\\n No two builders edit the same path or silently cross a lane boundary. Builders report the exact task ID, changed paths, checks attempted, failures, and unresolved assumptions. If a dependency requires a shared edit, builders stop and hand it to the coordinator for integration rather than overlapping. The build wave is complete only after all three builder reports arrive.\\\\n \\\\n ### Ordered gates\\\\n \\\\n 1. Assign the exact `M##` or repair ID and record verified dependencies, lane ownership, and acceptance rows.\\\\n 2. Run the three-lane `SOL HIGH build` wave concurrently, with no more than three subagents.\\\\n 3. Wait for all builder reports and changed paths; do not integrate or declare a result while a report is missing.\\\\n 4. Run independent `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` gates only after that wait. They may run concurrently when their scopes are independent, but docs must not fill a missing QA result with an implementation claim.\\\\n 5. The coordinator alone integrates changes, updates status/evidence, and performs git operations. It does not implement, perform QA, or write roadmap prose.\\\\n 6. On any failure, skip, unavailable provider, stale-data condition, accessibility finding, restore failure, secret-review failure, connectivity loss, or missing artifact, keep the task `Pending`, `In progress`, or `Blocked`; create `R-M##-<n>`, repair the root cause, and rerun the failed and affected checks.\\\\n 7. After each accepted roadmap milestone, complete its export gate (`EXP-M00` through `EXP-M07`) before starting the next milestone. The final gate is `EXP-FINAL` and is allowed only after `ASTRA-FINAL` is `Accepted` and all Astra repairs have passed retest.\\\\n \\\\n ### Versioned session-export gates\\\\n \\\\n Every milestone has a separately recorded export task ID: `EXP-M00`, `EXP-M01`, `EXP-M02`, `EXP-M03`, `EXP-M04`, `EXP-M05`, `EXP-M06`, or `EXP-M07`. The coordinator uses OpenCode `/export`, or a verified CLI equivalent, to overwrite exactly one tracked root artifact, `SESSION-EXPORT.md`. The export must be a full-session record containing tool calls and subagent outputs; a summary, partial transcript, or untracked local file does not satisfy the gate.\\\\n \\\\n Before commit, the export receives a documented secret review. The record then names the export revision/commit, commit, pushed branch, remote verification, and CI result. Any failed, skipped, unavailable, or connectivity-blocked export, secret review, push, remote check, or CI check is recorded with its result and blocks acceptance. Git history supplies the version for the stable overwritten path; the export task ID supplies milestone identity. This task intentionally does not create the export, commit, or push it.\\\\n \\\\n ### Independent final Astra gate\\\\n \\\\n After `M07` dependencies and its QA/docs evidence are complete, an independent GPT-6 Astra reviewer executes task `ASTRA-FINAL`. Astra must use an evidence matrix—not implementation claims—to confirm every shipped feature, every API and UI endpoint, every visible click/control, every browser journey on the supported viewports, and every persistence effect. The matrix must name the check, environment, UTC timestamp, commit, result, artifact/link, limitation, and reviewer for each row.\\\\n \\\\n Any missing, failing, skipped, unavailable, or unconfirmed row creates `R-ASTRA-<n>`. The repair goes through the same three-lane build handoff, independent QA/docs gates, and Astra retest. Repeat until the `ASTRA-FINAL` record explicitly says `Accepted`; no final release or `EXP-FINAL` may precede that wording.\\\\n \\\\n ## Product Goal\\\\n \\\\n Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF and receives two forecast views:\\\\n \\\\n 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\\\\n 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\\\\n \\\\n Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. Every displayed result must identify its symbol, asset type, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\\\n \\\\n This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\\\\n \\\\n ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\\\\n \\\\n ### API boundary\\\\n \\\\n - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\\\n - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\\\\n - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\\\\n - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\\\\n \\\\n ### Data source and time semantics\\\\n \\\\n - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\\\\n - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\\\\n - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\\\n - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\\\n \\\\n ### Persistence and auditability\\\\n \\\\n - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\\\n - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\\\n - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\\\n - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\\\n - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\\\n - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\\\n \\\\n ### User experience\\\\n \\\\n - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\\\n - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\\\n - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\\\n - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\\\n - Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\\\\n \\\\n ### Deployment and resources\\\\n \\\\n - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\\\n - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\\\n - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\\\n - Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\\\\n - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\\\n \\\\n ## Planned Architecture\\\\n \\\\n The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\\\n \\\\n The API/application layers should remain separable:\\\\n \\\\n - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\\\n - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\\\n - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\\\n - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\\\n - **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\\\\n \\\\n The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\\\n \\\\n ## Forecast Contract\\\\n \\\\n The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\\\n \\\\n - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\\\n - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\\\n - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\\\n - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\\\n - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\\\n - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\\\n - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\\\n \\\\n The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\\\\n \\\\n ## Task Register\\\\n \\\\n The coordinator assigns the exact task ID and no more than three subagents concurrently. Each implementation milestone runs the three-lane build wave, waits for handoff, then runs the independent QA/docs gates. The listed acceptance evidence is required before status can become **Completed**, and the matching `EXP-M##` gate is required before the milestone is released onward.\\\\n \\\\n ### M00 - Documentation Baseline\\\\n \\\\n - **Status:** Completed, docs only.\\\\n - **Dependencies:** None.\\\\n - **Agents:** `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n - **Scope:** Create the plan, roadmap, compact agent rules, and honest repository README.\\\\n - **Acceptance evidence:** [x] `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md` exist; [x] current prototype is distinguished from planned implementation; [x] no implementation milestone is presented as completed without its evidence.\\\\n - **Verification:** [x] documentation-only diff reviewed; [x] required product invariants, orchestration, evidence fields, repair loop, and final definition of done are present.\\\\n - **Repair record:** None at baseline creation.\\\\n-- **Post-milestone gate:** `EXP-M00` must overwrite and review `SESSION-EXPORT.md`, then record commit/push/remote/CI evidence. No such export or release operation is claimed by this task.\\\\n+- **Post-milestone gate:** `EXP-M00` must overwrite and review `SESSION-EXPORT.md`, then record commit/push/remote/CI evidence. It must demonstrate:\\\\n \\\\n - A close-to-close forecast based on a clearly recorded completed-session close and applicable next close.\\\\n - A latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close forecast that excludes an in-progress bar and states its session rule.\\\\n - Direction/threshold probabilities and explicit magnitude intervals with definitions, levels, units, as-of time, model/version, and data-quality state.\\\\n - Source, market-session, stale-data, error, limitation, and immutable input/result provenance.\\\\n - Searchable history containing every submitted successful, failed, and repeated search.\\\\n - Append-only observed outcomes that never rewrite the original forecast.\\\\n - Verified, non-destructive backup/restore and secure loopback defaults suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop.\\\\n \\\\n The boundary is strict: browser application data must use FastAPI `/api/v1`; the browser must not open SQLite, issue SQL, receive a database path, or call Yahoo Finance directly. The dashboard must be responsive and accessible, with text equivalents for visual data and understandable empty, loading, success, repeated, stale, validation, and failure states.\\\\n \\\\n These are acceptance requirements, not a promise that the current working tree satisfies them. Forecasts are informational research outputs, not investment advice or a guarantee of future prices.\\\\n \\\\n ## Required Future Workflow\\\\n \\\\n All future work maximizes safe parallelism with no more than three concurrent subagents. Each build wave uses three `SOL HIGH build` instances on non-overlapping lanes: transport/application, domain/provider/persistence, and presentation/browser/operations. Builders declare paths and exact task IDs, finish, and report before integration.\\\\n \\\\n Only after all builder reports arrive do the independent `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` gates run. The coordinator owns integration, status, and git only; it does not implement, perform QA, or write roadmap prose. Failures, skips, unavailable providers, stale data, accessibility findings, restore failures, secret-review failures, and connectivity loss remain visible and create `R-M##-<n>` repairs with rerun evidence.\\\\n \\\\n `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` are roadmap deliverables. Reconcile both after each milestone and again during final acceptance; neither may claim more than the evidence supports.\\\\n \\\\n ## Export And Release Gates\\\\n \\\\n After every roadmap milestone, complete its exact export task: `EXP-M00` through `EXP-M07`. OpenCode `/export` (or a verified CLI equivalent) must overwrite the one tracked root artifact `SESSION-EXPORT.md` with the full session, including tool calls and subagent outputs. Review the entire export for secrets before commit; never commit an unreviewed export.\\\\n \\\\n Record the export revision, secret-review result, commit, pushed branch, remote verification, CI result, artifact/link, UTC timestamp, environment, and named reviewer. A failed, skipped, unavailable, or connectivity-blocked export, review, push, remote check, or CI check blocks acceptance and must not be summarized as green. Git commit/revision versions the stable overwritten export path and provides a recoverable checkpoint so work can resume after connectivity loss.\\\\n \\\\n After M07, independent GPT-6 Astra executes `ASTRA-FINAL`. Astra must confirm every feature, API/UI endpoint, click/control, browser journey, and persistence effect in an evidence matrix. Any gap creates `R-ASTRA-<n>`; repair, QA, and Astra retest repeat until the independent record says `Accepted`. Only then may `EXP-FINAL` complete the final export/commit/push/remote/CI gate.\\\\n \\\\n ## Evidence Record Minimum\\\\n \\\\n Every record uses an exact task ID (`M##`, `R-M##-<n>`, `EXP-M##`, `ASTRA-FINAL`, `R-ASTRA-<n>`, or `EXP-FINAL`) and includes:\\\\n \\\\n - status: `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`;\\\\n - owner/phase, verified dependency IDs, and change summary;\\\\n - one evidence row per acceptance requirement with check/command, environment, UTC timestamp, commit, result (`Pass`, `Fail`, `Skipped`, or `Unavailable`), artifact/link, and reviewer;\\\\n - repair history, limitations, export ID/revision, secret review, commit/push, remote/CI result, and named reviewer.\\\\n \\\\n Missing evidence is not a pass. The detailed acceptance contract and task register are in `MVP-PLAN.md`; dependency order, gate status, Astra matrix, and export rules are in `MVP-ROADMAP.md`; compact operating rules are in `AGENTS.md`.\\\\n \\\\n ## Local Development Guidance\\\\n \\\\n The `Makefile` and pinned manifests describe setup, deterministic checks, browser checks, MCP smoke, backup, restore, and release-check entry points. Treat them as candidate operational paths until the corresponding task and environment evidence is recorded. Do not use `burry_env/` as a source of truth; it is tracked legacy dependency noise. `.venv/` and other local environments are local state, not dependency declarations or release evidence.\\\\n\\\",\\n+              \\\"additions\\\": 13,\\n+              \\\"deletions\\\": 2,\\n+              \\\"status\\\": \\\"modified\\\"\\n+            }\\n+          ]\\n         },\\n-        \\\"id\\\": \\\"msg_08c4689e6001QvHx6aOg5L0Vvl\\\",\\n-        \\\"sessionID\\\": \\\"ses_f73b976e8ffekNCE6SNIanpXFb\\\"\\n+        \\\"id\\\": \\\"msg_08e153d39001r2YtjT5MzSvArg\\\",\\n+        \\\"sessionID\\\": \\\"ses_f71ec0499ffeokWj4h6tVwyYk1\\\"\\n       },\\n       \\\"parts\\\": [\\n         {\\n           \\\"type\\\": \\\"text\\\",\\n-          \\\"text\\\": \\\"Create or update `AGENTS.md` for this repository.\\\\n\\\\nThe goal is a compact instruction file that helps future OpenCode sessions avoid mistakes and ramp up quickly. Every line should answer: \\\\\\\"Would an agent likely miss this without help?\\\\\\\" If not, leave it out.\\\\n\\\\nUser-provided focus or constraints (honor these):\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## How to investigate\\\\n\\\\nRead the highest-value sources first:\\\\n- `README*`, root manifests, workspace config, lockfiles\\\\n- build, test, lint, formatter, typecheck, and codegen config\\\\n- CI workflows and pre-commit / task runner config\\\\n- existing instruction files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules/`, `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`)\\\\n- repo-local OpenCode config such as `opencode.json`\\\\n\\\\nIf architecture is still unclear after reading config and docs, inspect a small number of representative code files to find the real entrypoints, package boundaries, and execution flow. If docs conflict with config or scripts, trust the executable source and only keep what you can verify.\\\\n\\\\n## What to extract\\\\n\\\\nLook for the highest-signal facts for an agent working in this repo:\\\\n- exact developer commands, especially non-obvious ones\\\\n- how to run a single test, a single package, or a focused verification step\\\\n- required command order when it matters, such as `lint -> typecheck -> test`\\\\n- monorepo or multi-package boundaries, ownership of major directories, and the real app/library entrypoints\\\\n- framework or toolchain quirks: generated code, migrations, codegen, build artifacts, special env loading, dev servers, infra deploy flow\\\\n- repo-specific style or workflow conventions that differ from defaults\\\\n- testing quirks: fixtures, integration test prerequisites, snapshot workflows, required services, flaky or expensive suites\\\\n- important constraints from existing instruction files worth preserving\\\\n\\\\nGood `AGENTS.md` content is usually hard-earned context that took reading multiple files to infer.\\\\n\\\\n## Questions\\\\n\\\\nOnly ask the user questions if the repo cannot answer something important. Use the `question` tool for one short batch at most.\\\\n\\\\nGood questions:\\\\n- undocumented team conventions\\\\n- branch / PR / release expectations\\\\n- missing setup or test prerequisites that are known but not written down\\\\n\\\\nDo not ask about anything the repo already makes clear.\\\\n\\\\n## Writing rules\\\\n\\\\nInclude only high-signal, repo-specific guidance such as:\\\\n- exact commands and shortcuts the agent would otherwise guess wrong\\\\n- architecture notes that are not obvious from filenames\\\\n- conventions that differ from language or framework defaults\\\\n- setup requirements, environment quirks, and operational gotchas\\\\n- references to existing instruction sources that matter\\\\n\\\\nExclude:\\\\n- generic software advice\\\\n- long tutorials or exhaustive file trees\\\\n- obvious language conventions\\\\n- speculative claims or anything you could not verify\\\\n- content better stored in another file referenced via `opencode.json` `instructions`\\\\n\\\\nWhen in doubt, omit.\\\\n\\\\nPrefer short sections and bullets. If the repo is simple, keep the file simple. If the repo is large, summarize the few structural facts that actually change how an agent should work.\\\\n\\\\nIf `AGENTS.md` already exists at `/home/eddie/stock_probs`, improve it in place rather than rewriting blindly.
