Name to your liking, use `command` type with the command `npx @playwright/mcp@latest`. You can also verify config or add command like arguments via clicking `Edit`.\\\\n\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>Factory</summary>\\\\n\\\\nUse the Factory CLI to add the Playwright MCP server:\\\\n\\\\n```bash\\\\ndroid mcp add playwright \\\\\\\"npx @playwright/mcp@latest\\\\\\\"\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nAlternatively, type `/mcp` within Factory droid to open an interactive UI for managing MCP servers.\\\\n\\\\nFor more information, see the [Factory MCP documentation](https://docs.factory.ai/cli/configuration/mcp).\\\\n\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>Gemini CLI</summary>\\\\n\\\\nFollow the MCP install [guide](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/tools/mcp-server.md#configure-the-mcp-server-in-settingsjson), use the standard config above.\\\\n\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>Goose</summary>\\\\n\\\\n#### Click the button to install:\\\\n\\\\n[![Install in Goose](https://block.github.io/goose/img/extension-install-dark.svg)](https://block.github.io/goose/extension?cmd=npx&arg=%40playwright%2Fmcp%40latest&id=playwright&name=Playwright&description=Interact%20with%20web%20pages%20through%20structured%20accessibility%20snapshots%20using%20Playwright)\\\\n\\\\n#### Or install manually:\\\\n\\\\nGo to `Advanced settings` -> `Extensions` -> `Add custom extension`. Name to your liking, use type `STDIO`, and set the `command` to `npx @playwright/mcp`. Click \\\\\\\"Add Extension\\\\\\\".\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>Grok</summary>\\\\n\\\\nUse the Grok CLI to add the Playwright MCP server:\\\\n\\\\n```bash\\\\ngrok mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nAlternatively, create or edit the configuration file `~/.grok/config.toml` and add:\\\\n\\\\n```toml\\\\n[mcp_servers.playwright]\\\\ncommand = \\\\\\\"npx\\\\\\\"\\\\nargs = [\\\\\\\"@playwright/mcp@latest\\\\\\\"]\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nFor more information, see the [Grok MCP documentation](https://docs.x.ai/build/features/mcp-servers).\\\\n\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>Junie</summary>\\\\n\\\\nTo add the Playwright MCP server in Junie CLI:\\\\n\\\\n1. Type `/mcp`\\\\n2. Press `Ctrl+A` to add a new MCP server\\\\n3. Select **Playwright** from the list\\\\n\\\\nAlternatively, add to `.junie/mcp/mcp.json`:\\\\n\\\\n```json\\\\n{\\\\n  \\\\\\\"mcpServers\\\\\\\": {\\\\n    \\\\\\\"Playwright\\\\\\\": {\\\\n      \\\\\\\"command\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"npx\\\\\\\",\\\\n      \\\\\\\"args\\\\\\\": [\\\\n        \\\\\\\"-y\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"@playwright/mcp@latest\\\\\\\"\\\\n      ]\\\\n    }\\\\n  }\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nFor more information, see the [Junie MCP configuration documentation](https://junie.jetbrains.com/docs/junie-cli-mcp-configuration.html).\\\\n\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>Kiro</summary>\\\\n\\\\n[![Add to Kiro](https://kiro.dev/images/add-to-kiro.svg)](https://kiro.dev/launch/mcp/add?name=playwright&config=%7B%22command%22%3A%22npx%22%2C%22args%22%3A%5B%22%40playwright%2Fmcp%40latest%22%5D%7D)\\\\n\\\\nFollow the MCP Servers [documentation](https://kiro.dev/docs/mcp/). For example in `.kiro/settings/mcp.json`:\\\\n\\\\n```json\\\\n{\\\\n  \\\\\\\"mcpServers\\\\\\\": {\\\\n    \\\\\\\"playwright\\\\\\\": {\\\\n      \\\\\\\"command\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"npx\\\\\\\",\\\\n      \\\\\\\"args\\\\\\\": [\\\\n        \\\\\\\"@playwright/mcp@latest\\\\\\\"\\\\n      ]\\\\n    }\\\\n  }\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>LM Studio</summary>\\\\n\\\\n#### Click the button to install:\\\\n\\\\n[![Add MCP Server playwright to LM Studio](https://files.lmstudio.ai/deeplink/mcp-install-light.svg)](https://lmstudio.ai/install-mcp?name=playwright&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoibnB4IiwiYXJncyI6WyJAcGxheXdyaWdodC9tY3BAbGF0ZXN0Il19)\\\\n\\\\n#### Or install manually:\\\\n\\\\nGo to `Program` in the right sidebar -> `Install` -> `Edit mcp.json`. Use the standard config above.\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>opencode</summary>\\\\n\\\\nFollow the MCP Servers [documentation](https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/). For example in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:\\\\n\\\\n```json\\\\n{\\\\n  \\\\\\\"$schema\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"https://opencode.ai/config.json\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"mcp\\\\\\\": {\\\\n    \\\\\\\"playwright\\\\\\\": {\\\\n      \\\\\\\"type\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"local\\\\\\\",\\\\n      \\\\\\\"command\\\\\\\": [\\\\n        \\\\\\\"npx\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"@playwright/mcp@latest\\\\\\\"\\\\n      ],\\\\n      \\\\\\\"enabled\\\\\\\": true\\\\n    }\\\\n  }\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>Qodo Gen</summary>\\\\n\\\\nOpen [Qodo Gen](https://docs.qodo.ai/qodo-documentation/qodo-gen) chat panel in VSCode or IntelliJ → Connect more tools → + Add new MCP → Paste the standard config above.\\\\n\\\\nClick <code>Save</code>.\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>VS Code</summary>\\\\n\\\\n#### Click the button to install:\\\\n\\\\n[<img src=\\\\\\\"https://img.shields.io/badge/VS_Code-VS_Code?style=flat-square&label=Install%20Server&color=0098FF\\\\\\\" alt=\\\\\\\"Install in VS Code\\\\\\\">](https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect?url=vscode%3Amcp%2Finstall%3F%257B%2522name%2522%253A%2522playwright%2522%252C%2522command%2522%253A%2522npx%2522%252C%2522args%2522%253A%255B%2522%2540playwright%252Fmcp%2540latest%2522%255D%257D) [<img alt=\\\\\\\"Install in VS Code Insiders\\\\\\\" src=\\\\\\\"https://img.shields.io/badge/VS_Code_Insiders-VS_Code_Insiders?style=flat-square&label=Install%20Server&color=24bfa5\\\\\\\">](https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect?url=vscode-insiders%3Amcp%2Finstall%3F%257B%2522name%2522%253A%2522playwright%2522%252C%2522command%2522%253A%2522npx%2522%252C%2522args%2522%253A%255B%2522%2540playwright%252Fmcp%2540latest%2522%255D%257D)\\\\n\\\\n#### Or install manually:\\\\n\\\\nFollow the MCP install [guide](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/chat/mcp-servers#_add-an-mcp-server), use the standard config above. You can also install the Playwright MCP server using the VS Code CLI:\\\\n\\\\n```bash\\\\n# For VS Code\\\\ncode --add-mcp '{\\\\\\\"name\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"playwright\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"command\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"npx\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"args\\\\\\\":[\\\\\\\"@playwright/mcp@latest\\\\\\\"]}'\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nAfter installation, the Playwright MCP server will be available for use with your GitHub Copilot agent in VS Code.\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>Warp</summary>\\\\n\\\\nGo to `Settings` -> `AI` -> `Manage MCP Servers` -> `+ Add` to [add an MCP Server](https://docs.warp.dev/knowledge-and-collaboration/mcp#adding-an-mcp-server). Use the standard config above.\\\\n\\\\nAlternatively, use the slash command `/add-mcp` in the Warp prompt and paste the standard config from above:\\\\n```js\\\\n{\\\\n  \\\\\\\"mcpServers\\\\\\\": {\\\\n    \\\\\\\"playwright\\\\\\\": {\\\\n      \\\\\\\"command\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"npx\\\\\\\",\\\\n      \\\\\\\"args\\\\\\\": [\\\\n        \\\\\\\"@playwright/mcp@latest\\\\\\\"\\\\n      ]\\\\n    }\\\\n  }\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>Windsurf</summary>\\\\n\\\\nFollow Windsurf MCP [documentation](https://docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/mcp). Use the standard config above.\\\\n\\\\n</details>\\\\n\\\\n### Configuration\\\\n\\\\nPlaywright MCP server supports following arguments. They can be provided in the JSON configuration above, as a part of the `\\\\\\\"args\\\\\\\"` list:\\\\n\\\\n<!--- Options generated by update-readme.js -->\\\\n\\\\n| Option | Description |\\\\n|--------|-------------|\\\\n| --allowed-hosts <hosts...> | comma-separated list of hosts this server is allowed to serve from. Defaults to the host the server is bound to. Pass '*' to disable the host check.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` |\\\\n| --allowed-origins <origins> | semicolon-separated list of TRUSTED origins to allow the browser to request. Default is to allow all. Important: *does not* serve as a security boundary and *does not* affect redirects.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` |\\\\n| --allow-unrestricted-file-access | allow access to files outside of the workspace roots. Also allows unrestricted access to file:// URLs. By default access to file system is restricted to workspace root directories (or cwd if no roots are configured) only, and navigation to file:// URLs is blocked.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ALLOW_UNRESTRICTED_FILE_ACCESS` |\\\\n| --blocked-origins <origins> | semicolon-separated list of origins to block the browser from requesting. Blocklist is evaluated before allowlist. If used without the allowlist, requests not matching the blocklist are still allowed. Important: *does not* serve as a security boundary and *does not* affect redirects.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_BLOCKED_ORIGINS` |\\\\n| --block-service-workers | block service workers<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_BLOCK_SERVICE_WORKERS` |\\\\n| --browser <browser> | browser or chrome channel to use, possible values: chrome, firefox, webkit, msedge.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_BROWSER` |\\\\n| --caps <caps> | comma-separated list of additional capabilities to enable, possible values: vision, pdf, devtools.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CAPS` |\\\\n| --cdp-endpoint <endpoint> | CDP endpoint to connect to.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CDP_ENDPOINT` |\\\\n| --cdp-header <headers...> | CDP headers to send with the connect request, multiple can be specified.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CDP_HEADERS` |\\\\n| --cdp-timeout <timeout> | timeout in milliseconds for connecting to CDP endpoint, defaults to 30000ms<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CDP_TIMEOUT` |\\\\n| --codegen <lang> | specify the language to use for code generation, possible values: \\\\\\\"typescript\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"python\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"java\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"csharp\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"none\\\\\\\". Default is \\\\\\\"typescript\\\\\\\".<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CODEGEN` |\\\\n| --config <path> | path to the configuration file.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CONFIG` |\\\\n| --console-level <level> | level of console messages to return: \\\\\\\"error\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"warning\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"info\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"debug\\\\\\\". Each level includes the messages of more severe levels.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CONSOLE_LEVEL` |\\\\n| --device <device> | device to emulate, for example: \\\\\\\"iPhone 15\\\\\\\"<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_DEVICE` |\\\\n| --mobile | emulate a generic mobile device (Pixel 10 for Chromium, iPhone 17 for WebKit). Mobile pages are usually lighter, which saves tokens. Cannot be combined with --device.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_MOBILE` |\\\\n| --executable-path <path> | path to the browser executable.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH` |\\\\n| --extension | Connect to a running browser instance (Edge/Chrome only). Requires the \\\\\\\"Playwright Extension\\\\\\\" to be installed.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXTENSION` |\\\\n| --endpoint <endpoint> | Bound browser endpoint to connect to.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ENDPOINT` |\\\\n| --grant-permissions <permissions...> | List of permissions to grant to the browser context, for example \\\\\\\"geolocation\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"clipboard-read\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"clipboard-write\\\\\\\".<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_GRANT_PERMISSIONS` |\\\\n| --headless | run browser in headless mode, headed by default<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_HEADLESS` |\\\\n| --host <host> | host to bind server to. Default is localhost. Use 0.0.0.0 to bind to all interfaces.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_HOST` |\\\\n| --ignore-https-errors | ignore https errors<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_IGNORE_HTTPS_ERRORS` |\\\\n| --init-page <path...> | path to TypeScript file to evaluate on Playwright page object<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_INIT_PAGE` |\\\\n| --init-script <path...> | path to JavaScript file to add as an initialization script. The script will be evaluated in every page before any of the page's scripts. Can be specified multiple times.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_INIT_SCRIPT` |\\\\n| --isolated | keep the browser profile in memory, do not save it to disk.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_ISOLATED` |\\\\n| --image-responses <mode> | whether to send image responses to the client. Can be \\\\\\\"allow\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\"omit\\\\\\\", Defaults to \\\\\\\"allow\\\\\\\".<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_IMAGE_RESPONSES` |\\\\n| --no-sandbox | disable the sandbox for all process types that are normally sandboxed.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_NO_SANDBOX` |\\\\n| --output-dir <path> | path to the directory for output files.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR` |\\\\n| --output-max-size <bytes> | Threshold for evicting old output files, in bytes.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_OUTPUT_MAX_SIZE` |\\\\n| --port <port> | port to listen on for SSE transport.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PORT` |\\\\n| --proxy-bypass <bypass> | comma-separated domains to bypass proxy, for example \\\\\\\".com,chromium.org,.domain.com\\\\\\\"<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PROXY_BYPASS` |\\\\n| --proxy-server <proxy> | specify proxy server, for example \\\\\\\"http://myproxy:3128\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\"socks5://myproxy:8080\\\\\\\"<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PROXY_SERVER` |\\\\n| --sandbox | enable the sandbox for all process types that are normally not sandboxed.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SANDBOX` |\\\\n| --save-session | Whether to save the Playwright MCP session into the output directory.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SAVE_SESSION` |\\\\n| --secrets <path> | path to a file containing secrets in the dotenv format<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SECRETS_FILE` |\\\\n| --shared-browser-context | reuse the same browser context between all connected HTTP clients.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SHARED_BROWSER_CONTEXT` |\\\\n| --snapshot-boxes | include each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height] in snapshots. Coordinates are viewport-relative, in CSS pixels.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SNAPSHOT_BOXES` |\\\\n| --snapshot-mode <mode> | when taking snapshots for responses, specifies the mode to use. Can be \\\\\\\"full\\\\\\\" or \\\\\\\"none\\\\\\\". Default is \\\\\\\"full\\\\\\\".<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SNAPSHOT_MODE` |\\\\n| --storage-state <path> | path to the storage state file for isolated sessions.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_STORAGE_STATE` |\\\\n| --test-id-attribute <attribute> | specify the attribute to use for test ids, defaults to \\\\\\\"data-testid\\\\\\\"<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TEST_ID_ATTRIBUTE` |\\\\n| --timeout-action <timeout> | specify action timeout in milliseconds, defaults to 5000ms<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TIMEOUT_ACTION` |\\\\n| --timeout-navigation <timeout> | specify navigation timeout in milliseconds, defaults to 60000ms<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TIMEOUT_NAVIGATION` |\\\\n| --timeout-settle <timeout> | how long to wait after each action for triggered work to settle, in milliseconds, defaults to 500ms<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TIMEOUT_SETTLE` |\\\\n| --user-agent <ua string> | specify user agent string<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_USER_AGENT` |\\\\n| --user-data-dir <path> | path to the user data directory. If not specified, a temporary directory will be created.<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_USER_DATA_DIR` |\\\\n| --viewport-size <size> | specify browser viewport size in pixels, for example \\\\\\\"1280x720\\\\\\\"<br>*env* `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VIEWPORT_SIZE` |\\\\n\\\\n<!--- End of options generated section -->\\\\n\\\\n### User profile\\\\n\\\\nYou can run Playwright MCP with persistent profile like a regular browser (default), in isolated contexts for testing sessions, or connect to your existing browser using the browser extension.\\\\n\\\\n**Persistent profile**\\\\n\\\\nAll the logged in information will be stored in the persistent profile, you can delete it between sessions if you'd like to clear the offline state.\\\\nPersistent profile is located at the following locations and you can override it with the `--user-data-dir` argument.\\\\n\\\\n```bash\\\\n# Windows\\\\n%USERPROFILE%\\\\\\\\AppData\\\\\\\\Local\\\\\\\\ms-playwright\\\\\\\\mcp-{channel}-{workspace-hash}\\\\n\\\\n# macOS\\\\n- ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/mcp-{channel}-{workspace-hash}\\\\n\\\\n# Linux\\\\n- ~/.cache/ms-playwright/mcp-{channel}-{workspace-hash}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n`{workspace-hash}` is derived from the MCP client's workspace root, so different projects get separate profiles automatically.\\\\n\\\\n> [!IMPORTANT]\\\\n> A persistent profile can only be used by one browser instance at a time, so concurrent MCP clients sharing the same workspace will conflict. To run several clients in parallel, start each additional client with `--isolated` or point it at a distinct `--user-data-dir`.\\\\n\\\\n**Isolated**\\\\n\\\\nIn the isolated mode, each session is started in the isolated profile. Every time you ask MCP to close the browser,\\\\nthe session is closed and all the storage state for this session is lost. You can provide initial storage state\\\\nto the browser via the config's `contextOptions` or via the `--storage-state` argument. Learn more about the storage\\\\nstate [here](https://playwright.dev/docs/auth).\\\\n\\\\n```js\\\\n{\\\\n  \\\\\\\"mcpServers\\\\\\\": {\\\\n    \\\\\\\"playwright\\\\\\\": {\\\\n      \\\\\\\"command\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"npx\\\\\\\",\\\\n      \\\\\\\"args\\\\\\\": [\\\\n        \\\\\\\"@playwright/mcp@latest\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"--isolated\\\\\\\",\\\\n        \\\\\\\"--storage-state={path/to/storage.json}\\\\\\\"\\\\n      ]\\\\n    }\\\\n  }\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n**Browser Extension**\\\\n\\\\nThe Playwright MCP Chrome Extension allows you to connect to existing browser tabs and leverage your logged-in sessions and browser state. See [microsoft/playwright › packages/extension](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/tree/main/packages/extension#readme) for installation and setup instructions.\\\\n\\\\n### Initial state\\\\n\\\\nThere are multiple ways to provide the initial state to the browser context or a page.\\\\n\\\\nFor the storage state, you can either:\\\\n- Start with a user data directory using the `--user-data-dir` argument. This will persist all browser data between the sessions.\\\\n- Start with a storage state file using the `--storage-state` argument. This will load cookies and local storage from the file into an isolated browser context.\\\\n\\\\nFor the page state, you can use:\\\\n\\\\n- `--init-page` to point to a TypeScript file that will be evaluated on the Playwright page object. This allows you to run arbitrary code to set up the page.\\\\n\\\\n```ts\\\\n// init-page.ts\\\\nexport default async ({ page }) => {\\\\n  await page.context().grantPermissions(['geolocation']);\\\\n  await page.context().setGeolocation({ latitude: 37.7749, longitude: -122.4194 });\\\\n  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1280, height: 720 });\\\\n};\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n- `--init-script` to point to a JavaScript file that will be added as an initialization script. The script will be evaluated in every page before any of the page's scripts.\\\\nThis is useful for overriding browser APIs or setting up the environment.\\\\n\\\\n```js\\\\n// init-script.js\\\\nwindow.isPlaywrightMCP = true;\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Configuration file\\\\n\\\\nThe Playwright MCP server can be configured using a JSON configuration file. You can specify the configuration file\\\\nusing the `--config` command line option:\\\\n\\\\n```bash\\\\nnpx @playwright/mcp@latest --config path/to/config.json\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n<details>\\\\n<summary>Configuration file schema</summary>\\\\n\\\\n<!--- Config generated by update-readme.js -->\\\\n\\\\n```typescript\\\\n{\\\\n  /**\\\\n   * The browser to use.\\\\n   */\\\\n  browser?: {\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * The type of browser to use.\\\\n     */\\\\n    browserName?: 'chromium' | 'firefox' | 'webkit';\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * Keep the browser profile in memory, do not save it to disk.\\\\n     */\\\\n    isolated?: boolean;\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * Path to a user data directory for browser profile persistence.\\\\n     * Temporary directory is created by default.\\\\n     */\\\\n    userDataDir?: string;\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * Launch options passed to\\\\n     * @see https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-launch-persistent-context\\\\n     *\\\\n     * This is useful for settings options like `channel`, `headless`, `executablePath`, etc.\\\\n     */\\\\n    launchOptions?: playwright.LaunchOptions;\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * Context options for the browser context.\\\\n     *\\\\n     * This is useful for settings options like `viewport`.\\\\n     */\\\\n    contextOptions?: playwright.BrowserContextOptions;\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint to connect to an existing browser instance in case of Chromium family browsers.\\\\n     */\\\\n    cdpEndpoint?: string;\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * CDP headers to send with the connect request.\\\\n     */\\\\n    cdpHeaders?: Record<string, string>;\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * Timeout in milliseconds for connecting to CDP endpoint. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds). Pass 0 to disable timeout.\\\\n     */\\\\n    cdpTimeout?: number;\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * Remote endpoint to connect to an existing Playwright server. May be a\\\\n     * WebSocket URL string, or a [ConnectOptions] object that mirrors the\\\\n     * `connectOptions` shape used by the test runner. When passed as an object,\\\\n     * `exposeNetwork`, `headers`, `slowMo`, and `timeout` are forwarded to the\\\\n     * underlying connect call.\\\\n     */\\\\n    remoteEndpoint?: string | playwright.ConnectOptions & { endpoint: string };\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * Paths to TypeScript files to add as initialization scripts for Playwright page.\\\\n     */\\\\n    initPage?: string[];\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * Paths to JavaScript files to add as initialization scripts.\\\\n     * The scripts will be evaluated in every page before any of the page's scripts.\\\\n     */\\\\n    initScript?: string[];\\\\n  },\\\\n\\\\n  /**\\\\n   * Connect to a running browser instance (Edge/Chrome only). If specified, `browser`\\\\n   * config is ignored.\\\\n   * Requires the \\\\\\\"Playwright Extension\\\\\\\" to be installed.\\\\n   */\\\\n  extension?: boolean;\\\\n\\\\n  server?: {\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * The port to listen on for SSE or MCP transport.\\\\n     */\\\\n    port?: number;\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * The host to bind the server to. Default is localhost. Use 0.0.0.0 to bind to all interfaces.\\\\n     */\\\\n    host?: string;\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * The hosts this server is allowed to serve from. Defaults to the host server is bound to.\\\\n     * This is not for CORS, but rather for the DNS rebinding protection.\\\\n     */\\\\n    allowedHosts?: string[];\\\\n  },\\\\n\\\\n  /**\\\\n   * List of enabled tool capabilities. Possible values:\\\\n   *   - 'core': Core browser automation features.\\\\n   *   - 'pdf': PDF generation and manipulation.\\\\n   *   - 'vision': Coordinate-based interactions.\\\\n   *   - 'devtools': Developer tools features.\\\\n   */\\\\n  capabilities?: ToolCapability[];\\\\n\\\\n  /**\\\\n   * Whether to save the Playwright session into the output directory.\\\\n   */\\\\n  saveSession?: boolean;\\\\n\\\\n  /**\\\\n   * Reuse the same browser context between all connected HTTP clients.\\\\n   */\\\\n  sharedBrowserContext?: boolean;\\\\n\\\\n  /**\\\\n   * Secrets are used to replace matching plain text in the tool responses to prevent the LLM\\\\n   * from accidentally getting sensitive data. It is a convenience and not a security feature,\\\\n   * make sure to always examine information coming in and from the tool on the client.\\\\n   */\\\\n  secrets?: Record<string, string>;\\\\n\\\\n  /**\\\\n   * The directory to save output files.\\\\n   */\\\\n  outputDir?: string;\\\\n\\\\n  /**\\\\n   * Threshold for evicting old output files, in bytes.\\\\n   */\\\\n  outputMaxSize?: number;\\\\n\\\\n  console?: {\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * The level of console messages to return. Each level includes the messages of more severe levels. Defaults to \\\\\\\"info\\\\\\\".\\\\n     */\\\\n    level?: 'error' | 'warning' | 'info' | 'debug';\\\\n  },\\\\n\\\\n  network?: {\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * List of origins to allow the browser to request. Default is to allow all. Origins matching both `allowedOrigins` and `blockedOrigins` will be blocked.\\\\n     *\\\\n     * Supported formats:\\\\n     * - Full origin: `https://example.com:8080` - matches only that origin\\\\n     * - Wildcard port: `http://localhost:*` - matches any port on localhost with http protocol\\\\n     */\\\\n    allowedOrigins?: string[];\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * List of origins to block the browser to request. Origins matching both `allowedOrigins` and `blockedOrigins` will be blocked.\\\\n     *\\\\n     * Supported formats:\\\\n     * - Full origin: `https://example.com:8080` - matches only that origin\\\\n     * - Wildcard port: `http://localhost:*` - matches any port on localhost with http protocol\\\\n     */\\\\n    blockedOrigins?: string[];\\\\n  };\\\\n\\\\n  /**\\\\n   * Specify the attribute to use for test ids, defaults to \\\\\\\"data-testid\\\\\\\".\\\\n   */\\\\n  testIdAttribute?: string;\\\\n\\\\n  timeouts?: {\\\\n    /*\\\\n     * Configures default action timeout: https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-set-default-timeout. Defaults to 5000ms.\\\\n     */\\\\n    action?: number;\\\\n\\\\n    /*\\\\n     * Configures default navigation timeout: https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-set-default-navigation-timeout. Defaults to 60000ms.\\\\n     */\\\\n    navigation?: number;\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * Configures default expect timeout: https://playwright.dev/docs/test-timeouts#expect-timeout. Defaults to 5000ms.\\\\n     */\\\\n    expect?: number;\\\\n\\\\n    /**\\\\n     * How long to wait after each action for triggered work (navigations, requests) to settle before responding. Defaults to 500ms.\\\\n     */\\\\n    settle?: number;\\\\n  };\\\\n\\\\n  /**\\\\n   * Whether to send image responses to the client. Can be \\\\\\\"allow\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"omit\\\\\\\", or \\\\\\\"auto\\\\\\\". Historical reconstruction\\\\n\\\\nThe interface distinguishes:\\\\n\\\\n- **Saved forecast:** the result actually recorded at that time.\\\\n- **Historical reconstruction:** a calculation performed later using a historical cutoff.\\\\n\\\\nYahoo can revise historical data. Saved input snapshots establish what this application used; a later reconstruction cannot establish exactly what Yahoo originally served.\\\\n\\\\n### E. Model evaluation\\\\n\\\\nUse chronological walk-forward evaluation and a separate final evaluation period.\\\\n\\\\nReport:\\\\n- Direction and threshold Brier scores.\\\\n- Reliability plots.\\\\n- Prediction-interval coverage.\\\\n- Baseline comparisons.\\\\n- Sample counts and evaluation dates.\\\\n\\\\nNo future prices, current retrospective metadata, or future corporate-action information may enter historical features improperly.\\\\n\\\\nVolatility adjustment primarily affects move magnitude and tail risk. Additional directional models should be introduced only after demonstrating value in out-of-sample evaluation.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 8. Frontend experience\\\\n\\\\n### Dashboard\\\\n\\\\n- Company/ticker search with identity confirmation.\\\\n- Forecast-mode selection.\\\\n- Historical cutoff controls.\\\\n- Reference price, target close, and freshness.\\\\n- Direction-probability cards.\\\\n- Threshold table.\\\\n- Prediction-interval and distribution displays.\\\\n- Historical-price chart.\\\\n- Model and sample-size details.\\\\n\\\\n### History\\\\n\\\\n- Search by original text, company, and symbol.\\\\n- Filter by date, mode, and status.\\\\n- Reopen original results.\\\\n- Compare forecasts with observed outcomes.\\\\n- Start a fresh analysis from a previous query.\\\\n- Export CSV/JSON.\\\\n\\\\n### Design acceptance\\\\n\\\\n- Responsive desktop and narrow-screen layouts.\\\\n- Keyboard-accessible controls.\\\\n- Readable contrast and typography.\\\\n- Optional dark mode.\\\\n- Numerical summaries for charts.\\\\n- Clear loading, error, empty, stale-data, and insufficient-history states.\\\\n\\\\nCharts are downsampled for rendering while calculations retain full eligible data.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 9. SQLite persistence and backups\\\\n\\\\n### Core records\\\\n\\\\n| Record | Contents |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| Instruments | Canonical symbol, company, exchange, currency, timezone |\\\\n| Market bars | Daily/intraday OHLCV, actions, timestamps, provenance |\\\\n| Queries | Original input, parameters, timestamps, status, failure information |\\\\n| Input snapshots | Immutable, compressed, deduplicated forecast inputs |\\\\n| Forecasts | Saved results, reference/target times, model version |\\\\n| Outcomes | Observed returns and scoring results |\\\\n\\\\nEvery submitted search, analysis, reconstruction, and refresh is recorded. Deliberately repeated submissions remain distinct. Autocomplete keystrokes are interface activity rather than submitted queries.\\\\n\\\\n### Database behavior\\\\n\\\\n- Explicit transactions and foreign keys.\\\\n- Short writes; provider calls outside transactions.\\\\n- Thread-owned connections.\\\\n- Busy timeout.\\\\n- Versioned SQL migrations.\\\\n- Indexed filters and full-text search.\\\\n- No automatic expiry of query history.\\\\n\\\\nStart with rollback-journal mode. This suits the workload and avoids relying on WAL behavior in the installed SQLite version, which falls within the documented WAL-reset issue’s affected range.[4]\\\\n\\\\n### Backup acceptance\\\\n\\\\n- Automatic backup when due while the app is running.\\\\n- Backup before migrations.\\\\n- Manual backup command.\\\\n- SQLite online backup API.\\\\n- Integrity checks before marking a backup successful.\\\\n- Configurable destination, retention, and disk limits.\\\\n- Restore while the application is stopped.\\\\n- Browser verification of restored history.\\\\n\\\\nGit stores source revisions. SQLite backups preserve application data.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 10. Security and performance\\\\n\\\\n### Security\\\\n\\\\n- Bind to `127.0.0.1`.\\\\n- Validate Host/Origin and protect state-changing requests.\\\\n- Use parameterized SQL and allowlisted sort fields.\\\\n- Validate symbol syntax, input lengths, dates, and thresholds.\\\\n- Escape user/provider text.\\\\n- Serve scripts locally under a restrictive Content Security Policy.\\\\n- Keep databases, backups, logs, secrets, and caches outside static paths.\\\\n- Use restrictive data-file permissions.\\\\n- Sanitize spreadsheet exports.\\\\n- Pin dependencies and run vulnerability checks.\\\\n- Keep restore operations in the local CLI.\\\\n\\\\n### Performance targets\\\\n\\\\nMeasure on this laptop:\\\\n\\\\n| Measurement | Proposed target |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| Normal application-server memory | Below 500 MiB |\\\\n| Cached single-symbol forecast | Below one second |\\\\n| Indexed history search on 100,000-query fixture | Below 250 ms |\\\\n| Idle behavior | Negligible background CPU consumption |\\\\n\\\\nNetwork latency and browser-test resource usage are recorded separately.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 11. Playwright MCP acceptance\\\\n\\\\n### Setup\\\\n\\\\nUse the official **`@playwright/mcp`** server through OpenCode’s local MCP integration.\\\\n\\\\n- Install a supported ARM64 Node.js LTS runtime.\\\\n- Pin MCP and browser-test dependencies under `tools/browser/`.\\\\n- Register the server in `opencode.json`.\\\\n- Configure headless Chromium explicitly.\\\\n- Use isolated browser profiles and a dedicated acceptance database.\\\\n- Validate browser/tool compatibility on ARM.\\\\n- Capture session evidence and bounded diagnostic artifacts.\\\\n- Restart OpenCode after configuration changes.\\\\n\\\\nPlaywright MCP is headed by default, making explicit headless configuration important.[5]\\\\n\\\\n### QA ownership\\\\n\\\\n`sol-qa` operates the MCP browser during acceptance. The coordinator verifies that the tools are actually available to that subagent and that the selected model is SOL.\\\\n\\\\nMCP unavailability or browser-launch failure blocks the relevant gate.\\\\n\\\\n### Test path\\\\n\\\\n```text\\\\nSOL QA agent\\\\n  → Playwright MCP\\\\n  → Headless Chromium\\\\n  → Real frontend\\\\n  → Real API\\\\n  → Real application services\\\\n  → Real temporary SQLite database\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nDeterministic tests substitute data at the Yahoo adapter boundary. Browser/API/database behavior remains real.\\\\n\\\\nFinal live-data checks use the actual Yahoo adapter.\\\\n\\\\n### Browser acceptance matrix\\\\n\\\\n| ID | Required behavior |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| B01 | Search by company name and select the correct instrument |\\\\n| B02 | Switch symbols without mixing results or history |\\\\n| B03 | Complete a daily forecast with correct displayed results |\\\\n| B04 | Complete an intraday forecast with correct reference and target times |\\\\n| B05 | Display populated charts, thresholds, and intervals |\\\\n| B06 | Run and correctly label historical reconstruction |\\\\n| B07 | Find successful, failed, and repeated queries |\\\\n| B08 | Restart and reopen an original forecast |\\\\n| B09 | Refresh data without changing an earlier saved result |\\\\n| B10 | Handle invalid symbols, missing data, rate limits, and stale data |\\\\n| B11 | Export and verify CSV/JSON contents |\\\\n| B12 | Restore a backup and retrieve restored history through the browser |\\\\n| B13 | Operate core flows by keyboard and at narrow viewport widths |\\\\n| B14 | Confirm API-mediated data access and inaccessible database files |\\\\n| B15 | Complete real-Yahoo daily and intraday user journeys |\\\\n| B16 | Identify uncaught browser errors and unexpected external dependencies |\\\\n\\\\nSuccessful data-rich scenarios must produce numerical forecasts. Error-state handling alone cannot satisfy forecasting acceptance.\\\\n\\\\n### Automated regression tests\\\\n\\\\nAlongside MCP acceptance:\\\\n- Python pytest covers numerical, API, and database behavior.\\\\n- Checked-in Playwright Test scenarios run in CI.\\\\n- MCP-driven QA covers interactive acceptance and diagnosis.\\\\n\\\\n**Both recorded MCP acceptance and automated regression checks are required.**\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 12. Correctness tests\\\\n\\\\nHighest-priority tests include:\\\\n\\\\n1. Appending future prices cannot change an earlier forecast.\\\\n2. Yahoo cache updates cannot alter saved results.\\\\n3. Larger downside thresholds cannot have higher exceedance probabilities.\\\\n4. Up/down/unchanged probabilities sum to one.\\\\n5. Prediction intervals are ordered and use the displayed reference price.\\\\n6. Splits and currency-unit changes do not become artificial crashes.\\\\n7. Incomplete bars are excluded.\\\\n8. Session gaps do not become ordinary daily returns.\\\\n9. Intraday evaluation groups observations by session.\\\\n10. History survives restart and restore.\\\\n11. Interrupted and failed requests remain identifiable.\\\\n12. API validation and frontend/export handling resist injection.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 13. Task states and evidence\\\\n\\\\n### States\\\\n\\\\n```text\\\\npending\\\\n  → in_progress\\\\n  → verifying\\\\n  → accepted\\\\n  → published\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nFailures return work to implementation. Missing external prerequisites produce `blocked`.\\\\n\\\\n### Required task record\\\\n\\\\n```text\\\\nTask ID:\\\\nRequirement IDs:\\\\nAcceptance criteria:\\\\nDependencies:\\\\nBuild / QA / Documentation assignments:\\\\nAssigned files:\\\\nStatus:\\\\nVerification commands:\\\\nMCP scenarios:\\\\nTested source revision or working-tree identifier:\\\\nObserved results:\\\\nArtifact/report locations:\\\\nOutstanding defects:\\\\nPublished checkpoint and CI URL:\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThe coordinator owns status changes. Documentation may prepare evidence summaries, but acceptance requires QA results.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 16. Orchestrated acceptance loop\\\\n\\\\n### Step 1 — Select and define\\\\n\\\\nThe coordinator:\\\\n- Selects a ready task.\\\\n- Confirms dependencies.\\\\n- Defines observable acceptance criteria.\\\\n- Assigns file ownership.\\\\n- Dispatches up to three SOL roles.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 2 — Build and prepare\\\\n\\\\n- Build implements.\\\\n- QA develops independent verification cases.\\\\n- Documentation prepares relevant updates.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 3 — Stable handoff\\\\n\\\\nBuild reports:\\\\n- Files changed.\\\\n- Implemented behavior.\\\\n- Developer checks performed.\\\\n- Known limitations.\\\\n\\\\nChanges to the verification target pause.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 4 — Independent QA\\\\n\\\\nQA:\\\\n- Reviews the implementation against requirements.\\\\n- Runs focused tests.\\\\n- Exercises applicable flows through Playwright MCP.\\\\n- Inspects API/network behavior, browser errors, and persistence.\\\\n- Returns pass/fail findings with evidence.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 5 — Repair\\\\n\\\\nIf QA fails:\\\\n- Coordinator creates explicit defect tasks.\\\\n- Build repairs the root cause.\\\\n- Documentation adjusts affected descriptions.\\\\n- QA reruns affected checks and the required regression gate.\\\\n\\\\nAn unexplained intermittent pass is not sufficient. Repeated failures without a new diagnosis become a documented blocker rather than an endless blind retry loop.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 6 — Documentation verification\\\\n\\\\nDocumentation confirms:\\\\n- Setup commands execute as documented.\\\\n- API behavior matches actual responses.\\\\n- Model terminology matches implementation.\\\\n- Backup and restore procedures match tested behavior.\\\\n- No unfinished functionality is described as complete.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 7 — Accept and publish\\\\n\\\\nThe coordinator:\\\\n1. Reviews QA and documentation evidence.\\\\n2. Inspects Git status, diff, and recent commits.\\\\n3. Stages intended files.\\\\n4. Commits the checkpoint.\\\\n5. Pushes it.\\\\n6. Verifies the remote revision and CI.\\\\n7. Marks the checkpoint published.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 8 — Continue\\\\n\\\\nAdvance to the next ready task. Regressions reopen affected tasks.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 17. SOL subagent orchestration\\\\n\\\\n### Coordinator\\\\n\\\\nThe primary agent owns:\\\\n\\\\n- Task decomposition and dependency order.\\\\n- Acceptance criteria and file ownership.\\\\n- Dispatching and resuming subagents.\\\\n- Resolving disagreements between Build and QA.\\\\n- Roadmap status and evidence tracking.\\\\n- Git staging, commits, pushes, and release verification.\\\\n\\\\n### Three available SOL roles\\\\n\\\\n| Role | Responsibilities | Ownership |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| **`sol-build`** | Implement application behavior, migrations, integrations, and focused developer tests; repair QA findings | Assigned application/configuration files and unit/integration tests |\\\\n| **`sol-qa`** | Independently verify requirements, review changes, maintain acceptance tests, operate Playwright MCP, and report defects | Acceptance tests and QA evidence; application changes return to Build |\\\\n| **`sol-docs`** | Document verified setup, API behavior, model behavior, operational procedures, and changes | Assigned documentation files |\\\\n\\\\nAll three profiles will explicitly select **GPT-5.6 Sol** using the verified identifier for the authenticated provider.\\\\n\\\\nOpenCode documents `opencode/gpt-5.6-sol` for its Zen provider. The current local configuration contains no SOL role profiles, so model availability and actual subagent model selection must be verified during bootstrap.[1]\\\\n\\\\n### Orchestration limits\\\\n\\\\n- Up to **three subagents per task**, one per role.\\\\n- At most three active subagents across the project initially.\\\\n- One implementation workstream at a time on this laptop.\\\\n- Reuse the same role sessions during repairs.\\\\n- Subagents do not create additional subagents.\\\\n- Only the coordinator performs Git publication and changes acceptance status.\\\\n\\\\n### Parallel work and handoff\\\\n\\\\nAt task start:\\\\n\\\\n- Build implements.\\\\n- QA prepares independent acceptance cases and fixtures.\\\\n- Documentation prepares the relevant document structure.\\\\n\\\\nAfter Build supplies a stable handoff:\\\\n\\\\n- Build pauses changes to the files under verification.\\\\n- QA tests that specific source revision.\\\\n- Documentation checks the actual implementation and verified commands.\\\\n- QA findings return to Build.\\\\n- Any behavior change invalidates the affected acceptance evidence.\\\\n\\\\nOnly QA controls the acceptance browser during a verification session. Shared files, such as manifests and the roadmap, have one designated writer.\\\\n\\\\n### Task packet\\\\n\\\\nEvery delegated task receives:\\\\n\\\\n```text\\\\nTask ID and objective\\\\nRequirement IDs\\\\nDependencies and relevant design decisions\\\\nAssigned files\\\\nAcceptance criteria\\\\nRequired verification commands and MCP journeys\\\\nExpected outputs\\\\nKnown constraints\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nEvery role returns a concise report with changed files, evidence, unresolved issues, and handoff instructions.\\\\n\\\\n**A Build agent’s completion claim is not sufficient for acceptance.**\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 4. Application architecture\\\\n\\\\n```text\\\\nBrowser\\\\n  ├── HTML/CSS/JavaScript\\\\n  └── HTTP requests to /api/v1/*\\\\n                 │\\\\n                 ▼\\\\n              FastAPI\\\\n                 │\\\\n                 ▼\\\\n         Application services\\\\n          ├── Yahoo adapter\\\\n          ├── Forecast engine\\\\n          ├── Outcome evaluation\\\\n          └── Database repository\\\\n                       │\\\\n                       ▼\\\\n                     SQLite\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Stack\\\\n\\\\n| Layer | Technology |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| Backend | FastAPI, one Uvicorn worker |\\\\n| Frontend | Jinja2 page shells, CSS, small JavaScript modules |\\\\n| Charts | Locally served Chart.js |\\\\n| Market data | yfinance behind an application-owned adapter |\\\\n| Numerical work | NumPy/pandas, SciPy where useful |\\\\n| Trading schedules | `exchange_calendars` |\\\\n| Database | Python `sqlite3` |\\\\n| Python dependencies | `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` |\\\\n| Browser tooling | Project-local npm package and lockfile |\\\\n| Agent browser testing | Official Playwright MCP server |\\\\n| Regression tests | pytest and Playwright Test |\\\\n| Code checks | Ruff, mypy, dependency vulnerability checks |\\\\n\\\\n### Mandatory API boundary\\\\n\\\\nThe frontend obtains forecasts, prices, query history, exports, and backup status through the API.\\\\n\\\\nSQL, database connections, provider calls, and database files belong to the backend. Database and backup directories are outside publicly served paths.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 5. API contract\\\\n\\\\n| Endpoint | Responsibility |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| `POST /api/v1/searches` | Record and execute a company/ticker search |\\\\n| `POST /api/v1/forecasts` | Validate a forecast request, obtain inputs, calculate, and persist |\\\\n| `GET /api/v1/forecasts/{id}` | Return an original saved forecast |\\\\n| `GET /api/v1/history` | Search and paginate submitted queries |\\\\n| `GET /api/v1/instruments/{id}/prices` | Return historical price data |\\\\n| `GET /api/v1/exports` | Export selected records through validated filters |\\\\n| `GET /api/v1/backups/status` | Return backup status |\\\\n| `GET /api/v1/health` | Support readiness checks |\\\\n\\\\nForecast responses include:\\\\n\\\\n- Instrument identity, exchange, and currency.\\\\n- Requested mode and effective mode.\\\\n- Reference price and observation timestamp.\\\\n- Data-fetch timestamp and freshness.\\\\n- Target session and close time.\\\\n- Probabilities, thresholds, and prediction intervals.\\\\n- Sample size and data-quality status.\\\\n- Model/configuration version.\\\\n- Saved forecast identifier.\\\\n\\\\nErrors use consistent codes and readable messages. Pagination, query sizes, and sorting are bounded and validated.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 6. Yahoo Finance data pipeline\\\\n\\\\n```text\\\\nRecord request\\\\n  → Resolve instrument\\\\n  → Check cache and market schedule\\\\n  → Fetch eligible data\\\\n  → Validate and normalize\\\\n  → Save forecast input snapshot\\\\n  → Calculate forecast\\\\n  → Persist result\\\\n  → Return API response\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Data handling\\\\n\\\\n- Retrieve daily history on demand, up to ten years where available.\\\\n- Retrieve five-minute history for intraday analysis.\\\\n- Store market-observation time separately from download time.\\\\n- Preserve exchange timezone, currency, and corporate actions.\\\\n- Exclude incomplete bars from completed-period calculations.\\\\n- Identify missing sessions rather than treating gaps as ordinary one-day returns.\\\\n- Verify the price-adjustment policy with split and dividend fixtures.\\\\n- Preserve genuine large moves while identifying corrupt or inconsistent data.\\\\n- Resolve the exchange calendar explicitly; unsupported schedules produce a clear status.\\\\n\\\\n### Freshness and failure behavior\\\\n\\\\n- Refresh daily data when another session may have completed.\\\\n- Refresh intraday data at bounded intervals while relevant.\\\\n- Pause frontend polling when the page is hidden.\\\\n- Coalesce duplicate in-flight provider requests.\\\\n- Apply timeouts and limited backoff.\\\\n- Preserve cached results with their actual timestamps.\\\\n- Backfill available gaps when the laptop resumes.\\\\n\\\\nYahoo five-minute history is limited to approximately 60 calendar days in yfinance’s implementation. The local archive will grow as data is collected; gaps beyond the provider’s retention remain identifiable.[2]\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 7. Forecast definitions and model\\\\n\\\\n### A. Close-to-close\\\\n\\\\n**Reference:** the latest completed trading session’s close.\\\\n\\\\n**Target:** the next trading session’s close.\\\\n\\\\nThe initial model will compare:\\\\n1. An empirical historical distribution.\\\\n2. A volatility-adjusted historical distribution.\\\\n\\\\nThe volatility-adjusted model:\\\\n\\\\n- Calculates historical returns.\\\\n- Estimates volatility causally.\\\\n- Standardizes historical shocks.\\\\n- Rescales those shocks to the current volatility estimate.\\\\n- Derives all probabilities and intervals from one consistent distribution.\\\\n\\\\nFiltered historical simulation is suitable for a lightweight numerical implementation, but its quality depends on the volatility estimate and available history.[3]\\\\n\\\\n### B. Intraday-to-close\\\\n\\\\n**Reference:** the newest eligible completed five-minute bar.\\\\n\\\\n**Target:** the upcoming regular-session close.\\\\n\\\\nUse historical returns from comparable intraday cutoffs to their session closes, respecting exchange-local time and session type.\\\\n\\\\nWhen no fresh eligible regular-session observation exists, show a closed-market or stale-data state and identify the available daily forecast.\\\\n\\\\nIntraday sample sizes are smaller. Minimum-data criteria and uncertainty must be visible, especially for rare large moves.\\\\n\\\\n### C. Outputs\\\\n\\\\n- Probability of rising, falling, or remaining unchanged.\\\\n- Median predicted percentage move.\\\\n- Conditional median gain and conditional median loss.\\\\n- 50%, 80%, and 95% prediction intervals.\\\\n- Initial thresholds of ±1%, ±3%, ±5%, and ±10%.\\\\n- Equivalent price levels in the instrument’s currency.\\\\n\\\\nThese describe outcomes **at the target close**. Intraday barrier-touch probabilities would require a separately defined model.\\\\n\\\\n### D. Historical reconstruction\\\\n\\\\nThe interface distinguishes:\\\\n\\\\n- **Saved forecast:** the result actually recorded at that time.\\\\n- **Historical reconstruction:** a calculation performed later using a historical cutoff.\\\\n\\\\nYahoo can revise historical data. Saved input snapshots establish what this application used; a later reconstruction cannot establish exactly what Yahoo originally served.\\\\n\\\\n### E. Model evaluation\\\\n\\\\nUse chronological walk-forward evaluation and a separate final evaluation period.\\\\n\\\\nReport:\\\\n- Direction and threshold Brier scores.\\\\n- Reliability plots.\\\\n- Prediction-interval coverage.\\\\n- Baseline comparisons.\\\\n- Sample counts and evaluation dates.\\\\n\\\\nNo future prices, current retrospective metadata, or future corporate-action information may enter historical features improperly.\\\\n\\\\nVolatility adjustment primarily affects move magnitude and tail risk. Additional directional models should be introduced only after demonstrating value in out-of-sample evaluation.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 8. Frontend experience\\\\n\\\\n### Dashboard\\\\n\\\\n- Company/ticker search with identity confirmation.\\\\n- Forecast-mode selection.\\\\n- Historical cutoff controls.\\\\n- Reference price, target close, and freshness.\\\\n- Direction-probability cards.\\\\n- Threshold table.\\\\n- Prediction-interval and distribution displays.\\\\n- Historical-price chart.\\\\n- Model and sample-size details.\\\\n\\\\n### History\\\\n\\\\n- Search by original text, company, and symbol.\\\\n- Filter by date, mode, and status.\\\\n- Reopen original results.\\\\n- Compare forecasts with observed outcomes.\\\\n- Start a fresh analysis from a previous query.\\\\n- Export CSV/JSON.\\\\n\\\\n### Design acceptance\\\\n\\\\n- Responsive desktop and narrow-screen layouts.\\\\n- Keyboard-accessible controls.\\\\n- Readable contrast and typography.\\\\n- Optional dark mode.\\\\n- Numerical summaries for charts.\\\\n- Clear loading, error, empty, stale-data, and insufficient-history states.\\\\n\\\\nCharts are downsampled for rendering while calculations retain full eligible data.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 9. SQLite persistence and backups\\\\n\\\\n### Core records\\\\n\\\\n| Record | Contents |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| Instruments | Canonical symbol, company, exchange, currency, timezone |\\\\n| Market bars | Daily/intraday OHLCV, actions, timestamps, provenance |\\\\n| Queries | Original input, parameters, timestamps, status, failure information |\\\\n| Input snapshots | Immutable, compressed, deduplicated forecast inputs |\\\\n| Forecasts | Saved results, reference/target times, model version |\\\\n| Outcomes | Observed returns and scoring results |\\\\n\\\\nEvery submitted search, analysis, reconstruction, and refresh is recorded. Deliberately repeated submissions remain distinct. Autocomplete keystrokes are interface activity rather than submitted queries.\\\\n\\\\n### Database behavior\\\\n\\\\n- Explicit transactions and foreign keys.\\\\n- Short writes; provider calls outside transactions.\\\\n- Thread-owned connections.\\\\n- Busy timeout.\\\\n- Versioned SQL migrations.\\\\n- Indexed filters and full-text search.\\\\n- No automatic expiry of query history.\\\\n\\\\nStart with rollback-journal mode. This suits the workload and avoids relying on WAL behavior in the installed SQLite version, which falls within the documented WAL-reset issue’s affected range.[4]\\\\n\\\\n### Backup acceptance\\\\n\\\\n- Automatic backup when due while the app is running.\\\\n- Backup before migrations.\\\\n- Manual backup command.\\\\n- SQLite online backup API.\\\\n- Integrity checks before marking a backup successful.\\\\n- Configurable destination, retention, and disk limits.\\\\n- Restore while the application is stopped.\\\\n- Browser verification of restored history.\\\\n\\\\nGit stores source revisions. SQLite backups preserve application data.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 10. Security and performance\\\\n\\\\n### Security\\\\n\\\\n- Bind to `127.0.0.1`.\\\\n- Validate Host/Origin and protect state-changing requests.\\\\n- Use parameterized SQL and allowlisted sort fields.\\\\n- Validate symbol syntax, input lengths, dates, and thresholds.\\\\n- Escape user/provider text.\\\\n- Serve scripts locally under a restrictive Content Security Policy.\\\\n- Keep databases, backups, logs, secrets, and caches outside static paths.\\\\n- Use restrictive data-file permissions.\\\\n- Sanitize spreadsheet exports.\\\\n- Pin dependencies and run vulnerability checks.\\\\n- Keep restore operations in the local CLI.\\\\n\\\\n### Performance targets\\\\n\\\\nMeasure on this laptop:\\\\n\\\\n| Measurement | Proposed target |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| Normal application-server memory | Below 500 MiB |\\\\n| Cached single-symbol forecast | Below one second |\\\\n| Indexed history search on 100,000-query fixture | Below 250 ms |\\\\n| Idle behavior | Negligible background CPU consumption |\\\\n\\\\nNetwork latency and browser-test resource usage are recorded separately.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 11. Playwright MCP acceptance\\\\n\\\\n### Setup\\\\n\\\\nUse the official **`@playwright/mcp`** server through OpenCode’s local MCP integration.\\\\n\\\\n- Install a supported ARM64 Node.js LTS runtime.\\\\n- Pin MCP and browser-test dependencies under `tools/browser/`.\\\\n- Register the server in `opencode.json`.\\\\n- Configure headless Chromium explicitly.\\\\n- Use isolated browser profiles and a dedicated acceptance database.\\\\n- Validate browser/tool compatibility on ARM.\\\\n- Capture session evidence and bounded diagnostic artifacts.\\\\n- Restart OpenCode after configuration changes.\\\\n\\\\nPlaywright MCP is headed by default, making explicit headless configuration important.[5]\\\\n\\\\n### QA ownership\\\\n\\\\n`sol-qa` operates the MCP browser during acceptance. The coordinator verifies that the tools are actually available to that subagent and that the selected model is SOL.\\\\n\\\\nMCP unavailability or browser-launch failure blocks the relevant gate.\\\\n\\\\n### Test path\\\\n\\\\n```text\\\\nSOL QA agent\\\\n  → Playwright MCP\\\\n  → Headless Chromium\\\\n  → Real frontend\\\\n  → Real API\\\\n  → Real application services\\\\n  → Real temporary SQLite database\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nDeterministic tests substitute data at the Yahoo adapter boundary. Browser/API/database behavior remains real.\\\\n\\\\nFinal live-data checks use the actual Yahoo adapter.\\\\n\\\\n### Browser acceptance matrix\\\\n\\\\n| ID | Required behavior |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| B01 | Search by company name and select the correct instrument |\\\\n| B02 | Switch symbols without mixing results or history |\\\\n| B03 | Complete a daily forecast with correct displayed results |\\\\n| B04 | Complete an intraday forecast with correct reference and target times |\\\\n| B05 | Display populated charts, thresholds, and intervals |\\\\n| B06 | Run and correctly label historical reconstruction |\\\\n| B07 | Find successful, failed, and repeated queries |\\\\n| B08 | Restart and reopen an original forecast |\\\\n| B09 | Refresh data without changing an earlier saved result |\\\\n| B10 | Handle invalid symbols, missing data, rate limits, and stale data |\\\\n| B11 | Export and verify CSV/JSON contents |\\\\n| B12 | Restore a backup and retrieve restored history through the browser |\\\\n| B13 | Operate core flows by keyboard and at narrow viewport widths |\\\\n| B14 | Confirm API-mediated data access and inaccessible database files |\\\\n| B15 | Complete real-Yahoo daily and intraday user journeys |\\\\n| B16 | Identify uncaught browser errors and unexpected external dependencies |\\\\n\\\\nSuccessful data-rich scenarios must produce numerical forecasts. Error-state handling alone cannot satisfy forecasting acceptance.\\\\n\\\\n### Automated regression tests\\\\n\\\\nAlongside MCP acceptance:\\\\n- Python pytest covers numerical, API, and database behavior.\\\\n- Checked-in Playwright Test scenarios run in CI.\\\\n- MCP-driven QA covers interactive acceptance and diagnosis.\\\\n\\\\n**Both recorded MCP acceptance and automated regression checks are required.**\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 12. Correctness tests\\\\n\\\\nHighest-priority tests include:\\\\n\\\\n1. Appending future prices cannot change an earlier forecast.\\\\n2. Yahoo cache updates cannot alter saved results.\\\\n3. Larger downside thresholds cannot have higher exceedance probabilities.\\\\n4. Up/down/unchanged probabilities sum to one.\\\\n5. Prediction intervals are ordered and use the displayed reference price.\\\\n6. Splits and currency-unit changes do not become artificial crashes.\\\\n7. Incomplete bars are excluded.\\\\n8. Session gaps do not become ordinary daily returns.\\\\n9. Intraday evaluation groups observations by session.\\\\n10. History survives restart and restore.\\\\n11. Interrupted and failed requests remain identifiable.\\\\n12. API validation and frontend/export handling resist injection.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 13. Repository layout and commands\\\\n\\\\n### Proposed layout\\\\n\\\\n```text\\\\nMVP-PLAN.md\\\\nMVP-ROADMAP.md\\\\nAGENTS.md\\\\nREADME.md\\\\nopencode.json\\\\npyproject.toml\\\\nuv.lock\\\\nMakefile\\\\n\\\\n.opencode/agents/\\\\n  sol-build.md\\\\n  sol-qa.md\\\\n  sol-docs.md\\\\n\\\\nsrc/stock_probs/\\\\n  app.py\\\\n  cli.py\\\\n  services.py\\\\n  db.py\\\\n  providers/\\\\n  forecasting/\\\\n  templates/\\\\n  static/\\\\n\\\\nmigrations/\\\\ntests/\\\\ntools/browser/\\\\ndocs/\\\\nlegacy/\\\\n.github/workflows/\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n`AGENTS.md` will reference the plan and roadmap and contain only verified commands, boundaries, and repository-specific pitfalls.\\\\n\\\\n### Commands to implement\\\\n\\\\n| Command | Purpose |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| `make setup` | Install locked development dependencies |\\\\n| `make browser-install` | Install compatible Chromium and system prerequisites |\\\\n| `make dev` | Start the local application |\\\\n| `make check` | Format check, lint, typecheck, unit/API tests |\\\\n| `make browser-test` | Run deterministic browser regressions |\\\\n| `make acceptance` | Run deterministic acceptance, including restore tests |\\\\n| `make live-smoke` | Run explicit real-Yahoo verification |\\\\n| `make release-check` | Verify release evidence and required checks |\\\\n\\\\nMCP browser journeys are performed by QA through the configured tools. A shell command passing does not imply those journeys have occurred.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# `MVP-ROADMAP.md`\\\\n\\\\n## 14. Milestones and commit gates\\\\n\\\\nAll milestones are currently pending.\\\\n\\\\n| ID | Deliverables | Dependencies | Acceptance gate |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| **M00 — Plan and orchestration** | Save plan/roadmap; create compact instructions and SOL profiles; verify model routing | Editing enabled | Configuration validates; roles resolve to SOL; ownership and delegation limits established |\\\\n| **M01 — Foundation** | Package structure, lockfiles, task runner, Git ignores, prototype archive, development prerequisites | M00 | Reproducible ARM setup; imports work; tracked-file review; GitHub access verified |\\\\n| **M02 — Browser infrastructure** | Playwright MCP, headless Chromium, QA tool access, isolated fixtures, CI browser smoke | M01 | QA performs an actual MCP browser interaction; automated browser smoke passes |\\\\n| **M03 — Persistence** | Schema, migrations, query recording, snapshots, backup/restore | M01 | Restart, interruption, immutability, integrity, and restore tests pass |\\\\n| **M04 — API** | Validated contracts, pagination, repository integration, error responses, secure defaults | M03 | API/security tests pass; public database access fails |\\\\n| **M05 — Yahoo integration** | Search, retrieval, normalization, caching, calendars, freshness | M04 | Provider fixtures pass; real adapter smoke recorded |\\\\n| **M06 — Daily forecasting** | Baselines, volatility-adjusted distribution, reconstruction, outcomes, evaluation | M05 | Numerical/leakage tests pass; evaluation report produced |\\\\n| **M07 — Dashboard and history** | Daily UI, charts, search history, exports, backup status | M02, M06 | Applicable browser scenarios pass through MCP and regression tests |\\\\n| **M08 — Intraday** | Intraday archive, cutoff matching, model, target-session handling, UI | M05, M07 | Intraday correctness tests and MCP acceptance pass |\\\\n| **M09 — Full acceptance** | Responsive/keyboard checks, security audit, performance measurements, restore drill | M08 | All deterministic requirements accepted on laptop and CI |\\\\n| **M10 — Release** | Fresh-install verification, live journeys, final documentation, Git publication | M09 | Both modes pass live verification; evidence matches source; remote revision/tag verified |\\\\n\\\\nM00 is the coordinator’s bootstrap task. Once the profiles are loaded, the Build/QA/Documentation pattern applies to subsequent work.\\\\n\\\\nEach milestone is divided into small tasks before delegation.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 15. Task states and evidence\\\\n\\\\n### States\\\\n\\\\n```text\\\\npending\\\\n  → in_progress\\\\n  → verifying\\\\n  → accepted\\\\n  → published\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nFailures return work to implementation. Missing external prerequisites produce `blocked`.\\\\n\\\\n### Required task record\\\\n\\\\n```text\\\\nTask ID:\\\\nRequirement IDs:\\\\nAcceptance criteria:\\\\nDependencies:\\\\nBuild / QA / Documentation assignments:\\\\nAssigned files:\\\\nStatus:\\\\nVerification commands:\\\\nMCP scenarios:\\\\nTested source revision or working-tree identifier:\\\\nObserved results:\\\\nArtifact/report locations:\\\\nOutstanding defects:\\\\nPublished checkpoint and CI URL:\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThe coordinator owns status changes. Documentation may prepare evidence summaries, but acceptance requires QA results.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 16. Orchestrated acceptance loop\\\\n\\\\n### Step 1 — Select and define\\\\n\\\\nThe coordinator:\\\\n- Selects a ready task.\\\\n- Confirms dependencies.\\\\n- Defines observable acceptance criteria.\\\\n- Assigns file ownership.\\\\n- Dispatches up to three SOL roles.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 2 — Build and prepare\\\\n\\\\n- Build implements.\\\\n- QA develops independent verification cases.\\\\n- Documentation prepares relevant updates.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 3 — Stable handoff\\\\n\\\\nBuild reports:\\\\n- Files changed.\\\\n- Implemented behavior.\\\\n- Developer checks performed.\\\\n- Known limitations.\\\\n\\\\nChanges to the verification target pause.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 4 — Independent QA\\\\n\\\\nQA:\\\\n- Reviews the implementation against requirements.\\\\n- Runs focused tests.\\\\n- Exercises applicable flows through Playwright MCP.\\\\n- Inspects API/network behavior, browser errors, and persistence.\\\\n- Returns pass/fail findings with evidence.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 5 — Repair\\\\n\\\\nIf QA fails:\\\\n- Coordinator creates explicit defect tasks.\\\\n- Build repairs the root cause.\\\\n- Documentation adjusts affected descriptions.\\\\n- QA reruns affected checks and the required regression gate.\\\\n\\\\nAn unexplained intermittent pass is not sufficient. Repeated failures without a new diagnosis become a documented blocker rather than an endless blind retry loop.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 6 — Documentation verification\\\\n\\\\nDocumentation confirms:\\\\n- Setup commands execute as documented.\\\\n- API behavior matches actual responses.\\\\n- Model terminology matches implementation.\\\\n- Backup and restore procedures match tested behavior.\\\\n- No unfinished functionality is described as complete.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 7 — Accept and publish\\\\n\\\\nThe coordinator:\\\\n1. Reviews QA and documentation evidence.\\\\n2. Inspects Git status, diff, and recent commits.\\\\n3. Stages intended files.\\\\n4. Commits the checkpoint.\\\\n5. Pushes it.\\\\n6. Verifies the remote revision and CI.\\\\n7. Marks the checkpoint published.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 8 — Continue\\\\n\\\\nAdvance to the next ready task. Regressions reopen affected tasks.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 17. Git and CI workflow\\\\n\\\\nRepository: [`eddiesoz/stock_probs`](https://github.com/eddiesoz/stock_probs).\\\\n\\\\n### Foundation work\\\\n\\\\n- Verify remote state and write access.\\\\n- Install/authenticate GitHub CLI as needed.\\\\n- Untrack virtual environments while preserving local installations.\\\\n- Exclude databases, backups, caches, browser binaries, dependencies, secrets, and generated artifacts.\\\\n- Preserve the prototype implementation under `legacy/`.\\\\n\\\\n### Checkpoint policy\\\\n\\\\n- Coordinator alone stages, commits, and pushes.\\\\n- Each checkpoint includes implementation, tests, and verified documentation.\\\\n- Browser-facing checkpoints require MCP evidence and passing browser regressions.\\\\n- CI failures reopen the relevant milestone.\\\\n- Release tags identify the accepted source version.\\\\n\\\\nSource-control publication and database backups are verified separately.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 18. Final definition of done\\\\n\\\\nThe MVP is complete only when:\\\\n\\\\n- Every requirement has an accepted task and recorded evidence.\\\\n- Both forecast modes work with sufficient-data inputs.\\\\n- User-selected stocks and ETFs work without hardcoded application dependencies.\\\\n- Frontend data access passes through the API.\\\\n- Query history is searchable and survives restart.\\\\n- Saved forecasts and their inputs remain immutable.\\\\n- Backup restoration is demonstrated through the application.\\\\n- Playwright MCP acceptance is completed by QA.\\\\n- Automated checks pass on the laptop and in CI.\\\\n- Real Yahoo end-to-end verification succeeds.\\\\n- Security and resource results are documented.\\\\n- Fresh setup works from the committed instructions.\\\\n- SOL Build, QA, and Documentation handoffs are complete.\\\\n- The accepted source revision and release tag are verified on GitHub.\\\\n\\\\n## Research references\\\\n\\\\n1. [OpenCode model catalog, including GPT-5.6 Sol](https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/)\\\\n2. [yfinance historical-data implementation](https://github.com/ranaroussi/yfinance/blob/main/yfinance/scrapers/history.py)\\\\n3. [Bank of England: filtered historical simulation](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/working-paper/2015/filtered-historical-simulation-value-at-risk-models-and-their-competitors.pdf)\\\\n4. [SQLite WAL documentation and WAL-reset issue](https://sqlite.org/wal.html#the_wal_reset_bug)\\\\n5. [Official Playwright MCP server](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp)\\\\n6. [OpenCode MCP integration](https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/)\\\\n7. [Chronological model validation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html)\\\\n8. [Probability calibration](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html)\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n**Status:** the full plan now includes SOL orchestration, API-only frontend data access, Playwright MCP acceptance, and the completion loop. LUNA Docs finalizes documentation against verified behavior.\\\\n6.
