Probability MVP Plan\\\\n2: \\\\n3: ## Status And Scope\\\\n4: \\\\n5: This is the implementation contract for the planned local ARM64 stock probability web app. The repository currently contains only exploratory Python scripts. It does not yet contain the application described below.\\\\n6: \\\\n7: - `M00` is **Completed** for the four documentation files created in this baseline: `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md`.\\\\n8: - `M01` through `M07` are **Pending**. No implementation milestone is complete.\\\\n9: - A task may move to **Completed** only after its acceptance evidence, verification result, repair history, and reviewer are recorded.\\\\n10: \\\\n11: ## Product Goal\\\\n12: \\\\n13: Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF and receives two forecast views:\\\\n14: \\\\n15: 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\\\\n16: 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\\\\n17: \\\\n18: Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. Every displayed result must identify its symbol, asset type, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\\\n19: \\\\n20: This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\\\\n21: \\\\n22: ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\\\\n23: \\\\n24: ### API boundary\\\\n25: \\\\n26: - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\\\n27: - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\\\\n28: - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\\\\n29: - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\\\\n30: \\\\n31: ### Data source and time semantics\\\\n32: \\\\n33: - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\\\\n34: - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\\\\n35: - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\\\n36: - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\\\n37: \\\\n38: ### Persistence and auditability\\\\n39: \\\\n40: - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\\\n41: - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\\\n42: - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\\\n43: - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\\\n44: - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\\\n45: - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\\\n46: \\\\n47: ### User experience\\\\n48: \\\\n49: - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\\\n50: - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\\\n51: - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\\\n52: - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\\\n53: - Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\\\\n54: \\\\n55: ### Deployment and resources\\\\n56: \\\\n57: - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\\\n58: - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\\\n59: - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\\\n60: - Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\\\\n61: - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\\\n62: \\\\n63: ## Planned Architecture\\\\n64: \\\\n65: The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\\\n66: \\\\n67: The API/application layers should remain separable:\\\\n68: \\\\n69: - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\\\n70: - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\\\n71: - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\\\n72: - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\\\n73: - **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\\\\n74: \\\\n75: The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\\\n76: \\\\n77: ## Forecast Contract\\\\n78: \\\\n79: The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\\\n80: \\\\n81: - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\\\n82: - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\\\n83: - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\\\n84: - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\\\n85: - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\\\n86: - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\\\n87: - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\\\n88: \\\\n89: The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\\\\n90: \\\\n91: ## Task Register\\\\n92: \\\\n93: The coordinator assigns no more than three agents to a task in addition to the coordinator. The listed acceptance evidence is required before status can become **Completed**.\\\\n94: \\\\n95: ### M00 - Documentation Baseline\\\\n96: \\\\n97: - **Status:** Completed, docs only.\\\\n98: - **Dependencies:** None.\\\\n99: - **Agents:** `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n100: - **Scope:** Create the plan, roadmap, compact agent rules, and honest repository README.\\\\n101: - **Acceptance evidence:** [x] `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md` exist; [x] current prototype is distinguished from planned implementation; [x] implementation milestones remain pending.\\\\n102: - **Verification:** [x] documentation-only diff reviewed; [x] required product invariants, orchestration, evidence fields, repair loop, and final definition of done are present.\\\\n103: - **Repair record:** None at baseline creation.\\\\n104: \\\\n105: ### M01 - API And Application Shell\\\\n106: \\\\n107: - **Status:** Pending.\\\\n108: - **Dependencies:** M00.\\\\n109: - **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n110: - **Scope:** Establish the ARM64-friendly application layout, FastAPI service, versioned `/api/v1` boundary, structured errors, health/readiness behavior, frontend shell, and documented local loopback launch path.\\\\n111: - **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] API contract and schema tests pass; [ ] a browser can obtain application data only through `/api/v1`; [ ] no frontend source imports a database driver or opens a SQLite path; [ ] loopback smoke test passes on the target ARM64 environment; [ ] non-obvious code decisions have useful comments.\\\\n112: - **Verification:** [ ] unit and API tests; [ ] negative validation tests; [ ] browser network inspection; [ ] local ARM64 startup and bounded-resource smoke test.\\\\n113: - **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M01-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\\\n114: \\\\n115: ### M02 - SQLite Audit And Immutable Records\\\\n116: \\\\n117: - **Status:** Pending.\\\\n118: - **Dependencies:** M01.\\\\n119: - **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n120: - **Scope:** Define migrations and repositories for search events, successful/failed/repeated status, immutable forecast inputs, immutable results, append-only outcomes, provenance, and bounded searchable history.\\\\n121: - **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] migration is reproducible on a clean database; [ ] every submission persists exactly one auditable event even on failure or repetition; [ ] input, result, and outcome records cannot be silently overwritten; [ ] history filters and pagination work through `/api/v1`; [ ] restart preserves records.\\\\n122: - **Verification:** [ ] repository and migration tests; [ ] success/failure/repeat matrix; [ ] immutability and concurrent-write tests; [ ] API authorization/boundary test showing no direct browser database access.\\\\n123: - **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M02-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\\\n124: \\\\n125: ### M03 - Yahoo Finance Data And Forecast Engine\\\\n126: \\\\n127: - **Status:** Pending.\\\\n128: - **Dependencies:** M01 and M02.\\\\n129: - **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n130: - **Scope:** Implement the provider adapter, symbol/asset validation, completed-bar selection, close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close horizons, probability calculations, magnitude intervals, provenance, stale/missing-data handling, and immutable forecast writes.\\\\n131: - **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] stock and ETF selections follow one tested contract; [ ] an in-progress five-minute bar is excluded; [ ] both horizons identify their origin and target timestamps; [ ] probabilities and magnitude intervals include definitions, levels, units, and model/version; [ ] provider failures and insufficient data create auditable failed searches without fabricated results; [ ] deterministic fixtures reproduce recorded outputs.\\\\n132: - **Verification:** [ ] provider adapter tests with fixtures; [ ] timezone/session and boundary-time tests; [ ] incomplete-bar, missing-bar, stale-data, and out-of-session tests; [ ] numerical invariants and repeatability checks; [ ] ARM64 resource smoke test.\\\\n133: - **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M03-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\\\n134: \\\\n135: ### M04 - Dashboard And Searchable History\\\\n136: \\\\n137: - **Status:** Pending.\\\\n138: - **Dependencies:** M01, M02, and M03.\\\\n139: - **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n140: - **Scope:** Build the responsive accessible dashboard for symbol selection, forecast submission, result comparison, source/as-of/stale/error context, and searchable history.\\\\n141: - **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] desktop and mobile layouts retain all essential content; [ ] keyboard and screen-reader flows cover search, results, errors, and history; [ ] loading, empty, failed, repeated, stale, and successful states are understandable without color; [ ] result views show both forecast modes, probabilities, and magnitude intervals; [ ] all data requests use `/api/v1`.\\\\n142: - **Verification:** [ ] component and API integration tests; [ ] accessibility audit and keyboard pass; [ ] checked-in browser regression scenarios; [ ] browser network assertion for the API-only boundary; [ ] low-resource render smoke test.\\\\n143: - **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M04-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\\\n144: \\\\n145: ### M05 - Backup, Restore, And Secure Loopback Operations\\\\n146: \\\\n147: - **Status:** Pending.\\\\n148: - **Dependencies:** M02 and M04.\\\\n149: - **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n150: - **Scope:** Add verified backup and restore workflow, integrity/manifest checks, safe restore staging, loopback deployment defaults, input/path validation, timeout limits, and operational documentation.\\\\n151: - **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] a backup includes the required SQLite data and verifiable metadata/checksum; [ ] restore to a clean or staging location validates schema, integrity, and representative counts before promotion; [ ] a tampered, truncated, incompatible, or unsafe-path artifact is rejected; [ ] active data is not silently destroyed; [ ] default bind is loopback and security behavior is documented.\\\\n152: - **Verification:** [ ] backup/restore round trip; [ ] negative artifact and path tests; [ ] restart and recovery test; [ ] loopback exposure check; [ ] resource and timeout checks on ARM64.\\\\n153: - **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M05-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\\\n154: \\\\n155: ### M06 - QA, Playwright MCP, Browser Regressions, And CI\\\\n156: \\\\n157: - **Status:** Pending.\\\\n158: - **Dependencies:** M01, M02, M03, M04, and M05.\\\\n159: - **Agents:** `LUNA MAX QA`, `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n160: - **Scope:** Configure the official `@playwright/mcp` headless for agent QA, check in automated browser regressions, and establish Git/CI gates for linting, typing or static checks where adopted, unit/API tests, accessibility, security, resource limits, migration, and backup/restore.\\\\n161: - **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] the official MCP configuration is discoverable and runs headless; [ ] browser regressions are checked in and run against a deterministic local app; [ ] CI blocks a failing unit/API/browser/accessibility/security/restore gate; [ ] test artifacts identify task and commit context; [ ] no test depends on the tracked `burry_env/` or local `.venv/`.\\\\n162: - **Verification:** [ ] clean-environment CI run; [ ] intentional-failure gate test; [ ] headless MCP smoke run; [ ] browser regression run on desktop and mobile viewports; [ ] ARM64 or documented equivalent resource run.\\\\n163: - **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M06-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\\\n164: \\\\n165: ### M07 - Integrated MVP Acceptance\\\\n166: \\\\n167: - **Status:** Pending.\\\\n168: - **Dependencies:** M06.\\\\n169: - **Agents:** `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n170: - **Scope:** Run the complete user journey and release review on a low-resource ARM64 laptop, reconcile all task evidence, and publish the supported local operation and limitations.\\\\n171: - **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] a user selects a stock and an ETF and receives both forecast horizons; [ ] probabilities and magnitude intervals are traceable to immutable inputs/results; [ ] successful, failed, and repeated searches appear in searchable history; [ ] outcomes can be appended without changing forecasts; [ ] backup/restore is verified; [ ] responsive/accessibility, loopback security, MCP/browser, comments, and Git/CI gates all pass; [ ] README and roadmap state the shipped scope honestly.\\\\n172: - **Verification:** [ ] full CI; [ ] end-to-end browser journey; [ ] restore from the produced artifact; [ ] security and accessibility sign-off; [ ] performance/resource evidence; [ ] coordinator review of every dependency and evidence field.\\\\n173: - **Repair record:** Record each failed release check as `R-M07-<n>` and keep M07 pending until repaired and rerun.\\\\n174: \\\\n175: ## Evidence Record Format\\\\n176: \\\\n177: Every implementation task must maintain these fields in its task record or linked review:\\\\n178: \\\\n179: - **Task ID:** the exact `M##` or `R-M##-<n>` identifier.\\\\n180: - **Status:** `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`.\\\\n181: - **Dependencies verified:** the completed task IDs and evidence references.\\\\n182: - **Change summary:** what changed and what did not change.\\\\n183: - **Acceptance evidence:** links, test names, fixture IDs, screenshots, logs, checksums, or measured resource results.\\\\n184: - **Verification result:** command/check name, environment, timestamp, and pass/fail result.\\\\n185: - **Repair history:** each failure, root cause, repair, and rerun result; use `None` only when no repair was needed.\\\\n186: - **Reviewer:** the coordinator and the verifying agent.\\\\n187: \\\\n188: Evidence is not a prose promise. A skipped or unavailable check must be recorded as such and cannot satisfy a required acceptance field.\\\\n189: \\\\n190: ## Verification And Repair Loop\\\\n191: \\\\n192: 1. The coordinator selects the next pending task only after its dependencies have completed with evidence.\\\\n193: 2. The assigned build, QA, and documentation agents work within the task scope and keep the task status visible.\\\\n194: 3. The coordinator runs the targeted verification set, then the applicable repository/Git/CI gates.\\\\n195: 4. If any check fails, the task remains pending or in progress. The coordinator records the failure, creates `R-M##-<n>`, assigns no more than three agents, and repairs the root cause rather than weakening the check.\\\\n196: 5. QA reruns the failed check and the relevant regression set. Documentation records the new evidence and any limitation.\\\\n197: 6. The coordinator marks the task completed only when every required acceptance field passes and the reviewer is named.\\\\n198: \\\\n199: ## Final Definition Of Done\\\\n200: \\\\n201: The MVP is done only when all of the following are true:\\\\n202: \\\\n203: - M00 through M07 have explicit statuses and evidence, with no implementation milestone marked complete by assertion alone.\\\\n204: - A user can select Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs and receive close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close forecasts with clear session/bar semantics.\\\\n205: - Results contain probabilities and defined magnitude intervals with source, as-of, stale/error, model/version, input, and output provenance.\\\\n206: - Every submitted successful, failed, and repeated search is retained, history is searchable through `/api/v1`, and forecast inputs/results/outcomes are immutable or append-only as specified.\\\\n207: - Backup artifacts and restores are verified through integrity, compatibility, representative-data, and non-destructive promotion checks.\\\\n208: - The frontend uses FastAPI `/api/v1` for all application data and has no direct SQLite access.\\\\n209: - The dashboard is responsive and accessible, including keyboard, screen-reader, text-equivalent, loading, empty, stale, repeated, and failure behavior.\\\\n210: - The default deployment is secure loopback, bounded for a low-resource ARM64 laptop, and documented with its limitations.\\\\n211: - The official headless `@playwright/mcp` supports agent QA, automated browser regressions are checked in, and Git/CI gates fail closed on required regressions.\\\\n212: - Code comments explain non-obvious behavior, the supported local workflow is documented, and README claims match the evidence actually shipped.\\\\n\\\\n(End of file - It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\\\n- Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\\\n\\\\n### Persistence and auditability\\\\n\\\\n- Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\\\n- A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\\\n- The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\\\n- An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\\\n- Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\\\n- History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\\\n\\\\n### User experience\\\\n\\\\n- The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\\\n- Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\\\n- Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\\\n- History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\\\n- Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\\\\n\\\\n### Deployment and resources\\\\n\\\\n- The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\\\n- Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\\\n- Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\\\n- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\\\\n- All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\\\n\\\\n## Planned Architecture\\\\n\\\\nThe intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\\\n\\\\nThe API/application layers should remain separable:\\\\n\\\\n- **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\\\n- **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\\\n- **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\\\n- **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\\\n- **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\\\\n\\\\nThe exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\\\n\\\\n## Forecast Contract\\\\n\\\\nThe forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\\\n\\\\n- Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\\\n- Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\\\n- What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\\\n- What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\\\n- What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\\\n- What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\\\n- What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\\\n\\\\nThe current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\\\\n\\\\n## Task Register\\\\n\\\\nThe coordinator assigns no more than three agents to a task in addition to the coordinator. The listed acceptance evidence is required before status can become **Completed**.\\\\n\\\\n### M00 - Documentation Baseline\\\\n\\\\n- **Status:** Completed, docs only.\\\\n- **Dependencies:** None.\\\\n- **Agents:** `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n- **Scope:** Create the plan, roadmap, compact agent rules, and honest repository README.\\\\n- **Acceptance evidence:** [x] `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md` exist; [x] current prototype is distinguished from planned implementation; [x] implementation milestones remain pending.\\\\n- **Verification:** [x] documentation-only diff reviewed; [x] required product invariants, orchestration, evidence fields, repair loop, and final definition of done are present.\\\\n- **Repair record:** None at baseline creation.\\\\n\\\\n### M01 - API And Application Shell\\\\n\\\\n- **Status:** Pending.\\\\n- **Dependencies:** M00.\\\\n- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n- **Scope:** Establish the ARM64-friendly application layout, FastAPI service, versioned `/api/v1` boundary, structured errors, health/readiness behavior, frontend shell, and documented local loopback launch path.\\\\n- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] API contract and schema tests pass; [ ] a browser can obtain application data only through `/api/v1`; [ ] no frontend source imports a database driver or opens a SQLite path; [ ] loopback smoke test passes on the target ARM64 environment; [ ] non-obvious code decisions have useful comments.\\\\n- **Verification:** [ ] unit and API tests; [ ] negative validation tests; [ ] browser network inspection; [ ] local ARM64 startup and bounded-resource smoke test.\\\\n- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M01-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\\\n\\\\n### M02 - SQLite Audit And Immutable Records\\\\n\\\\n- **Status:** Pending.\\\\n- **Dependencies:** M01.\\\\n- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n- **Scope:** Define migrations and repositories for search events, successful/failed/repeated status, immutable forecast inputs, immutable results, append-only outcomes, provenance, and bounded searchable history.\\\\n- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] migration is reproducible on a clean database; [ ] restart preserves records.\\\\n- **Verification:** [ ] repository and migration tests; [ ] success/failure/repeat matrix; [ ] immutability and concurrent-write tests; [ ] API authorization/boundary test showing no direct browser database access.\\\\n- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M02-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\\\n\\\\n### M03 - Yahoo Finance Data And Forecast Engine\\\\n\\\\n- **Status:** Pending.\\\\n- **Dependencies:** M01 and M02.\\\\n- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n- **Scope:** Implement the provider adapter, symbol/asset validation, completed-bar selection, close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close horizons, probability calculations, magnitude intervals, provenance, stale/missing-data handling, and immutable forecast writes.\\\\n- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] stock and ETF selections follow one tested contract; [ ] timezone/session and boundary-time tests; [ ] incomplete-bar, missing-bar, stale-data, and out-of-session tests; [ ] numerical invariants and repeatability checks; [ ] ARM64 resource smoke test.\\\\n- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M03-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\\\n\\\\n### M04 - Dashboard And Searchable History\\\\n\\\\n- **Status:** Pending.\\\\n- **Dependencies:** M01, M02, and M03.\\\\n- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n- **Scope:** Build the responsive accessible dashboard for symbol selection, forecast submission, result comparison, source/as-of/stale/error context, and searchable history.\\\\n- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] desktop and mobile layouts retain all essential content; [ ] browser regressions are checked in and run against a deterministic local app; [ ] CI blocks a failing unit/API/browser/accessibility/security/restore gate; [ ] test artifacts identify task and commit context; [ ] no test depends on the tracked `burry_env/` or local `.venv/`.\\\\n- **Verification:** [ ] clean-environment CI run; [ ] intentional-failure gate test; [ ] headless MCP smoke run; [ ] browser regression run on desktop and mobile viewports; [ ] ARM64 or documented equivalent resource run.\\\\n- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M06-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\\\\n\\\\n### M07 - Integrated MVP Acceptance\\\\n\\\\n- **Status:** Pending.\\\\n- **Dependencies:** M06.\\\\n- **Agents:** `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n- **Scope:** Run the complete user journey and release review on a low-resource ARM64 laptop, reconcile all task evidence, and publish the supported local operation and limitations.\\\\n- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] a user selects a stock and an ETF and receives both forecast horizons; [ ] probabilities and magnitude intervals are traceable to immutable inputs/results; [ ] successful, failed, and repeated searches appear in searchable history; [ ] outcomes can be appended without changing forecasts; [ ] backup/restore is verified; [ ] responsive/accessibility, loopback security, MCP/browser, comments, and Git/CI gates all pass; [ ] README and roadmap state the shipped scope honestly.\\\\n- **Verification:** [ ] full CI; [ ] end-to-end browser journey; [ ] restore from the produced artifact; [ ] security and accessibility sign-off; [ ] performance/resource evidence; [ ] coordinator review of every dependency and evidence field.\\\\n- **Repair record:** Record each failed release check as `R-M07-<n>` and keep M07 pending until repaired and rerun.\\\\n\\\\n## Evidence Record Format\\\\n\\\\nEvery implementation task must maintain these fields in its task record or linked review:\\\\n\\\\n- **Task ID:** the exact `M##` or `R-M##-<n>` identifier.\\\\n- **Status:** `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`.\\\\n- **Dependencies verified:** the completed task IDs and evidence references.\\\\n- **Change summary:** what changed and what did not change.\\\\n- **Acceptance evidence:** links, test names, fixture IDs, screenshots, logs, checksums, or measured resource results.\\\\n- **Verification result:** command/check name, environment, timestamp, and pass/fail result.\\\\n- **Repair history:** each failure, root cause, repair, and rerun result; use `None` only when no repair was needed.\\\\n- **Reviewer:** the coordinator and the verifying agent.\\\\n\\\\nEvidence is not a prose promise. A skipped or unavailable check must be recorded as such and cannot satisfy a required acceptance field.\\\\n\\\\n## Verification And Repair Loop\\\\n\\\\n1. The coordinator selects the next pending task only after its dependencies have completed with evidence.\\\\n2. The assigned build, QA, and documentation agents work within the task scope and keep the task status visible.\\\\n3. The coordinator runs the targeted verification set, then the applicable repository/Git/CI gates.\\\\n4. If any check fails, the task remains pending or in progress. The coordinator records the failure, creates `R-M##-<n>`, assigns no more than three agents, and repairs the root cause rather than weakening the check.\\\\n5. QA reruns the failed check and the relevant regression set. Documentation records the new evidence and any limitation.\\\\n6. The coordinator marks the task completed only when every required acceptance field passes and the reviewer is named.\\\\n\\\\n## Final Definition Of Done\\\\n\\\\nThe MVP is done only when all of the The key gate is not a plausible number; it is reproducibility from captured completed bars, explicit session rules, model/version, probabilities, intervals, and data-quality state.\\\\n\\\\n### Phase 3: Make The Workflow Usable\\\\n\\\\n`M04` turns the API into a responsive accessible dashboard and searchable history view. Loading, empty, failure, stale, repeated, and success states are part of the feature. All frontend application data continues to use FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\\\n\\\\n### Phase 4: Make Local Operation Durable\\\\n\\\\n`M05` adds verified backups/restores and secure loopback defaults. A restore is not accepted because a file exists; it must pass integrity, compatibility, representative-data, and non-destructive promotion checks.\\\\n\\\\n### Phase 5: Make Regressions Visible\\\\n\\\\n`M06` configures the official `@playwright/mcp` headless for agent QA, checks browser regressions into the repository, and makes Git/CI gates enforce the contract. The test environment must not depend on `burry_env/` or the local `.venv/`.\\\\n\\\\n### Phase 6: Release Only With Evidence\\\\n\\\\n`M07` exercises the full workflow on a low-resource ARM64 laptop and reconciles every acceptance field. A missing provider result, skipped accessibility check, unverified restore, direct database path, or undocumented limitation keeps the release pending.\\\\n\\\\n## Ownership Model\\\\n\\\\n- The **coordinator** owns task assignment, dependency checks, integration, status, evidence, and release decisions.\\\\n- **SOL HIGH build** owns application implementation, API/storage/provider/UI changes, and targeted engineering fixes.\\\\n- **LUNA MAX QA** owns unit/API/browser/accessibility/security/performance/restore verification and regression evidence.\\\\n- **LUNA MAX docs** owns this roadmap, the detailed plan, runbooks, evidence records, and honest status wording.\\\\n- Each task uses the coordinator plus no more than three agents. Agents must work from the explicit task ID and may not silently expand scope.\\\\n\\\\n## Gates And Repair Loop\\\\n\\\\nThe coordinator uses the following loop for every milestone:\\\\n\\\\n1. Confirm all dependency IDs are completed with evidence.\\\\n2. Assign up to three agents and record the task's change summary and acceptance fields.\\\\n3. Run targeted checks, then the relevant Git/CI gates.\\\\n4. On failure, leave the task pending or in progress, record the failed evidence, create a repair ID such as `R-M03-1`, and fix the root cause.\\\\n5. Rerun the failed check plus the affected regression set. Record the environment, result, and reviewer.\\\\n6. Mark completed only when all required evidence passes; never replace missing evidence with a narrative status update.\\\\n\\\\n## Roadmap Completion Record\\\\n\\\\nUse this record when a milestone is reviewed. It is intentionally blank for implementation work until that work occurs.\\\\n\\\\n- **Task ID:** `M##`.\\\\n- **Dependencies verified:** task IDs and evidence references.\\\\n- **Status:** `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`.\\\\n- **Acceptance evidence:** test names, logs, screenshots, fixtures, checksums, or measured resource results.\\\\n- **Verification result:** environment, check, timestamp, and pass/fail.\\\\n- **Repair history:** repair IDs, root causes, fixes, and reruns.\\\\n- **Reviewer:** coordinator plus verifying agent.\\\\n\\\\n## Release Definition Of Done\\\\n\\\\nThe roadmap is complete only when `M00` through `M07` are accounted for and the planned app can demonstrate all of these outcomes:\\\\n\\\\n- User-selected Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs support both forecast horizons, with the latest five-minute input always a completed bar.\\\\n- Probabilities and magnitude intervals have explicit definitions, levels, units, timestamps, source, model/version, and data-quality context.\\\\n- SQLite retains every successful, failed, and repeated search and immutable forecast inputs/results with append-only outcomes.\\\\n- Searchable history and verified backup/restore work through the FastAPI boundary; the frontend never accesses SQLite directly.\\\\n- The dashboard is responsive and accessible, and the default deployment is secure loopback with bounded ARM64 resource use.\\\\n- The official headless `@playwright/mcp`, checked-in browser regressions, useful code comments, and Git/CI gates are present and passing.\\\\n- README, plan, and roadmap describe only behavior supported by the final evidence.\\\",\\n-                \\\"lineStart\\\": 1,\\n-                \\\"lineEnd\\\": 95,\\n-                \\\"totalLines\\\": 95,\\n-                \\\"truncated\\\": false\\n-              }\\n-            },\\n-            \\\"title\\\": \\\"MVP-ROADMAP.md\\\",\\n-            \\\"time\\\": {\\n-              \\\"start\\\": 1789063154013,\\n-              \\\"end\\\": 1789063154132\\n-            }\\n-          },\\n-          \\\"metadata\\\": {\\n-            \\\"openai\\\": {\\n-              \\\"itemId\\\": \\\"fc_09cb69de2e5decd9016aa2eff1f60887d19c678ed0b06c20af\\\"\\n-            }\\n-          },\\n-          \\\"id\\\": \\\"prt_08c79493e001jL2Y9Xnc7rFa0g\\\",\\n-          \\\"sessionID\\\": \\\"ses_f73b976e8ffekNCE6SNIanpXFb\\\",\\n-          \\\"messageID\\\": \\\"msg_08c79218c001JVCg3DC6A3z6MZ\\\"\\n-        },\\n-        {\\n-          \\\"type\\\": \\\"tool\\\",\\n-          \\\"tool\\\": \\\"read\\\",\\n-          \\\"callID\\\": \\\"call_V1HtXOXwvSUcABvt4Yivkzwt\\\",\\n-          \\\"state\\\": {\\n-            \\\"status\\\": \\\"completed\\\",\\n-            \\\"input\\\": {\\n-              \\\"filePath\\\": \\\"/home/eddie/stock_probs/AGENTS.md\\\"\\n-            },\\n-            \\\"output\\\": \\\"<path>/home/eddie/stock_probs/AGENTS.md</path>\\\\n<type>file</type>\\\\n<content>\\\\n1: # Agent Rules\\\\n2: \\\\n3: ## Repository truth\\\\n4: \\\\n5: - The tracked application material is an exploratory Python probability prototype, not the planned web app.\\\\n6: - `burry_env/` is tracked legacy dependency noise. application\\\",\\n-              \\\"prompt\\\": \\\"Act as SOL HIGH build for the stock_probs repository. You own ALL implementation writing for M01-M06, including application code, manifests/lockfiles, migrations, frontend assets, OpenCode/Playwright MCP configuration, scripts/task runner, CI, and focused developer/unit/API/browser regression tests. Do not edit MVP-PLAN.md, MVP-ROADMAP.md, AGENTS.md, or README.md; LUNA docs owns those. Do not commit or push. Read those four docs and current repo first. Do not touch tracked burry_env/ or local .venv/, and preserve unrelated work.\\\\n\\\\nImplement a development-ready, fully functional local MVP, not a sketch. Requirements: FastAPI /api/v1 is the only application-data path for the frontend; no DB path/SQL/direct SQLite in frontend. User-selected Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs. Record every submitted successful, failed, and repeated search. SQLite schema/migrations support immutable forecast inputs/results and append-only outcomes. Searchable bounded history. Verified backup/restore with integrity/checksum/safe paths and no destructive unverified promotion. Secure loopback defaults, host/origin validation as appropriate, CSP, bounded provider calls/timeouts, validation, safe exports. Both forecasts: latest completed daily close to next close; latest completed 5-minute bar to applicable close, excluding incomplete bars and respecting exchange timezone/session. Forecast output must include up/down/flat probabilities, explicit threshold probabilities, magnitude intervals in return and price units, provenance, timestamps, model version, quality/stale state. Use a simple leakage-safe empirical/EWMA-volatility-adjusted distribution suitable for ARM64 and deterministic fixtures. A historical reconstruction endpoint/view and append-only outcome route are required. Provider errors must create audit records.\\\\n\\\\nBuild a polished responsive accessible dashboard (desktop/mobile, keyboard, semantic labels, loading/error/empty/stale states, charts with textual/table equivalents) using lightweight server-served HTML/CSS/JS. All frontend fetches must target /api/v1.\\\\n\\\\nConfigure official @playwright/mcp in repo-local opencode.json as a local server, explicit --headless, --isolated, Chromium, loopback allowed origin, bounded output; pin package in tools/browser/package.json + lock if feasible. Visual design brief\\\\n\\\\nThe presentation builder should evolve Signal Ledger into a polished financial research interface:\\\\n\\\\n- Warm paper surfaces, deep ink typography, restrained rust accents, and consistent spacing.\\\\n- Clear numerical hierarchy and aligned tabular figures.\\\\n- A compact search area that keeps useful results prominent.\\\\n- Side-by-side horizon cards on desktop, stacked naturally on mobile.\\\\n- Readable probability and interval graphics with equivalent tables.\\\\n- Clearly distinguished current, stale, failed, repeated, and reconstructed states.\\\\n- Detailed provenance available without overwhelming the primary result.\\\\n- Locally served assets and a lightweight frontend.\\\\n\\\\n### Visual acceptance criteria\\\\n\\\\n- Review screenshots at **360, 390, 768, 1280, and 1440 pixels**.\\\\n- No clipped content, overlapping controls, or unintended page overflow.\\\\n- Review populated results and every important state—not only the empty screen.\\\\n- Verify contrast, keyboard focus, touch targets, zoom/reflow, and reduced motion.\\\\n- Include actual assistive-technology evidence; axe and keyboard tests alone do not establish screen-reader acceptance.\\\\n- Require a named visual reviewer to record findings and repairs.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## 5. Repeat until the `ASTRA-FINAL` record explicitly says `Accepted`; no final release or `EXP-FINAL` may precede that wording.\\\\n \\\\n ## Product Goal\\\\n \\\\n-Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF and receives two forecast views:\\\\n+Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF, confirms its company name and instrument identity, and receives two forecast views:\\\\n \\\\n 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\\\\n 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\\\\n \\\\n-Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. Every displayed result must identify its symbol, asset type, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\\\n+Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. The probability contract includes up/down/unchanged direction, `+/-1%`, `+/-3%`, `+/-5%`, and `+/-10%` return thresholds, conditional gain/loss probabilities, and 50%, 80%, and 95% return and price intervals. Every displayed result must identify its company name, symbol, asset type, instrument identity, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\\\n \\\\n-This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\\\\n+This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy. Optional dark mode and news features are not part of the contract; options trading and public hosting are out of scope.\\\\n \\\\n ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\\\\n \\\\n ### API boundary\\\\n \\\\n - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\\\n - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\\\\n - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\\\\n - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\\\\n \\\\n ### Data source and time semantics\\\\n \\\\n - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\\\\n - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\\\\n - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\\\n - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\\\n+- Yahoo Finance five-minute history has an approximate 60-day availability limitation. The provider and UI must state that archive limitation and the applicable archive/session semantics; an unavailable or stale interval is evidence to record, not a reason to fabricate a result.\\\\n \\\\n ### Persistence and auditability\\\\n \\\\n - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\\\n - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\\\n - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\\\n - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\\\n - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\\\n - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\\\n+- Reopening a saved forecast must display the immutable recorded inputs/results and must not silently recalculate. A historical cutoff reconstruction is a separately labelled fresh analysis using the data available at that cutoff, with its own as-of time, model/version, and provenance.\\\\n \\\\n ### User experience\\\\n \\\\n - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\\\n - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\\\n - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\\\n+- Historical price and return-distribution charts must have equivalent tables/text and remain understandable in every state. The distinctive Signal Ledger direction is intentional: polished tabular numeric hierarchy, clear status evidence, and restrained visual encoding rather than a generic trading dashboard.\\\\n - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\\\n-- Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\\\\n+- Accessible names, semantic structure, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and actual assistive-technology/screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish. Axe and keyboard checks do not substitute for an actual screen-reader run.\\\\n \\\\n ### Deployment and resources\\\\n \\\\n - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\\\n - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\\\n - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\\\n-- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\\\\n+- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for low-resource native x86-64 and ARM64 Linux. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe; the target is below 500 MiB normal server memory, a cached forecast under 1 second, an indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU.\\\\n - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\\\n \\\\n ## Planned Architecture\\\\n \\\\n The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\\\n \\\\n The API/application layers should remain separable:\\\\n \\\\n - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\\\n - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\\\n - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\\\n - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\\\n-- **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\\\\n+- **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, dual-architecture, and browser regression checks.\\\\n \\\\n The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\\\n \\\\n ## Forecast Contract\\\\n \\\\n The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\\\n \\\\n - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\\\n - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\\\n - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\\\n - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\\\n - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\\\n - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\\\n - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\\\n \\\\n+The evaluation record must use chronological walk-forward splits with no future leakage, compare against a documented baseline, and report Brier score, reliability/calibration, and interval coverage. Rare-event estimates must expose sample counts and uncertainty rather than implying precision from sparse observations. Historical price and return-distribution views must use the same recorded provenance and provide text/table equivalents. A saved result remains a recorded result; a historical-cutoff reconstruction is explicitly a fresh analysis.\\\\n+\\\\n The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\\\\n \\\\n+## Restored Acceptance Contract Map\\\\n+\\\\n+These requirements were omitted from a condensed milestone plan and are restored here as milestone acceptance rows. Yahoo's approximate 60-day five-minute archive limitation must be visible with archive/session semantics.\\\\n+- Saved forecasts reopen as immutable recorded results. Forecasts are informational research outputs, not investment advice or a guarantee of future prices.\\\\n \\\\n+## Eventual User Guide\\\\n+\\\\n+This is the intended user journey once the corresponding milestone evidence is accepted:\\\\n+\\\\n+1. Start the app locally and open its loopback address. Confirm the displayed source/as-of and data-quality state.\\\\n+2. Search by symbol or company name. Confirm the returned exchange, asset type, and instrument identity before submitting a forecast.\\\\n+3. Review both forecast horizons: completed-session close to next close, and latest completed five-minute bar to close. The latter must state why an in-progress bar was excluded.\\\\n+4. Read the explicit up/down/unchanged and threshold probabilities, conditional gain/loss, 50/80/95 return and price intervals, model/version, units, stale state, provider limitation, and provenance. Do not interpret a probability as a guarantee.\\\\n+5. Reopen a saved forecast to view the immutable recorded result. Use historical-cutoff reconstruction only when a separately labelled fresh analysis is wanted; it is not a rewrite or reopen of the saved result.\\\\n+6. Use history filters to find successful, failed, and repeated searches. Review historical price and return-distribution charts alongside their text/table equivalents, then append later outcomes without changing the original forecast.\\\\n+7. Export the selected records as CSV or JSON when those gates are available. Treat exported data as auditable research data, not investment advice.\\\\n+\\\\n+## Eventual Operator Guide\\\\n+\\\\n+### Install and run\\\\n+\\\\n+Use the pinned dependency manifest and the repository `Makefile`/launch documentation to create an isolated environment and perform a clean install. Do not use `burry_env/`, `.venv/`, or another local environment as a dependency declaration or release artifact. The default service binds to loopback; a broader bind is not part of the supported contract.\\\\n+\\\\n+### Data, history, and backups\\\\n+\\\\n+The server owns Yahoo Finance access and SQLite. The browser receives application data only through FastAPI `/api/v1` and never receives a database path. Operators should preserve provider/as-of and stale-data messages, keep query history unless an explicit documented policy says otherwise, observe disk/retention limits, and verify automatic due and pre-migration backups. Restore must stage and validate integrity, schema, representative counts, and trust-key state before promotion without destroying active data.\\\\n+\\\\n+Trust keys require a documented transfer, rotation, retirement, and backup lifecycle. Missing or incorrect keys must fail closed. A release gate must restore backups in both directions between native x86-64 and native ARM64; a hosted ARM runner does not replace resource measurements on the original physical low-resource laptop.\\\\n+\\\\n+### Support and resource gate\\\\n+\\\\n+Both native architectures require actual package build/clean install, `make check`, loopback startup, Node/Chromium, official headless `@playwright/mcp` application interaction, desktop/mobile browser checks, and resource evidence. The measured targets are below 500 MiB normal server memory, cached forecast under 1 second, indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU. Current x86_64 host and historical ARM64 results do not yet establish this dual-architecture gate.\\\\n+\\\\n+## Visual And Accessibility Direction\\\\n+\\\\n+The eventual interface keeps the distinctive **Signal Ledger** direction: calm, high-signal status treatment; polished tabular numeric hierarchy; charts paired with tables/text; and clear provenance instead of decorative trading noise. Every state—empty, loading, validation, success, repeated, stale, and failure—must be legible at 360, 390, 768, 1280, and 1440 CSS-pixel viewports with no overlap or overflow. Reduced motion, WCAG AA contrast/structure, visible keyboard focus, keyboard journeys, and actual assistive-technology/screen-reader runs are release evidence. Axe output and keyboard checks are useful separate checks, but neither substitutes for the actual screen-reader run.\\\\n+\\\\n+## Scope Classification\\\\n+\\\\n+- **Contract:** local Linux operation on native x86-64/amd64 and ARM64/aarch64; Yahoo stock/ETF lookup and auditable forecasts; `/api/v1` boundary; SQLite audit/history; exports; backup/restore; accessible responsive UI; official MCP/browser/CI and resource gates.\\\\n+- **Optional, not contract:** dark mode and news.\\\\n+- **Out of scope:** options trading and public hosting.\\\\n+\\\\n ## Required Future Workflow\\\\n \\\\n-All future work maximizes safe parallelism with no more than three concurrent subagents. No alias is a pass, and no later repair may reuse one of these fresh IDs for a different defect.\\\\n58: \\\\n59: ## Mandatory Delivery Workflow\\\\n60: \\\\n61: The coordinator applies this workflow to every milestone and repair. It is a sequencing rule, not permission to infer that an existing source file works.\\\\n62: \\\\n63: ### Safe build-wave ownership\\\\n64: \\\\n65: Use exactly three concurrent `SOL HIGH build` instances in each implementation or repair wave, never more than three. The coordinator records this lane manifest against the exact milestone or repair ID before work starts; the lanes cover every implementation, configuration, and test path:\\\\n66: \\\\n67: | Lane | Sole build ownership | Handoff boundary |\\\\n68: | --- | --- | --- |\\\\n69: | `SOL HIGH-A` | Transport/application: FastAPI routes, schemas, configuration, CLI, package/launch assumptions, and transport-facing tests | Versioned API contract and launch assumptions |\\\\n70: | `SOL HIGH-B` | Domain/provider/persistence: forecast semantics, Yahoo/fixture adapters, service, SQLite migrations/repositories, backup/restore, and domain/storage tests | Domain and storage contracts, fixtures, and migration assumptions |\\\\n71: | `SOL HIGH-C` | Presentation/browser/operations: static UI, browser harness, operational scripts, Make/CI/tool configuration, dependency/runtime tooling, and presentation/operations tests | UI states, browser journeys, resource limits, and operational assumptions |\\\\n72: \\\\n73: No two builders edit the same path or silently cross a lane boundary. `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `MVP-PLAN.md`, and `MVP-ROADMAP.md` are documentation-owned; `SESSION-EXPORT.md` is export-owned. Any implementation/config/test path not named in the lane manifest is assigned to A, B, or C before work starts. Builders report the exact task ID, changed paths, checks attempted, failures, and unresolved assumptions. If a dependency requires a shared edit, builders stop and hand it to the coordinator for mechanical integration; the coordinator does not author shared implementation/config/test content. The build wave is complete only after all three builder reports arrive.\\\\n74: \\\\n75: ### Ordered gates\\\\n76: \\\\n77: 1. Assign the exact `M##` or repair ID and record verified dependencies, lane ownership, and acceptance rows.\\\\n78: 2. Run the three-lane `SOL HIGH build` wave concurrently, with no more than three subagents.\\\\n79: 3. Wait for all builder reports and changed paths; do not integrate or declare a result while a report is missing.\\\\n80: 4. Run independent `LUNA MAX QA` and `LUNA MAX docs` gates only after that wait. They may run concurrently when their scopes are independent, but docs must not fill a missing QA result with an implementation claim.\\\\n81: 5. The coordinator alone integrates changes, updates status/evidence, and performs git operations. It does not implement, perform QA, or write roadmap prose.\\\\n82: 6. On any failure, skip, unavailable provider, stale-data condition, accessibility finding, restore failure, secret-review failure, connectivity loss, or missing artifact, keep the task `Pending`, `In progress`, or `Blocked`; create `R-M##-<n>`, repair the root cause, and rerun the failed and affected checks.\\\\n83: 7. Follow the canonical sequence exactly: `R-M00-1` -> `EXP-M00` -> `M01`/`EXP-M01` -> ... -> `M06`/`EXP-M06` -> `M07` QA/docs -> `ASTRA-FINAL` -> repairs/retests until `Accepted` -> `EXP-M07` -> `EXP-FINAL`. The final gate is allowed only after Astra acceptance and all repair retests.\\\\n84: \\\\n85: ### Versioned session-export gates\\\\n86: \\\\n87: Every milestone has a separately recorded export task ID: `EXP-M00`, `EXP-M01`, `EXP-M02`, `EXP-M03`, `EXP-M04`, `EXP-M05`, `EXP-M06`, or `EXP-M07`. The coordinator uses OpenCode `/export`, or a verified CLI equivalent, to overwrite exactly one tracked root artifact, `SESSION-EXPORT.md`. The export must be a full-session record containing tool calls and subagent outputs; a summary, partial transcript, or untracked local file does not satisfy the gate.\\\\n88: \\\\n89: Before commit, the export receives a documented full secret review. Commit and push the reviewed export as checkpoint SHA X; only then record external CI that explicitly tests SHA X. Preserve that CI receipt, plus the export and secret-review fields, in the next checkpoint/export; never claim SHA X contains a future CI result. The record names the export revision/commit, pushed branch, remote verification, CI result, artifact/link, UTC time, environment, and reviewer. Any failed, skipped, unavailable, or connectivity-blocked export, secret review, push, remote check, or CI check is recorded with its result and blocks acceptance. Git history supplies the version for the stable overwritten path; the export task ID supplies milestone identity. `R-M00-1` intentionally does not create, review, commit, or push the export.\\\\n90: \\\\n91: ### Independent final Astra gate\\\\n92: \\\\n93: After `M07` dependencies and its QA/docs evidence are complete, an independent GPT-6 Astra reviewer executes task `ASTRA-FINAL`. Astra must use an evidence matrix—not implementation claims—to confirm every shipped feature, every API and UI endpoint, every visible click/control, every browser journey on the supported viewports, and every persistence effect. The matrix must name the check, environment, UTC timestamp, commit, result, artifact/link, limitation, and reviewer for each row.\\\\n94: \\\\n95: Any missing, failing, skipped, unavailable, or unconfirmed row creates `R-ASTRA-<n>`. The repair goes through the same three-lane build handoff, independent QA/docs gates, and Astra retest. Repeat until the `ASTRA-FINAL` record explicitly says `Accepted`; no final release or `EXP-FINAL` may precede that wording.\\\\n96: \\\\n97: ## Product Goal\\\\n98: \\\\n99: Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF, confirms its company name and instrument identity, and receives two forecast views:\\\\n100: \\\\n101: 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\\\\n102: 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\\\\n103: \\\\n104: Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. The probability contract includes up/down/unchanged direction, `+/-1%`, `+/-3%`, `+/-5%`, and `+/-10%` return thresholds, conditional gain/loss probabilities, and 50%, 80%, and 95% return and price intervals. Every displayed result must identify its company name, symbol, asset type, instrument identity, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\\\n105: \\\\n106: This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy. Optional dark mode and news features are not part of the contract; options trading and public hosting are out of scope.\\\\n107: \\\\n108: ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\\\\n109: \\\\n110: ### API boundary\\\\n111: \\\\n112: - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\\\n113: - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\\\\n114: - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\\\\n115: - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\\\\n116: \\\\n117: ### Data source and time semantics\\\\n118: \\\\n119: - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\\\\n120: - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\\\\n121: - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\\\n122: - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\\\n123: - Yahoo Finance five-minute history has an approximate 60-day availability limitation. The provider and UI must state that archive limitation and the applicable archive/session semantics; an unavailable or stale interval is evidence to record, not a reason to fabricate a result.\\\\n124: \\\\n125: ### Persistence and auditability\\\\n126: \\\\n127: - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\\\n128: - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\\\n129: - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\\\n130: - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\\\n131: - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\\\n132: - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\\\n133: - Reopening a saved forecast must display the immutable recorded inputs/results and must not silently recalculate. A historical cutoff reconstruction is a separately labelled fresh analysis using the data available at that cutoff, with its own as-of time, model/version, and provenance.\\\\n134: \\\\n135: ### User experience\\\\n136: \\\\n137: - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\\\n138: - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\\\n139: - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\\\n140: - Historical price and return-distribution charts must have equivalent tables/text and remain understandable in every state. The distinctive Signal Ledger direction is intentional: polished tabular numeric hierarchy, clear status evidence, and restrained visual encoding rather than a generic trading dashboard.\\\\n141: - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\\\n142: - Accessible names, semantic structure, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and actual assistive-technology/screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish. Axe and keyboard checks do not substitute for an actual screen-reader run.\\\\n143: \\\\n144: ### Deployment and resources\\\\n145: \\\\n146: - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\\\n147: - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\\\n148: - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\\\n149: - Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for low-resource native x86-64 and ARM64 Linux. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe; the target is below 500 MiB normal server memory, a cached forecast under 1 second, an indexed 100,000-history query under 250 ms, and negligible idle CPU.\\\\n150: - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\\\n151: \\\\n152: ## Planned Architecture\\\\n153: \\\\n154: The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\\\n155: \\\\n156: The API/application layers should remain separable:\\\\n157: \\\\n158: - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\\\n159: - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\\\n160: - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\\\n161: - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\\\n162: - **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, dual-architecture, and browser regression checks.\\\\n163: \\\\n164: The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\\\n165: \\\\n166: ## Forecast Contract\\\\n167: \\\\n168: The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\\\n169: \\\\n170: - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\\\n171: - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\\\n172: - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\\\n173: - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\\\n174: - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\\\n175: - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\\\n176: - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\\\n177: \\\\n178: The evaluation record must use chronological walk-forward splits with no future leakage, compare against a documented baseline, and report Brier score, reliability/calibration, and interval coverage. Rare-event estimates must expose sample counts and uncertainty rather than implying precision from sparse observations. Historical price and return-distribution views must use the same recorded provenance and provide text/table equivalents. A saved result remains a recorded result; a historical-cutoff reconstruction is explicitly a fresh analysis.\\\\n179: \\\\n180: The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\\\\n181: \\\\n182: ## Restored Acceptance Contract Map\\\\n183: \\\\n184: These requirements were omitted from a condensed milestone plan and are restored here as milestone acceptance rows. They are requirements only; none is currently accepted by this documentation repair.\\\\n185: \\\\n186: | Contract requirement | Milestone acceptance row |\\\\n187: | --- | --- |\\\\n188: | Company-name lookup preserves symbol, exchange, asset type, and other instrument identity;
