You can also disable auto-reload entirely.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-### [Monthly limits](#monthly-limits)\\\\n-\\\\n-You can also set a monthly usage limit for the entire workspace and for each member of your team.\\\\n-\\\\n-For example, let’s say you set a monthly usage limit to $20, Zen will not use more than $20 in a month. But if you have auto-reload enabled, Zen might end up charging you more than $20 if your balance goes below $5.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-### [Deprecated models](#deprecated-models)\\\\n-\\\\n-Model\\\\n-\\\\n-Deprecation date\\\\n-\\\\n-GPT 5.2 Codex\\\\n-\\\\n-July 23, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-GPT 5.1 Codex\\\\n-\\\\n-July 23, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-GPT 5.1 Codex Max\\\\n-\\\\n-July 23, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-GPT 5.1 Codex Mini\\\\n-\\\\n-July 23, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-GPT 5 Codex\\\\n-\\\\n-July 23, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-Claude Opus 4.1\\\\n-\\\\n-August 5, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-Claude Sonnet 4\\\\n-\\\\n-June 15, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-Claude Haiku 3.5\\\\n-\\\\n-February 16, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-Gemini 3 Pro\\\\n-\\\\n-March 9, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-MiniMax M2.5\\\\n-\\\\n-August 5, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-MiniMax M2.1\\\\n-\\\\n-March 15, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-GLM 5\\\\n-\\\\n-May 14, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-GLM 4.7\\\\n-\\\\n-March 15, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-GLM 4.6\\\\n-\\\\n-March 15, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-Kimi K2.5\\\\n-\\\\n-August 5, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-Kimi K2 Thinking\\\\n-\\\\n-March 6, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-Kimi K2\\\\n-\\\\n-March 6, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n-Qwen3 Coder 480B\\\\n-\\\\n-February 6, 2026\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## [Privacy](#privacy)\\\\n-\\\\n-All our models are hosted in the US. Our providers follow a zero-retention policy and do not use your data for model training, with the following exceptions:\\\\n-\\\\n--   Big Pickle: During its free period, collected data may be used to improve the model.\\\\n--   MiMo-V2.5 Free: During its free period, collected data may be used to improve the model.\\\\n--   Ling 3.0 Flash Fin Free: During its free period, collected data may be used to improve the model.\\\\n--   Nemotron 3 Ultra Free (NVIDIA free endpoints): Trial use only — do not submit personal or confidential data. Your use is logged for security purposes and to improve NVIDIA products and services. The logged session data for improvement purposes is not linked to your identity or any persistent identifier. For more information about our data processing practices, see our [Privacy Policy](https://assets.ngc.nvidia.com/products/api-catalog/legal/NVIDIA%20API%20Trial%20Terms%20of%20Service.pdf). By interacting with this endpoint, you consent to our collection, recording, and use of such information and the [NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service](https://assets.ngc.nvidia.com/products/api-catalog/legal/NVIDIA%20API%20Trial%20Terms%20of%20Service.pdf).\\\\n--   Nemotron 3.5 Lightning Free (NVIDIA free endpoints): Trial use only — do not submit personal or confidential data. Your use is logged for security purposes and to improve NVIDIA products and services. The logged session data for improvement purposes is not linked to your identity or any persistent identifier. For more information about our data processing practices, see our [Privacy Policy](https://assets.ngc.nvidia.com/products/api-catalog/legal/NVIDIA%20API%20Trial%20Terms%20of%20Service.pdf). By interacting with this endpoint, you consent to our collection, recording, and use of such information and the [NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service](https://assets.ngc.nvidia.com/products/api-catalog/legal/NVIDIA%20API%20Trial%20Terms%20of%20Service.pdf).\\\\n--   OpenAI APIs: Requests are retained for 30 days in accordance with [OpenAI’s Data Policies](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/your-data).\\\\n--   Anthropic APIs: Requests are retained for 30 days in accordance with [Anthropic’s Data Policies](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/data-usage).\\\\n--   Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor Free: Heavily discounted token pricing in exchange for permission to use your prompts and completions to train future Meta models. [Learn more](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits#contributor-tier).\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## [For Teams](#for-teams)\\\\n-\\\\n-Zen also works great for teams. You can invite teammates, assign roles, curate the models your team uses, and more.\\\\n-\\\\n-Note\\\\n-\\\\n-Workspaces are currently free for teams as a part of the beta.\\\\n-\\\\n-Managing your workspace is currently free for teams as a part of the beta. We’ll be sharing more details on the pricing soon.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-### [Roles](#roles)\\\\n-\\\\n-You can invite teammates to your workspace and assign roles:\\\\n-\\\\n--   **Admin**: Manage models, members, API keys, and billing\\\\n--   **Member**: Manage only their own API keys\\\\n-\\\\n-Admins can also set monthly spending limits for each member to keep costs under control.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-### [Model access](#model-access)\\\\n-\\\\n-Admins can enable or disable specific models for the workspace. Requests made to a disabled model will return an error.\\\\n-\\\\n-This is useful for cases where you want to disable the use of a model that collects data.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-### [Bring your own key](#bring-your-own-key)\\\\n-\\\\n-You can use your own OpenAI or Anthropic API keys while still accessing other models in Zen.\\\\n-\\\\n-When you use your own keys, tokens are billed directly by the provider, not by Zen.\\\\n-\\\\n-For example, your organization might already have a key for OpenAI or Anthropic and you want to use that instead of the one that Zen provides.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## [Goals](#goals)\\\\n-\\\\n-We created OpenCode Zen to:\\\\n-\\\\n-1.  **Benchmark** the best models/providers for coding agents.\\\\n-2.  Have access to the **highest quality** options and not downgrade performance or route to cheaper providers.\\\\n-3.  Pass along any **price drops** by selling at cost; so the only markup is to cover our processing fees.\\\\n-4.  Have **no lock-in** by allowing you to use it with any other coding agent. And always let you use any other provider with OpenCode as well.\\\\n-\\\\n-[Edit page](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/edit/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/zen.mdx)[Found a bug? Open an issue](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/new)[Join our Discord community](https://opencode.ai/discord) Select language EnglishالعربيةBosanskiDanskDeutschEspañolFrançaisItaliano日本語한국어Norsk BokmålPolskiPortuguês (Brasil)РусскийไทยTürkçe简体中文繁體中文 \\\\n-\\\\n-© [Anomaly](https://anoma.ly)\\\\n-\\\\n-Last updated: Sep 10, 2026\\\\n-```\\\\n-\\\\n-**Tool: glob**\\\\n-\\\\n-**Input:**\\\\n-```json\\\\n-{\\\\n-  \\\\\\\"pattern\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"*models*\\\\\\\",\\\\n-  \\\\\\\"path\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"/home/eddie/.cache/opencode\\\\\\\"\\\\n-}\\\\n-```\\\\n-\\\\n-**Output:**\\\\n-```\\\\n-/home/eddie/.cache/opencode/models.json\\\\n-```\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## Assistant (Plan · GPT-6 Astra · 268.8s)\\\\n-\\\\n-_Thinking:_\\\\n-\\\\n-**Preparing model search**\\\\n-\\\\n-_Thinking:_\\\\n-\\\\n-**Defining workstream ownership**\\\\n-\\\\n-_Thinking:_\\\\n-\\\\n-**Clarifying closed-market state**\\\\n-\\\\n-_Thinking:_\\\\n-\\\\n-**Checking ETF calendar**\\\\n-\\\\n-_Thinking:_\\\\n-\\\\n-**Checking price semantics**\\\\n-\\\\n-_Thinking:_\\\\n-\\\\n-**Verifying version pin**\\\\n-\\\\n-_Thinking:_\\\\n-\\\\n-**Clarifying acceptance semantics**\\\\n-\\\\n-_Thinking:_\\\\n-\\\\n-**Preparing docs package**\\\\n-\\\\n-_Thinking:_\\\\n-\\\\n-**Recording SOL access status**\\\\n-\\\\n-# Full MVP plan\\\\n-\\\\n-**Build a fully functional local stock-probability application, delivered through a coordinator and up to three SOL subagents per task: Build, QA, and Documentation.**\\\\n-\\\\n-The application will use Yahoo Finance data, expose all application data through an API, preserve searchable history in SQLite, and require **headless Playwright MCP acceptance testing**.\\\\n-\\\\n-The sections below form the proposed contents of `MVP-PLAN.md` and `MVP-ROADMAP.md`.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-# `MVP-PLAN.md`\\\\n-\\\\n-## 1. Product objective\\\\n-\\\\n-The application must answer:\\\\n-\\\\n-> “Using the information available at this cutoff, what is the estimated probability this stock rises or falls by the target close, and what sizes of move are plausible?”\\\\n-\\\\n-### Required MVP capabilities\\\\n-\\\\n-| ID | Requirement |\\\\n-|---|---|\\\\n-| R01 | Search by company name or ticker and freely switch between stocks and ETFs |\\\\n-| R02 | Use the most recent eligible Yahoo Finance data, with visible timestamps and freshness |\\\\n-| R03 | Produce close-to-close forecasts |\\\\n-| R04 | Produce intraday-to-close forecasts |\\\\n-| R05 | Display direction probabilities, movement thresholds, conditional gains/losses, and prediction intervals |\\\\n-| R06 | Provide a polished, responsive dashboard with historical charts |\\\\n-| R07 | Route all frontend application-data access through the API |\\\\n-| R08 | Record and search every submitted query, including repeated and failed requests |\\\\n-| R09 | Preserve original forecasts, their inputs, and subsequent outcomes |\\\\n-| R10 | Provide verified SQLite backups and restoration |\\\\n-| R11 | Meet security, correctness, and laptop-performance acceptance criteria |\\\\n-| R12 | Pass Playwright MCP browser acceptance and automated regression tests |\\\\n-| R13 | Provide reproducible setup, documentation, CI, and published Git revisions |\\\\n-\\\\n-**Both forecast modes belong in the completed MVP.** A daily-only dashboard is an intermediate milestone.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 2. Verified environment and constraints\\\\n-\\\\n-| Component | Observed environment |\\\\n-|---|---|\\\\n-| Architecture | ARM64 / `aarch64` |\\\\n-| CPU | 8 cores, Cortex-A55 and Cortex-A76 |\\\\n-| Memory | 6.5 GiB |\\\\n-| Swap | None |\\\\n-| Workspace filesystem | 10 GiB total; approximately 5.9 GiB free during inspection |\\\\n-| OS | Debian 12 |\\\\n-| Python | 3.11.2 |\\\\n-| SQLite | 3.40.1 with full-text search support |\\\\n-| Node.js | Not currently available on `PATH` |\\\\n-| Git remote | `https://github.com/eddiesoz/stock_probs.git` |\\\\n-\\\\n-The repository currently contains prototype scripts, including a broken Yahoo Finance script, and a committed Python virtual environment.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Design implications\\\\n-\\\\n-- One application service and one SQLite database.\\\\n-- Bounded network concurrency.\\\\n-- Incremental data acquisition and caching.\\\\n-- Serial browser testing on the laptop.\\\\n-- Controlled backup and diagnostic-artifact retention.\\\\n-- Project-local, locked development dependencies.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 3. SOL subagent orchestration\\\\n-\\\\n-### Coordinator\\\\n-\\\\n-The primary agent owns:\\\\n-\\\\n-- Task decomposition and dependency order.\\\\n-- Acceptance criteria and file ownership.\\\\n-- Dispatching and resuming subagents.\\\\n-- Resolving disagreements between Build and QA.\\\\n-- Roadmap status and evidence tracking.\\\\n-- Git staging, commits, pushes, and release verification.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Three available SOL roles\\\\n-\\\\n-| Role | Responsibilities | Ownership |\\\\n-|---|---|---|\\\\n-| **`sol-build`** | Implement application behavior, migrations, integrations, and focused developer tests; repair QA findings | Assigned application/configuration files and unit/integration tests |\\\\n-| **`sol-qa`** | Independently verify requirements, review changes, maintain acceptance tests, operate Playwright MCP, and report defects | Acceptance tests and QA evidence; application changes return to Build |\\\\n-| **`sol-docs`** | Document verified setup, API behavior, model behavior, operational procedures, and changes | Assigned documentation files |\\\\n-\\\\n-All three profiles will explicitly select **GPT-5.6 Sol** using the verified identifier for the authenticated provider.\\\\n-\\\\n-OpenCode documents `opencode/gpt-5.6-sol` for its Zen provider. The current local configuration contains no SOL role profiles, so model availability and actual subagent model selection must be verified during bootstrap.[1]\\\\n-\\\\n-### Orchestration limits\\\\n-\\\\n-- Up to **three subagents per task**, one per role.\\\\n-- At most three active subagents across the project initially.\\\\n-- One implementation workstream at a time on this laptop.\\\\n-- Reuse the same role sessions during repairs.\\\\n-- Subagents do not create additional subagents.\\\\n-- Only the coordinator performs Git publication and changes acceptance status.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Parallel work and handoff\\\\n-\\\\n-At task start:\\\\n-\\\\n-- Build implements.\\\\n-- QA prepares independent acceptance cases and fixtures.\\\\n-- Documentation prepares the relevant document structure.\\\\n-\\\\n-After Build supplies a stable handoff:\\\\n-\\\\n-- Build pauses changes to the files under verification.\\\\n-- QA tests that specific source revision.\\\\n-- Documentation checks the actual implementation and verified commands.\\\\n-- QA findings return to Build.\\\\n-- Any behavior change invalidates the affected acceptance evidence.\\\\n-\\\\n-Only QA controls the acceptance browser during a verification session. Shared files, such as manifests and the roadmap, have one designated writer.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Task packet\\\\n-\\\\n-Every delegated task receives:\\\\n-\\\\n-```text\\\\n-Task ID and objective\\\\n-Requirement IDs\\\\n-Dependencies and relevant design decisions\\\\n-Assigned files\\\\n-Acceptance criteria\\\\n-Required verification commands and MCP journeys\\\\n-Expected outputs\\\\n-Known constraints\\\\n-```\\\\n-\\\\n-Every role returns a concise report with changed files, evidence, unresolved issues, and handoff instructions.\\\\n-\\\\n-**A Build agent’s completion claim is not sufficient for acceptance.**\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 4. Application architecture\\\\n-\\\\n-```text\\\\n-Browser\\\\n-  ├── HTML/CSS/JavaScript\\\\n-  └── HTTP requests to /api/v1/*\\\\n-                 │\\\\n-                 ▼\\\\n-              FastAPI\\\\n-                 │\\\\n-                 ▼\\\\n-         Application services\\\\n-          ├── Yahoo adapter\\\\n-          ├── Forecast engine\\\\n-          ├── Outcome evaluation\\\\n-          └── Database repository\\\\n-                       │\\\\n-                       ▼\\\\n-                     SQLite\\\\n-```\\\\n-\\\\n-### Stack\\\\n-\\\\n-| Layer | Technology |\\\\n-|---|---|\\\\n-| Backend | FastAPI, one Uvicorn worker |\\\\n-| Frontend | Jinja2 page shells, CSS, small JavaScript modules |\\\\n-| Charts | Locally served Chart.js |\\\\n-| Market data | yfinance behind an application-owned adapter |\\\\n-| Numerical work | NumPy/pandas, SciPy where useful |\\\\n-| Trading schedules | `exchange_calendars` |\\\\n-| Database | Python `sqlite3` |\\\\n-| Python dependencies | `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` |\\\\n-| Browser tooling | Project-local npm package and lockfile |\\\\n-| Agent browser testing | Official Playwright MCP server |\\\\n-| Regression tests | pytest and Playwright Test |\\\\n-| Code checks | Ruff, mypy, dependency vulnerability checks |\\\\n-\\\\n-### Mandatory API boundary\\\\n-\\\\n-The frontend obtains forecasts, prices, query history, exports, and backup status through the API.\\\\n-\\\\n-SQL, database connections, provider calls, and database files belong to the backend. Database and backup directories are outside publicly served paths.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 5. API contract\\\\n-\\\\n-| Endpoint | Responsibility |\\\\n-|---|---|\\\\n-| `POST /api/v1/searches` | Record and execute a company/ticker search |\\\\n-| `POST /api/v1/forecasts` | Validate a forecast request, obtain inputs, calculate, and persist |\\\\n-| `GET /api/v1/forecasts/{id}` | Return an original saved forecast |\\\\n-| `GET /api/v1/history` | Search and paginate submitted queries |\\\\n-| `GET /api/v1/instruments/{id}/prices` | Return historical price data |\\\\n-| `GET /api/v1/exports` | Export selected records through validated filters |\\\\n-| `GET /api/v1/backups/status` | Return backup status |\\\\n-| `GET /api/v1/health` | Support readiness checks |\\\\n-\\\\n-Forecast responses include:\\\\n-\\\\n-- Instrument identity, exchange, and currency.\\\\n-- Requested mode and effective mode.\\\\n-- Reference price and observation timestamp.\\\\n-- Data-fetch timestamp and freshness.\\\\n-- Target session and close time.\\\\n-- Probabilities, thresholds, and prediction intervals.\\\\n-- Sample size and data-quality status.\\\\n-- Model/configuration version.\\\\n-- Saved forecast identifier.\\\\n-\\\\n-Errors use consistent codes and readable messages. Pagination, query sizes, and sorting are bounded and validated.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 6. Yahoo Finance data pipeline\\\\n-\\\\n-```text\\\\n-Record request\\\\n-  → Resolve instrument\\\\n-  → Check cache and market schedule\\\\n-  → Fetch eligible data\\\\n-  → Validate and normalize\\\\n-  → Save forecast input snapshot\\\\n-  → Calculate forecast\\\\n-  → Persist result\\\\n-  → Return API response\\\\n-```\\\\n-\\\\n-### Data handling\\\\n-\\\\n-- Retrieve daily history on demand, up to ten years where available.\\\\n-- Retrieve five-minute history for intraday analysis.\\\\n-- Store market-observation time separately from download time.\\\\n-- Preserve exchange timezone, currency, and corporate actions.\\\\n-- Exclude incomplete bars from completed-period calculations.\\\\n-- Identify missing sessions rather than treating gaps as ordinary one-day returns.\\\\n-- Verify the price-adjustment policy with split and dividend fixtures.\\\\n-- Preserve genuine large moves while identifying corrupt or inconsistent data.\\\\n-- Resolve the exchange calendar explicitly; unsupported schedules produce a clear status.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Freshness and failure behavior\\\\n-\\\\n-- Refresh daily data when another session may have completed.\\\\n-- Refresh intraday data at bounded intervals while relevant.\\\\n-- Pause frontend polling when the page is hidden.\\\\n-- Coalesce duplicate in-flight provider requests.\\\\n-- Apply timeouts and limited backoff.\\\\n-- Preserve cached results with their actual timestamps.\\\\n-- Backfill available gaps when the laptop resumes.\\\\n-\\\\n-Yahoo five-minute history is limited to approximately 60 calendar days in yfinance’s implementation. The local archive will grow as data is collected; gaps beyond the provider’s retention remain identifiable.[2]\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 7. Forecast definitions and model\\\\n-\\\\n-### A. Close-to-close\\\\n-\\\\n-**Reference:** the latest completed trading session’s close.\\\\n-\\\\n-**Target:** the next trading session’s close.\\\\n-\\\\n-The initial model will compare:\\\\n-1. An empirical historical distribution.\\\\n-2. A volatility-adjusted historical distribution.\\\\n-\\\\n-The volatility-adjusted model:\\\\n-\\\\n-- Calculates historical returns.\\\\n-- Estimates volatility causally.\\\\n-- Standardizes historical shocks.\\\\n-- Rescales those shocks to the current volatility estimate.\\\\n-- Derives all probabilities and intervals from one consistent distribution.\\\\n-\\\\n-Filtered historical simulation is suitable for a lightweight numerical implementation, but its quality depends on the volatility estimate and available history.[3]\\\\n-\\\\n-### B. Intraday-to-close\\\\n-\\\\n-**Reference:** the newest eligible completed five-minute bar.\\\\n-\\\\n-**Target:** the upcoming regular-session close.\\\\n-\\\\n-Use historical returns from comparable intraday cutoffs to their session closes, respecting exchange-local time and session type.\\\\n-\\\\n-When no fresh eligible regular-session observation exists, show a closed-market or stale-data state and identify the available daily forecast.\\\\n-\\\\n-Intraday sample sizes are smaller. Minimum-data criteria and uncertainty must be visible, especially for rare large moves.\\\\n-\\\\n-### C. Outputs\\\\n-\\\\n-- Probability of rising, falling, or remaining unchanged.\\\\n-- Median predicted percentage move.\\\\n-- Conditional median gain and conditional median loss.\\\\n-- 50%, 80%, and 95% prediction intervals.\\\\n-- Initial thresholds of ±1%, ±3%, ±5%, and ±10%.\\\\n-- Equivalent price levels in the instrument’s currency.\\\\n-\\\\n-These describe outcomes **at the target close**. Intraday barrier-touch probabilities would require a separately defined model.\\\\n-\\\\n-### D. Historical reconstruction\\\\n-\\\\n-The interface distinguishes:\\\\n-\\\\n-- **Saved forecast:** the result actually recorded at that time.\\\\n-- **Historical reconstruction:** a calculation performed later using a historical cutoff.\\\\n-\\\\n-Yahoo can revise historical data. Saved input snapshots establish what this application used; a later reconstruction cannot establish exactly what Yahoo originally served.\\\\n-\\\\n-### E. Model evaluation\\\\n-\\\\n-Use chronological walk-forward evaluation and a separate final evaluation period.\\\\n-\\\\n-Report:\\\\n-- Direction and threshold Brier scores.\\\\n-- Reliability plots.\\\\n-- Prediction-interval coverage.\\\\n-- Baseline comparisons.\\\\n-- Sample counts and evaluation dates.\\\\n-\\\\n-No future prices, current retrospective metadata, or future corporate-action information may enter historical features improperly.\\\\n-\\\\n-Volatility adjustment primarily affects move magnitude and tail risk. Additional directional models should be introduced only after demonstrating value in out-of-sample evaluation.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 8. Frontend experience\\\\n-\\\\n-### Dashboard\\\\n-\\\\n-- Company/ticker search with identity confirmation.\\\\n-- Forecast-mode selection.\\\\n-- Historical cutoff controls.\\\\n-- Reference price, target close, and freshness.\\\\n-- Direction-probability cards.\\\\n-- Threshold table.\\\\n-- Prediction-interval and distribution displays.\\\\n-- Historical-price chart.\\\\n-- Model and sample-size details.\\\\n-\\\\n-### History\\\\n-\\\\n-- Search by original text, company, and symbol.\\\\n-- Filter by date, mode, and status.\\\\n-- Reopen original results.\\\\n-- Compare forecasts with observed outcomes.\\\\n-- Start a fresh analysis from a previous query.\\\\n-- Export CSV/JSON.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Design acceptance\\\\n-\\\\n-- Responsive desktop and narrow-screen layouts.\\\\n-- Keyboard-accessible controls.\\\\n-- Readable contrast and typography.\\\\n-- Optional dark mode.\\\\n-- Numerical summaries for charts.\\\\n-- Clear loading, error, empty, stale-data, and insufficient-history states.\\\\n-\\\\n-Charts are downsampled for rendering while calculations retain full eligible data.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 9. SQLite persistence and backups\\\\n-\\\\n-### Core records\\\\n-\\\\n-| Record | Contents |\\\\n-|---|---|\\\\n-| Instruments | Canonical symbol, company, exchange, currency, timezone |\\\\n-| Market bars | Daily/intraday OHLCV, actions, timestamps, provenance |\\\\n-| Queries | Original input, parameters, timestamps, status, failure information |\\\\n-| Input snapshots | Immutable, compressed, deduplicated forecast inputs |\\\\n-| Forecasts | Saved results, reference/target times, model version |\\\\n-| Outcomes | Observed returns and scoring results |\\\\n-\\\\n-Every submitted search, analysis, reconstruction, and refresh is recorded. Deliberately repeated submissions remain distinct. Autocomplete keystrokes are interface activity rather than submitted queries.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Database behavior\\\\n-\\\\n-- Explicit transactions and foreign keys.\\\\n-- Short writes; provider calls outside transactions.\\\\n-- Thread-owned connections.\\\\n-- Busy timeout.\\\\n-- Versioned SQL migrations.\\\\n-- Indexed filters and full-text search.\\\\n-- No automatic expiry of query history.\\\\n-\\\\n-Start with rollback-journal mode. This suits the workload and avoids relying on WAL behavior in the installed SQLite version, which falls within the documented WAL-reset issue’s affected range.[4]\\\\n-\\\\n-### Backup acceptance\\\\n-\\\\n-- Automatic backup when due while the app is running.\\\\n-- Backup before migrations.\\\\n-- Manual backup command.\\\\n-- SQLite online backup API.\\\\n-- Integrity checks before marking a backup successful.\\\\n-- Configurable destination, retention, and disk limits.\\\\n-- Restore while the application is stopped.\\\\n-- Browser verification of restored history.\\\\n-\\\\n-Git stores source revisions. SQLite backups preserve application data.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 10. Security and performance\\\\n-\\\\n-### Security\\\\n-\\\\n-- Bind to `127.0.0.1`.\\\\n-- Validate Host/Origin and protect state-changing requests.\\\\n-- Use parameterized SQL and allowlisted sort fields.\\\\n-- Validate symbol syntax, input lengths, dates, and thresholds.\\\\n-- Escape user/provider text.\\\\n-- Serve scripts locally under a restrictive Content Security Policy.\\\\n-- Keep databases, backups, logs, secrets, and caches outside static paths.\\\\n-- Use restrictive data-file permissions.\\\\n-- Sanitize spreadsheet exports.\\\\n-- Pin dependencies and run vulnerability checks.\\\\n-- Keep restore operations in the local CLI.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Performance targets\\\\n-\\\\n-Measure on this laptop:\\\\n-\\\\n-| Measurement | Proposed target |\\\\n-|---|---|\\\\n-| Normal application-server memory | Below 500 MiB |\\\\n-| Cached single-symbol forecast | Below one second |\\\\n-| Indexed history search on 100,000-query fixture | Below 250 ms |\\\\n-| Idle behavior | Negligible background CPU consumption |\\\\n-\\\\n-Network latency and browser-test resource usage are recorded separately.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 11. Playwright MCP acceptance\\\\n-\\\\n-### Setup\\\\n-\\\\n-Use the official **`@playwright/mcp`** server through OpenCode’s local MCP integration.\\\\n-\\\\n-- Install a supported ARM64 Node.js LTS runtime.\\\\n-- Pin MCP and browser-test dependencies under `tools/browser/`.\\\\n-- Register the server in `opencode.json`.\\\\n-- Configure headless Chromium explicitly.\\\\n-- Use isolated browser profiles and a dedicated acceptance database.\\\\n-- Validate browser/tool compatibility on ARM.\\\\n-- Capture session evidence and bounded diagnostic artifacts.\\\\n-- Restart OpenCode after configuration changes.\\\\n-\\\\n-Playwright MCP is headed by default, making explicit headless configuration important.[5]\\\\n-\\\\n-### QA ownership\\\\n-\\\\n-`sol-qa` operates the MCP browser during acceptance. The coordinator verifies that the tools are actually available to that subagent and that the selected model is SOL.\\\\n-\\\\n-MCP unavailability or browser-launch failure blocks the relevant gate.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Test path\\\\n-\\\\n-```text\\\\n-SOL QA agent\\\\n-  → Playwright MCP\\\\n-  → Headless Chromium\\\\n-  → Real frontend\\\\n-  → Real API\\\\n-  → Real application services\\\\n-  → Real temporary SQLite database\\\\n-```\\\\n-\\\\n-Deterministic tests substitute data at the Yahoo adapter boundary. Browser/API/database behavior remains real.\\\\n-\\\\n-Final live-data checks use the actual Yahoo adapter.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Browser acceptance matrix\\\\n-\\\\n-| ID | Required behavior |\\\\n-|---|---|\\\\n-| B01 | Search by company name and select the correct instrument |\\\\n-| B02 | Switch symbols without mixing results or history |\\\\n-| B03 | Complete a daily forecast with correct displayed results |\\\\n-| B04 | Complete an intraday forecast with correct reference and target times |\\\\n-| B05 | Display populated charts, thresholds, and intervals |\\\\n-| B06 | Run and correctly label historical reconstruction |\\\\n-| B07 | Find successful, failed, and repeated queries |\\\\n-| B08 | Restart and reopen an original forecast |\\\\n-| B09 | Refresh data without changing an earlier saved result |\\\\n-| B10 | Handle invalid symbols, missing data, rate limits, and stale data |\\\\n-| B11 | Export and verify CSV/JSON contents |\\\\n-| B12 | Restore a backup and retrieve restored history through the browser |\\\\n-| B13 | Operate core flows by keyboard and at narrow viewport widths |\\\\n-| B14 | Confirm API-mediated data access and inaccessible database files |\\\\n-| B15 | Complete real-Yahoo daily and intraday user journeys |\\\\n-| B16 | Identify uncaught browser errors and unexpected external dependencies |\\\\n-\\\\n-Successful data-rich scenarios must produce numerical forecasts. Error-state handling alone cannot satisfy forecasting acceptance.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Automated regression tests\\\\n-\\\\n-Alongside MCP acceptance:\\\\n-- Python pytest covers numerical, API, and database behavior.\\\\n-- Checked-in Playwright Test scenarios run in CI.\\\\n-- MCP-driven QA covers interactive acceptance and diagnosis.\\\\n-\\\\n-**Both recorded MCP acceptance and automated regression checks are required.**\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 12. Correctness tests\\\\n-\\\\n-Highest-priority tests include:\\\\n-\\\\n-1. Appending future prices cannot change an earlier forecast.\\\\n-2. Yahoo cache updates cannot alter saved results.\\\\n-3. Larger downside thresholds cannot have higher exceedance probabilities.\\\\n-4. Up/down/unchanged probabilities sum to one.\\\\n-5. Prediction intervals are ordered and use the displayed reference price.\\\\n-6. Splits and currency-unit changes do not become artificial crashes.\\\\n-7. Incomplete bars are excluded.\\\\n-8. Session gaps do not become ordinary daily returns.\\\\n-9. Intraday evaluation groups observations by session.\\\\n-10. History survives restart and restore.\\\\n-11. Interrupted and failed requests remain identifiable.\\\\n-12. API validation and frontend/export handling resist injection.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 13. Repository layout and commands\\\\n-\\\\n-### Proposed layout\\\\n-\\\\n-```text\\\\n-MVP-PLAN.md\\\\n-MVP-ROADMAP.md\\\\n-AGENTS.md\\\\n-README.md\\\\n-opencode.json\\\\n-pyproject.toml\\\\n-uv.lock\\\\n-Makefile\\\\n-\\\\n-.opencode/agents/\\\\n-  sol-build.md\\\\n-  sol-qa.md\\\\n-  sol-docs.md\\\\n-\\\\n-src/stock_probs/\\\\n-  app.py\\\\n-  cli.py\\\\n-  services.py\\\\n-  db.py\\\\n-  providers/\\\\n-  forecasting/\\\\n-  templates/\\\\n-  static/\\\\n-\\\\n-migrations/\\\\n-tests/\\\\n-tools/browser/\\\\n-docs/\\\\n-legacy/\\\\n-.github/workflows/\\\\n-```\\\\n-\\\\n-`AGENTS.md` will reference the plan and roadmap and contain only verified commands, boundaries, and repository-specific pitfalls.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Commands to implement\\\\n-\\\\n-| Command | Purpose |\\\\n-|---|---|\\\\n-| `make setup` | Install locked development dependencies |\\\\n-| `make browser-install` | Install compatible Chromium and system prerequisites |\\\\n-| `make dev` | Start the local application |\\\\n-| `make check` | Format check, lint, typecheck, unit/API tests |\\\\n-| `make browser-test` | Run deterministic browser regressions |\\\\n-| `make acceptance` | Run deterministic acceptance, including restore tests |\\\\n-| `make live-smoke` | Run explicit real-Yahoo verification |\\\\n-| `make release-check` | Verify release evidence and required checks |\\\\n-\\\\n-MCP browser journeys are performed by QA through the configured tools. A shell command passing does not imply those journeys have occurred.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-# `MVP-ROADMAP.md`\\\\n-\\\\n-## 14. Milestones and commit gates\\\\n-\\\\n-All milestones are currently pending.\\\\n-\\\\n-| ID | Deliverables | Dependencies | Acceptance gate |\\\\n-|---|---|---|---|\\\\n-| **M00 — Plan and orchestration** | Save plan/roadmap; create compact instructions and SOL profiles; verify model routing | Editing enabled | Configuration validates; roles resolve to SOL; ownership and delegation limits established |\\\\n-| **M01 — Foundation** | Package structure, lockfiles, task runner, Git ignores, prototype archive, development prerequisites | M00 | Reproducible ARM setup; imports work; tracked-file review; GitHub access verified |\\\\n-| **M02 — Browser infrastructure** | Playwright MCP, headless Chromium, QA tool access, isolated fixtures, CI browser smoke | M01 | QA performs an actual MCP browser interaction; automated browser smoke passes |\\\\n-| **M03 — Persistence** | Schema, migrations, query recording, snapshots, backup/restore | M01 | Restart, interruption, immutability, integrity, and restore tests pass |\\\\n-| **M04 — API** | Validated contracts, pagination, repository integration, error responses, secure defaults | M03 | API/security tests pass; public database access fails |\\\\n-| **M05 — Yahoo integration** | Search, retrieval, normalization, caching, calendars, freshness | M04 | Provider fixtures pass; real adapter smoke recorded |\\\\n-| **M06 — Daily forecasting** | Baselines, volatility-adjusted distribution, reconstruction, outcomes, evaluation | M05 | Numerical/leakage tests pass; evaluation report produced |\\\\n-| **M07 — Dashboard and history** | Daily UI, charts, search history, exports, backup status | M02, M06 | Applicable browser scenarios pass through MCP and regression tests |\\\\n-| **M08 — Intraday** | Intraday archive, cutoff matching, model, target-session handling, UI | M05, M07 | Intraday correctness tests and MCP acceptance pass |\\\\n-| **M09 — Full acceptance** | Responsive/keyboard checks, security audit, performance measurements, restore drill | M08 | All deterministic requirements accepted on laptop and CI |\\\\n-| **M10 — Release** | Fresh-install verification, live journeys, final documentation, Git publication | M09 | Both modes pass live verification; evidence matches source; remote revision/tag verified |\\\\n-\\\\n-M00 is the coordinator’s bootstrap task. Once the profiles are loaded, the Build/QA/Documentation pattern applies to subsequent work.\\\\n-\\\\n-Each milestone is divided into small tasks before delegation.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 15. Task states and evidence\\\\n-\\\\n-### States\\\\n-\\\\n-```text\\\\n-pending\\\\n-  → in_progress\\\\n-  → verifying\\\\n-  → accepted\\\\n-  → published\\\\n-```\\\\n-\\\\n-Failures return work to implementation. Missing external prerequisites produce `blocked`.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Required task record\\\\n-\\\\n-```text\\\\n-Task ID:\\\\n-Requirement IDs:\\\\n-Acceptance criteria:\\\\n-Dependencies:\\\\n-Build / QA / Documentation assignments:\\\\n-Assigned files:\\\\n-Status:\\\\n-Verification commands:\\\\n-MCP scenarios:\\\\n-Tested source revision or working-tree identifier:\\\\n-Observed results:\\\\n-Artifact/report locations:\\\\n-Outstanding defects:\\\\n-Published checkpoint and CI URL:\\\\n-```\\\\n-\\\\n-The coordinator owns status changes. Documentation may prepare evidence summaries, but acceptance requires QA results.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 16. Orchestrated acceptance loop\\\\n-\\\\n-### Step 1 — Select and define\\\\n-\\\\n-The coordinator:\\\\n-- Selects a ready task.\\\\n-- Confirms dependencies.\\\\n-- Defines observable acceptance criteria.\\\\n-- Assigns file ownership.\\\\n-- Dispatches up to three SOL roles.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Step 2 — Build and prepare\\\\n-\\\\n-- Build implements.\\\\n-- QA develops independent verification cases.\\\\n-- Documentation prepares relevant updates.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Step 3 — Stable handoff\\\\n-\\\\n-Build reports:\\\\n-- Files changed.\\\\n-- Implemented behavior.\\\\n-- Developer checks performed.\\\\n-- Known limitations.\\\\n-\\\\n-Changes to the verification target pause.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Step 4 — Independent QA\\\\n-\\\\n-QA:\\\\n-- Reviews the implementation against requirements.\\\\n-- Runs focused tests.\\\\n-- Exercises applicable flows through Playwright MCP.\\\\n-- Inspects API/network behavior, browser errors, and persistence.\\\\n-- Returns pass/fail findings with evidence.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Step 5 — Repair\\\\n-\\\\n-If QA fails:\\\\n-- Coordinator creates explicit defect tasks.\\\\n-- Build repairs the root cause.\\\\n-- Documentation adjusts affected descriptions.\\\\n-- QA reruns affected checks and the required regression gate.\\\\n-\\\\n-An unexplained intermittent pass is not sufficient. Repeated failures without a new diagnosis become a documented blocker rather than an endless blind retry loop.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Step 6 — Documentation verification\\\\n-\\\\n-Documentation confirms:\\\\n-- Setup commands execute as documented.\\\\n-- API behavior matches actual responses.\\\\n-- Model terminology matches implementation.\\\\n-- Backup and restore procedures match tested behavior.\\\\n-- No unfinished functionality is described as complete.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Step 7 — Accept and publish\\\\n-\\\\n-The coordinator:\\\\n-1. Reviews QA and documentation evidence.\\\\n-2. Inspects Git status, diff, and recent commits.\\\\n-3. Stages intended files.\\\\n-4. Commits the checkpoint.\\\\n-5. Pushes it.\\\\n-6. Verifies the remote revision and CI.\\\\n-7. Marks the checkpoint published.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Step 8 — Continue\\\\n-\\\\n-Advance to the next ready task. Regressions reopen affected tasks.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 17. Git and CI workflow\\\\n-\\\\n-Repository: [`eddiesoz/stock_probs`](https://github.com/eddiesoz/stock_probs).\\\\n-\\\\n-### Foundation work\\\\n-\\\\n-- Verify remote state and write access.\\\\n-- Install/authenticate GitHub CLI as needed.\\\\n-- Untrack virtual environments while preserving local installations.\\\\n-- Exclude databases, backups, caches, browser binaries, dependencies, secrets, and generated artifacts.\\\\n-- Preserve the prototype implementation under `legacy/`.\\\\n-\\\\n-### Checkpoint policy\\\\n-\\\\n-- Coordinator alone stages, commits, and pushes.\\\\n-- Each checkpoint includes implementation, tests, and verified documentation.\\\\n-- Browser-facing checkpoints require MCP evidence and passing browser regressions.\\\\n-- CI failures reopen the relevant milestone.\\\\n-- Release tags identify the accepted source version.\\\\n-\\\\n-Source-control publication and database backups are verified separately.\\\\n-\\\\n----\\\\n-\\\\n-## 18. Final definition of done\\\\n-\\\\n-The MVP is complete only when:\\\\n-\\\\n-- Every requirement has an accepted task and recorded evidence.\\\\n-- Both forecast modes work with sufficient-data inputs.\\\\n-- User-selected stocks and ETFs work without hardcoded application dependencies.\\\\n-- Frontend data access passes through the API.\\\\n-- Query history is searchable and survives restart.\\\\n-- Saved forecasts and their inputs remain immutable.\\\\n-- Backup restoration is demonstrated through the application.\\\\n-- Playwright MCP acceptance is completed by QA.\\\\n-- Automated checks pass on the laptop and in CI.\\\\n-- Real Yahoo end-to-end verification succeeds.\\\\n-- Security and resource results are documented.\\\\n-- Fresh setup works from the committed instructions.\\\\n-- SOL Build, QA, and Documentation handoffs are complete.\\\\n-- The accepted source revision and release tag are verified on GitHub.\\\\n-\\\\n-## Research references\\\\n-\\\\n-1. [OpenCode model catalog, including GPT-5.6 Sol](https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/)\\\\n-2. [yfinance historical-data implementation](https://github.com/ranaroussi/yfinance/blob/main/yfinance/scrapers/history.py)\\\\n-3. [Bank of England: filtered historical simulation](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/working-paper/2015/filtered-historical-simulation-value-at-risk-models-and-their-competitors.pdf)\\\\n-4. [SQLite WAL documentation and WAL-reset issue](https://sqlite.org/wal.html#the_wal_reset_bug)\\\\n-5. [Official Playwright MCP server](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp)\\\\n-6. It does not yet contain the application described below.\\\\n-6: \\\\n-7: - `M00` is **Completed** for the four documentation files created in this baseline: `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md`.\\\\n-8: - `M01` through `M07` are **Pending**. No implementation milestone is complete.\\\\n-9: - A task may move to **Completed** only after its acceptance evidence, verification result, repair history, and reviewer are recorded.\\\\n-10: \\\\n-11: ## Product Goal\\\\n-12: \\\\n-13: Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF and receives two forecast views:\\\\n-14: \\\\n-15: 1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\\\\n-16: 2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\\\\n-17: \\\\n-18: Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. Every displayed result must identify its symbol, asset type, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\\\\n-19: \\\\n-20: This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\\\\n-21: \\\\n-22: ## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\\\\n-23: \\\\n-24: ### API boundary\\\\n-25: \\\\n-26: - All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\\\\n-27: - The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\\\\n-28: - The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\\\\n-29: - API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\\\\n-30: \\\\n-31: ### Data source and time semantics\\\\n-32: \\\\n-33: - Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\\\\n-34: - The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\\\\n-35: - The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\\\\n-36: - Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\\\\n-37: \\\\n-38: ### Persistence and auditability\\\\n-39: \\\\n-40: - Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\\\\n-41: - A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\\\\n-42: - The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\\\\n-43: - An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\\\\n-44: - Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\\\\n-45: - History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\\\\n-46: \\\\n-47: ### User experience\\\\n-48: \\\\n-49: - The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\\\\n-50: - Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\\\\n-51: - Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\\\\n-52: - History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\\\\n-53: - Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\\\\n-54: \\\\n-55: ### Deployment and resources\\\\n-56: \\\\n-57: - The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\\\\n-58: - Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\\\\n-59: - Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\\\\n-60: - Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\\\\n-61: - All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\\\\n-62: \\\\n-63: ## Planned Architecture\\\\n-64: \\\\n-65: The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\\\\n-66: \\\\n-67: The API/application layers should remain separable:\\\\n-68: \\\\n-69: - **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\\\\n-70: - **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\\\\n-71: - **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\\\\n-72: - **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\\\\n-73: - **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\\\\n-74: \\\\n-75: The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\\\\n-76: \\\\n-77: ## Forecast Contract\\\\n-78: \\\\n-79: The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\\\\n-80: \\\\n-81: - Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\\\\n-82: - Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\\\\n-83: - What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\\\\n-84: - What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\\\\n-85: - What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\\\\n-86: - What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\\\\n-87: - What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\\\\n-88: \\\\n-89: The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\\\\n-90: \\\\n-91: ## Task Register\\\\n-92: \\\\n-93: The coordinator assigns no more than three agents to a task in addition to the coordinator. The listed acceptance evidence is required before status can become **Completed**.\\\\n-94: \\\\n-95: ### M00 - Documentation Baseline\\\\n-96: \\\\n-97: - **Status:** Completed, docs only.\\\\n-98: - **Dependencies:** None.\\\\n-99: - **Agents:** `LUNA MAX docs`.\\\\n-100: - **Scope:** Create the plan, roadmap, compact agent rules, and honest repository README.\\\\n-101: - **Acceptance evidence:** [x] `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md` exist; [ ] end-to-end browser journey; [ ] restore from the produced artifact; [ ] security and accessibility sign-off; [ ] performance/resource evidence; [ ] coordinator review of every dependency and evidence field.\\\\n-173: - **Repair record:** Record each failed release check as `R-M07-<n>` and keep M07 pending until repaired and rerun.\\\\n-174: \\\\n-175: ## Evidence Record Format\\\\n-176: \\\\n-177: Every implementation task must maintain these fields in its task record or linked review:\\\\n-178: \\\\n-179: - **Task ID:** the exact `M##` or `R-M##-<n>` identifier.\\\\n-180: - **Status:** `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`.\\\\n-181: - **Dependencies verified:** the completed task IDs and evidence references.\\\\n-182: - **Change summary:** what changed and what did not change.\\\\n-183: - **Acceptance evidence:** links, test names, fixture IDs, screenshots, logs, checksums, or measured resource results.\\\\n-184: - **Verification result:** command/check name, environment, timestamp, and pass/fail result.\\\\n-185: - **Repair history:** each failure, root cause, repair, and rerun result; use `None` only when no repair was needed.\\\\n-186: - **Reviewer:** the coordinator and the verifying agent.\\\\n-187: \\\\n-188: Evidence is not a prose promise. A skipped or unavailable check must be recorded as such and cannot satisfy a required acceptance field.\\\\n-189: \\\\n-190: ## Verification And Repair Loop\\\\n-191: \\\\n-192: 1. The coordinator selects the next pending task only after its dependencies have completed with evidence.\\\\n-193: 2. The assigned build, QA, and documentation agents work within the task scope and keep the task status visible.\\\\n-194: 3. The coordinator runs the targeted verification set, then the applicable repository/Git/CI gates.\\\\n-195: 4. If any check fails, the task remains pending or in progress. The coordinator records the failure, creates `R-M##-<n>`, assigns no more than three agents, and repairs the root cause rather than weakening the check.\\\\n-196: 5. QA reruns the failed check and the relevant regression set. Documentation records the new evidence and any limitation.\\\\n-197: 6. The coordinator marks the task completed only when every required acceptance field passes and the reviewer is named.\\\\n-198: \\\\n-199: ## Final Definition Of Done\\\\n-200: \\\\n-201: The MVP is done only when all of the following are true:\\\\n-202: \\\\n-203: - M00 through M07 have explicit statuses and evidence, with no implementation milestone marked complete by assertion alone.\\\\n-204: - A user can select Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs and receive close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close forecasts with clear session/bar semantics.\\\\n-205: - Always download, inspect, then run.\\n\\n```bash\\n# ❌ BAD — blind execution\\ncurl -sSL https://example.com/install.sh | bash\\n\\n# ✅ GOOD — inspect first\\ncurl -sSL https://example.com/install.sh > install.sh\\nless install.sh && bash install.sh\\n```\\n\\n### 🔴 NEVER Touch `$HOME/repos` or `/mnt`\\n\\nThe `$HOME/repos` directory and all subdirectories are off-limits for any Docker cleanup, WSL maintenance, or file operations. The `/mnt` directory (Windows drive mounts) is also off-limits. Before running ANY command that operates on paths, verify the path does not start with `$HOME/repos`, `/mnt`, or a resolved equivalent.\\n\\n### 🔴 Assess Before Acting; Confirm Before Destruction\\n\\nShow disk usage (`df -h`) before any destructive operation. Always confirm with the user before `docker system prune`, `apt autoremove --purge`, `rm -rf`, or similar destructive commands.\\n\\n### 🔴 Shell Safety\\n\\nMulti-command shell statements must follow `set -euo pipefail` safety patterns. Quote all variable expansions, use `|| true` tolerance for commands that may fail, never background processes with `&`.\\n\\n### 🔴 NEVER Append Output Redirection to Terminal Commands\\n\\nNever append `2>&1`, `>/dev/null`, `&>/dev/null`, or any standard output/error redirection to commands. All tool outputs must stream raw text back to the shell environment. Hiding output prevents error detection and debugging.\\n\\n```bash\\n# ❌ WRONG — hiding output breaks error detection\\ncurl http://localhost:4097/health 2>&1 | grep ok\\ndocker ps 2>/dev/null\\nnpm test &>/dev/null\\n\\n# ✅ CORRECT — full output, handle errors explicitly\\ncurl http://localhost:4097/health\\ndocker ps\\nnpm test\\n```\\n\\n### 🔴 Use `docker compose`, NOT `docker-compose`\\n\\nThe `docker-compose` standalone binary (with hyphen) is deprecated. Always use the modern Docker Compose plugin:\\n\\n```bash\\n# ❌ WRONG — docker-compose (hyphen) not installed on modern Docker\\ndocker-compose config\\ndocker-compose up -d\\n\\n# ✅ CORRECT — docker compose (space) is the modern command\\ndocker compose config\\ndocker compose up -d\\ndocker compose ps\\n```\\n\\nThe hyphen variant is a legacy Python script that may not exist on the system. The space variant is built into the Docker CLI as a plugin. Always use `docker compose` (space).\\n\\n### 🔴 Use `docker compose` for Container Lifecycle — Not Raw `docker run`\\n\\nAll container lifecycle management must go through `docker compose` — never raw `docker run`, `docker rm`, or `docker stop` commands. The `docker compose` tool manages networks, volumes, and dependencies correctly.\\n\\n```bash\\n# ❌ WRONG — raw docker commands bypass compose orchestration\\ndocker run -d --name myapp ...\\ndocker rm -f myapp\\ndocker stop myapp\\n\\n# ✅ CORRECT — compose handles networking, volumes, healthchecks, dependencies\\ndocker compose up -d\\ndocker compose down\\ndocker compose restart\\ndocker compose logs\\ndocker compose ps\\n```\\n\\n## Reference Files\\n\\n### CLI Toolkit\\n\\n| File | Content |\\n|------|---------|\\n| The shapes below cover the common surface area, but they are a\\n**summary, not the source of truth**.\\n\\n## Full schema reference\\n\\nThe authoritative list of every config option — with field types, enums,\\ndefaults, and descriptions — lives in the published JSON Schema:\\n\\n**<https://opencode.ai/config.json>**\\n\\nIf a field is not documented in this skill, or you need to confirm an exact\\nshape before writing config, **fetch that URL and read the schema directly**\\nrather than guessing. opencode hard-fails on invalid config, so the cost of a\\nwrong shape is a broken startup.\\n\\nIndependently, every `opencode.json` should declare\\n`\\\"$schema\\\": \\\"https://opencode.ai/config.json\\\"` so the user's editor catches\\nmistakes as they type.\\n\\n## Applying changes\\n\\nConfig is loaded once when opencode starts and is not hot-reloaded. After\\nsaving changes to `opencode.json`, an agent file, a skill, a plugin, or any\\nother config-time file, **tell the user to quit and restart opencode** for\\nthe changes to take effect. The running session will keep using the\\nalready-loaded config until then.\\n\\n## Where files live\\n\\n| Scope                         | Path                                                                                                                      |\\n| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\n| Project config                | `./opencode.json`, `./opencode.jsonc`, or `.opencode/opencode.json` (opencode walks up from the cwd to the worktree root) |\\n| Global config                 | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` or `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (NOT `~/.opencode/`)                            |\\n| Project agents                | `.opencode/agent/<name>.md` or `.opencode/agents/<name>.md`                                                               |\\n| Global agents                 | `~/.config/opencode/agent(s)/<name>.md`                                                                                   |\\n| Project commands              | `.opencode/command/<name>.md` or `.opencode/commands/<name>.md`                                                           |\\n| Global commands               | `~/.config/opencode/command(s)/<name>.md`                                                                                 |\\n| Project skills                | `.opencode/skill(s)/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                                                      |\\n| Global skills                 | `~/.config/opencode/skill(s)/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                                             |\\n| External skills (auto-loaded) | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                    |\\n\\nConfigs from each scope are deep-merged. Project overrides global. Unknown\\ntop-level keys in `opencode.json` are rejected with `ConfigInvalidError`.\\n\\n## opencode.json\\n\\nEvery field is optional.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"$schema\\\": \\\"https://opencode.ai/config.json\\\",\\n  \\\"username\\\": \\\"string\\\",\\n  \\\"model\\\": \\\"provider/model-id\\\",\\n  \\\"small_model\\\": \\\"provider/model-id\\\",\\n  \\\"default_agent\\\": \\\"agent-name\\\",\\n  \\\"shell\\\": \\\"/bin/zsh\\\",\\n  \\\"logLevel\\\": \\\"DEBUG\\\" | \\\"INFO\\\" | \\\"WARN\\\" | \\\"ERROR\\\",\\n  \\\"share\\\": \\\"manual\\\" | \\\"auto\\\" | \\\"disabled\\\",\\n  \\\"autoupdate\\\": true | false | \\\"notify\\\",\\n  \\\"snapshot\\\": true,\\n  \\\"instructions\\\": [\\\"AGENTS.md\\\", \\\"docs/style.md\\\"],\\n\\n  \\\"skills\\\": {\\n    \\\"paths\\\": [\\\".opencode/skills\\\", \\\"/abs/path/to/skills\\\"],\\n    \\\"urls\\\": [\\\"https://example.com/.well-known/skills/\\\"]\\n  },\\n\\n  \\\"references\\\": {\\n    \\\"docs\\\": {\\n      \\\"path\\\": \\\"../docs\\\",\\n      \\\"description\\\": \\\"Use for product behavior and documentation conventions\\\"\\n    },\\n    \\\"sdk\\\": {\\n      \\\"repository\\\": \\\"owner/sdk\\\",\\n      \\\"branch\\\": \\\"main\\\",\\n      \\\"description\\\": \\\"Use for SDK implementation details\\\",\\n      \\\"hidden\\\": true\\n    }\\n  },\\n\\n  \\\"agent\\\": {\\n    \\\"my-agent\\\": {\\n      \\\"model\\\": \\\"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\\\",\\n      \\\"mode\\\": \\\"subagent\\\",\\n      \\\"description\\\": \\\"...\\\",\\n      \\\"permission\\\": { \\\"edit\\\": \\\"deny\\\" }\\n    }\\n  },\\n\\n  \\\"command\\\": {\\n    \\\"deploy\\\": { \\\"description\\\": \\\"...\\\", \\\"template\\\": \\\"...\\\" }\\n  },\\n\\n  \\\"provider\\\": {\\n    \\\"anthropic\\\": { \\\"options\\\": { \\\"apiKey\\\": \\\"...\\\" } }\\n  },\\n  \\\"disabled_providers\\\": [\\\"openai\\\"],\\n  \\\"enabled_providers\\\": [\\\"anthropic\\\"],\\n\\n  \\\"mcp\\\": {\\n    \\\"playwright\\\": {\\n      \\\"type\\\": \\\"local\\\",\\n      \\\"command\\\": [\\\"npx\\\", \\\"-y\\\", \\\"@playwright/mcp\\\"],\\n      \\\"enabled\\\": true,\\n      \\\"environment\\\": {}\\n    },\\n    \\\"remote-thing\\\": {\\n      \\\"type\\\": \\\"remote\\\",\\n      \\\"url\\\": \\\"https://...\\\",\\n      \\\"headers\\\": { \\\"Authorization\\\": \\\"Bearer ...\\\" }\\n    }\\n  },\\n\\n  \\\"plugin\\\": [\\n    \\\"opencode-gemini-auth\\\",\\n    \\\"opencode-foo@1.2.3\\\",\\n    \\\"./local-plugin.ts\\\",\\n    [\\\"opencode-bar\\\", { \\\"option\\\": \\\"value\\\" }]\\n  ],\\n\\n  \\\"permission\\\": {\\n    \\\"edit\\\": \\\"deny\\\",\\n    \\\"bash\\\": { \\\"git *\\\": \\\"allow\\\", \\\"*\\\": \\\"ask\\\" }\\n  },\\n\\n  \\\"formatter\\\": false,\\n  \\\"lsp\\\": false,\\n\\n  \\\"experimental\\\": {\\n    \\\"primary_tools\\\": [\\\"edit\\\"],\\n    \\\"mcp_timeout\\\": 30000\\n  },\\n\\n  \\\"tool_output\\\": { \\\"max_lines\\\": 200, \\\"max_bytes\\\": 8192 },\\n\\n  \\\"compaction\\\": { \\\"auto\\\": true, \\\"tail_turns\\\": 15 }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nShape notes worth being explicit about:\\n\\n- `model` always carries a provider prefix: `\\\"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\\\"`.\\n- `skills` is an object with `paths` and/or `urls`, not an array.\\n- `references` is an object keyed by alias. Each value is a local path, Git repository, or string shorthand.\\n- `agent` is an object keyed by agent name, not an array.\\n- `command` is an object keyed by command name, not an array.\\n- `plugin` is an array of strings or `[name, options]` tuples, not an object.\\n- `mcp[name].command` is an array of strings, never a single string. `type` is required.\\n- `permission` is either a string action or an object keyed by tool name.\\n\\n## Skills\\n\\nopencode's skill loader scans for `**/SKILL.md` inside skill directories. The\\nfile is named `SKILL.md` exactly, and lives in its own folder named after the\\nskill:\\n\\n```\\n.opencode/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md\\n```\\n\\nFrontmatter:\\n\\n```markdown\\n---\\nname: my-skill\\ndescription: One sentence covering what this skill does AND when to trigger it. Front-load the literal keywords or filenames the user is likely to say.\\n---\\n\\n# My Skill\\n\\n(skill body in markdown: instructions, examples, references)\\n```\\n\\n- `name` is required, lowercase hyphen-separated, up to 64 chars, and matches the folder name.\\n- `description` is effectively required: skills without one are filtered out and never surfaced to the model. Cover both _what_ the skill does and _when_ to use it. Write in third person (\\\"Use when...\\\", not \\\"I help with...\\\"). Front-load concrete trigger keywords and filenames; gate with \\\"Use ONLY when...\\\" if the skill should stay quiet on adjacent topics.\\n- Optional: `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata` (string-string map).\\n\\nRegister skills from non-default locations via `skills.paths` (scanned\\nrecursively for `**/SKILL.md`) and `skills.urls` (each URL serves a list of\\nskills).\\n\\n## References\\n\\nReferences make local directories and Git repositories outside the active\\nproject available as supporting context. Configure them under `references`,\\nkeyed by the alias used in `@` autocomplete:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"references\\\": {\\n    \\\"docs\\\": {\\n      \\\"path\\\": \\\"../product-docs\\\",\\n      \\\"description\\\": \\\"Use for product behavior and terminology\\\"\\n    },\\n    \\\"effect\\\": {\\n      \\\"repository\\\": \\\"Effect-TS/effect\\\",\\n      \\\"branch\\\": \\\"main\\\",\\n      \\\"description\\\": \\\"Use for Effect implementation details\\\"\\n    }\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nLocal `path` values may be relative to the declaring config, absolute, or use\\n`~/`. Git `repository` values accept Git URLs, host/path references, and GitHub\\n`owner/repo` shorthand; `branch` is optional. Both forms support optional\\n`description` and `hidden` fields.\\n\\n- Only references with a `description` are advertised to agents in system context.\\n- `hidden: true` removes a reference from TUI `@` autocomplete only. It remains available to agents and by direct path.\\n- Reference directories are automatically allowed through the external-directory boundary; normal read/edit/tool permissions still apply.\\n- String shorthand is supported: use `\\\"docs\\\": \\\"../docs\\\"` for local paths or `\\\"effect\\\": \\\"Effect-TS/effect\\\"` for Git repositories.\\n\\n## Agents\\n\\nTwo ways to define an agent. Use the file form for anything non-trivial.\\n\\n### Inline (in `opencode.json`)\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"agent\\\": {\\n    \\\"my-reviewer\\\": {\\n      \\\"description\\\": \\\"Reviews PRs for style violations.\\\",\\n      \\\"mode\\\": \\\"subagent\\\",\\n      \\\"model\\\": \\\"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\\\",\\n      \\\"permission\\\": { \\\"edit\\\": \\\"deny\\\", \\\"bash\\\": \\\"ask\\\" },\\n      \\\"prompt\\\": \\\"You are a strict PR reviewer...\\\"\\n    }\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### File\\n\\n```\\n.opencode/agent/my-reviewer.md      OR     .opencode/agents/my-reviewer.md\\n```\\n\\n```markdown\\n---\\ndescription: Reviews PRs for style violations.\\nmode: subagent\\nmodel: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\\npermission:\\n  edit: deny\\n  bash: ask\\n---\\n\\nYou are a strict PR reviewer. Focus on...\\n```\\n\\nThe file body becomes the agent's `prompt`. Do not also put `prompt:` in the\\nfrontmatter.\\n\\n`mode` is one of `\\\"primary\\\"`, `\\\"subagent\\\"`, `\\\"all\\\"`.\\n\\nAllowed top-level frontmatter fields: `name, model, variant, description, mode,\\nhidden, color, steps, options, permission, disable, temperature, top_p`. Any\\nunknown field is silently routed into `options`.\\n\\nTo disable a built-in agent: `agent: { build: { disable: true } }`, or in a\\nfile, `disable: true` in frontmatter.\\n\\n`default_agent` must point to a non-hidden, primary-mode agent.\\n\\n### Built-in agents\\n\\nopencode ships with `build`, `plan`, `general`, `explore`. Hidden internal agents:\\n`compaction`, `title`, `summary`. To override a built-in's fields, define the\\nsame key in `agent: { <name>: { ... } }`.\\n\\n## Commands\\n\\nopencode's command loader scans for `**/*.md` inside command directories. The\\nfile is named after the command, and lives directly inside the `command` folder:\\n\\n```\\n.opencode/command/deploy.md\\n```\\n\\nFrontmatter:\\n\\n```markdown\\n---\\ndescription: One sentence describing what the command does.\\nagent: build\\nmodel: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\\n---\\n\\n(command body in markdown: the prompt opencode runs, with $ARGUMENTS for the user's input)\\n```\\n\\n- `template` is the command body — everything below the frontmatter — and is required: it is the prompt opencode runs when the command is invoked. Do not also put a `template:` key in the frontmatter.\\n- `$ARGUMENTS` is replaced with everything the user typed after the command; `$1`, `$2`, … pull individual positional arguments.\\n- Optional: `description`, `agent`, `model`, `variant`, `subtask`.\\n\\n## Plugins\\n\\n`plugin:` is an array. Each entry is one of:\\n\\n```json\\n\\\"plugin\\\": [\\n  \\\"opencode-gemini-auth\\\",            // npm spec, latest\\n  \\\"opencode-foo@1.2.3\\\",              // npm spec, pinned\\n  \\\"./local-plugin.ts\\\",               // file path, relative to the declaring config\\n  \\\"file:///abs/path/plugin.js\\\",      // file URL\\n  [\\\"opencode-bar\\\", { \\\"key\\\": \\\"val\\\" }] // tuple form with options\\n]\\n```\\n\\nAuto-discovered plugins (no config entry needed): any `*.ts` or `*.js` file in\\n`.opencode/plugin/` or `.opencode/plugins/`.\\n\\nA plugin module exports `default` (or any named export) of type\\n`Plugin = (input: PluginInput, options?) => Promise<Hooks>`. The export is a\\nfunction, not a plain object literal, and the function returns an object\\n(return `{}` if there is nothing to register).\\n\\n```ts\\nimport type { Plugin } from \\\"@opencode-ai/plugin\\\"\\n\\nexport default (async ({ client, project, directory, $ }) => {\\n  return {\\n    config: (cfg) => {\\n      // cfg is the live merged config; mutate fields here.\\n    },\\n    \\\"tool.execute.before\\\": async (input, output) => {\\n      // mutate output.args before the tool runs\\n    },\\n  }\\n}) satisfies Plugin\\n```\\n\\nHook surface (mutate `output` in place; return `void`):\\n\\n- `event(input)`: every bus event\\n- `config(cfg)`: once on init with the merged config\\n- `chat.message`, `chat.params`, `chat.headers`\\n- `tool.execute.before`, `tool.execute.after`\\n- `tool.definition`\\n- `command.execute.before`\\n- `shell.env`\\n- `permission.ask`\\n- `experimental.chat.messages.transform`, `experimental.chat.system.transform`,\\n  `experimental.session.compacting`, `experimental.compaction.autocontinue`,\\n  `experimental.text.complete`\\n\\nSpecial object-shaped (not callbacks): `tool: { my_tool: { ... } }`,\\n`auth: { ... }`, `provider: { ... }`.\\n\\n## MCP servers\\n\\n`mcp:` is an object keyed by server name. Each server is discriminated by\\n`type`:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"mcp\\\": {\\n    \\\"playwright\\\": {\\n      \\\"type\\\": \\\"local\\\",\\n      \\\"command\\\": [\\\"npx\\\", \\\"-y\\\", \\\"@playwright/mcp\\\"],\\n      \\\"enabled\\\": true,\\n      \\\"environment\\\": { \\\"BROWSER\\\": \\\"chromium\\\" }\\n    },\\n    \\\"github\\\": {\\n      \\\"type\\\": \\\"remote\\\",\\n      \\\"url\\\": \\\"https://...\\\",\\n      \\\"enabled\\\": true,\\n      \\\"headers\\\": { \\\"Authorization\\\": \\\"Bearer {env:GITHUB_TOKEN}\\\" }\\n    },\\n    \\\"old-server\\\": { \\\"enabled\\\": false }\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n`command` is an array of strings. `environment` sets environment variables for\\na local MCP server. `type` is required. Use `enabled: false` to\\ndisable a server inherited from a parent config. String values such as header\\ntokens support `{env:VAR}` interpolation (and `{file:path}`); the shell-style\\n`${VAR}` is not substituted.\\n\\n## Permissions\\n\\n```json\\n\\\"permission\\\": {\\n  \\\"edit\\\": \\\"deny\\\",\\n  \\\"bash\\\": { \\\"git *\\\": \\\"allow\\\", \\\"rm *\\\": \\\"deny\\\", \\\"*\\\": \\\"ask\\\" },\\n  \\\"external_directory\\\": { \\\"~/secrets/**\\\": \\\"deny\\\", \\\"*\\\": \\\"allow\\\" }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nActions: `\\\"allow\\\"`, `\\\"ask\\\"`, `\\\"deny\\\"`.\\n\\nPer-tool value forms: `\\\"allow\\\"` shorthand (treated as `{\\\"*\\\": \\\"allow\\\"}`), or an\\nobject `{ pattern: action }`. Within an object, **insertion order matters**.\\nopencode evaluates the LAST matching rule, so put broad rules first and narrow\\nrules last.\\n\\n`permission: \\\"allow\\\"` (a string at the top level) is shorthand for \\\"allow\\neverything\\\" and is rarely what the user wants.\\n\\nKnown permission keys: `read, edit, glob, grep, list, bash, task,\\nexternal_directory, todowrite, question, webfetch, websearch, lsp, doom_loop,\\nskill`. Some of these (`todowrite,\\nquestion, webfetch, websearch, doom_loop`) only accept a flat\\naction, not a per-pattern object.\\n\\n`external_directory` patterns are filesystem paths (use `~/`, absolute paths,\\nor globs like `~/projects/**`).\\n\\nPer-agent `permission:` overrides top-level `permission:`. Plan Mode lives on\\nthe `plan` agent's permission ruleset (`edit: deny *`).\\n\\n## Escape hatches\\n\\nWhen a user's config is broken and opencode won't start, these env vars help:\\n\\n- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1`: skip the project's local `opencode.json`\\n  and start from globals only. Run from the project directory, opencode loads,\\n  the user edits the broken file, then they restart without the flag.\\n- `OPENCODE_CONFIG=/path/to/file.json`: load an additional explicit config.\\n- `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{\\\"$schema\\\":\\\"https://opencode.ai/config.json\\\"}'`:\\n  inject inline JSON as a final local-scope merge.\\n- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=1`: skip default plugins.\\n- `OPENCODE_PURE=1`: skip external plugins entirely.\\n- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS=1`,\\n  `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS=1`: skip the external skill scans under\\n  `~/.claude/` and `~/.agents/`.\\n\\n## When proposing edits\\n\\n- Validate against the schema before writing. If you are unsure of a field's\\n  exact shape, or the field is not covered in this skill, fetch\\n  `https://opencode.ai/config.json` and read the schema rather than guessing.\\n- Preserve `$schema` and any existing fields the user did not ask to change.\\n- For agent, command, skill, and plugin definitions, prefer creating new files\\n  in the correct location over inlining everything in `opencode.json`.\\n- If the user's existing config is malformed, point them at the env-var escape\\n  hatches above so they can edit from inside opencode without breaking their\\n  session.\\n- After
